papers.sourceText:
Q1: Which of the animal product is used in the production of buttons?
A) Skin
B) Fur
C) Bone
D) Home
Answer: C

Q2: Subsistance farmers mostly practice
A) Monoculture
B) Monocropping
C) Mixed cropping
D) Crop rotation
Answer: C

Q3: A piece of land is said to be on lease to a farmer when it is
A) Given as compensation
B) Purchased on credit.
C) Rented for a period
D) Given as a gift.
Answer: C

Q4: Which of the following equipment is a farm implement?
A) Dryer
B) Sheller
C) Mower
D) Mistblower
Answer: C

Q5: A periodic maintenance activity carried out on the farm tractor is
A) Checking of radiator water
B) Checking of tyre pressure
C) Changing of engine oil
D) Cleaning after use.
Answer: C

Q6: Farm mechanization does not
A) Involve the use of motorized equipment
B) Require much capital
C) Promote employment
D) Involve the use of heavy machinery
Answer: C

Q7: Which of the following sources of farm power is most versatile in West Africa?
A) Biogas
B) Animal
C) Wind
D) Water
Answer: D

Q8: Farm surveying equipment include the following except
A) Abney level
B) Compass
C) Gunter's chain
D) Spade
Answer: D

Q9: The system in which a farmer uses a piece of land for a period and abandons it for another land is called
A) Crop rotation
B) Mix cropping
C) Shifting cultivation
D) Ley farming
Answer: C

Q10: A socio-cultural factor affecting land availability for agriculture include use of land for
A) Constructing road
B) Building houses
C) Building factories
D) Building religious houses.
Answer: D

Q11: Organisms which may be benefical to crop include
A) Nematodes
B) Bacteria
C) Viruses
D) Protozoa
Answer: B

Q12: Which of the following rocks is sedimentary?
A) Limestone
B) Gabbro
C) Granite
D) Marble
Answer: A

Q13: . Soil profile is important in agriculture because it
A) Determines the soil catena
B) Determines the type of the land tenure system
C) Gives indication of the types of crops to grow
D) Promotes the weathering of rocks
Answer: C

Q14: What is the percentage water content of soil sample which weighed 180g when fresh and 120g when oven-dried
A) 20.14%
B) 25.00%
C) 33.33%
D) 60.00%
Answer: C

Q15: A soil sample with a pH of 4.5 is said to be
A) Acidic
B) Alkaline
C) Neutral
D) Fertile
Answer: A

Q16: The property of soil which cannot easily be change by a famer is the
A) Porosity
B) Structure
C) Texture
D) Acidity
Answer: C

Q17: A farmer continuously applies sulphate of ammonia to his farmland for many years, the resultant soil solution is most likely to
A) Leave blue litmus paper unchanged
B) Change blue litmus paper to red
C) Change red litmus paper to blue
D) Be rich in soil microbes
Answer: B

Q18: Application of water to the subsoil through perforated pipes is known as
A) Flooding irrigation
B) Subsurface irrigation
C) Spinkler irrigation
D) Overhead irrigation
Answer: D

Q19: Which of the following statemnets describe the impact of land degradation?
A) 
B) 
C) 
D) 
Answer: 

Q20: Tabacco belongs to the group of crops called
A) Fibres
B) Beverages
C) Stimulants
D) Cereals
Answer: C

Q21: . Maize is a popular crop in West Africa because it
A) Is a cereal
B) Has multiple uses
C) Is of high nutritional value
D) Was introduced from Europe
Answer: B

Q22: If the spacing of maize is 0:9m by 0.3m and one seed is sown per stand, what will be the population of maize plants on a hectare of farmland?
A) 74,074
B) 54,000
C) 37,037
D) 27,000
Answer: D

Q23: The following crops require shade trees at the seedling stage except
A) Theobroma cacao
B) Coffea spp
C) Elaeis guineensis
D) Oryza sativa
Answer: D

Q24: . Crop which are primarily grown to provide food for farm animals are
A) Legumes
B) Weeds
C) Forages
D) Grasses
Answer: C

Q25: Crop selection is advantageous because
A) Seeds are collected from stands with desirable traits
B) Expertise is required in carring out the process
C) The breeder'd patien ce is being tasked
D) The process is time consuming
Answer: A

Q26: A fungus known as phytophthora palmivora is responsible for
A) Panama disease of banana
B) Bickarm disease of kola
C) Blackpod disease of cocoa
D) Blossom-end rot of tomato
Answer: C

Q27: Viral disease of crops can best be controlled through
A) Vector control
B) Planting reistant varieties
C) Spraying insecticides
D) Sterilizing farm equipment
Answer: B

Q28: . Piercing and sucking insect pests possess
A) Maxillae
B) Mandibles
C) . Labrums
D) Probosces
Answer: D

Q29: Callosobruchus maculatus is a common pest of
A) Sorghum
B) Rice
C) Maize
D) Cowpea
Answer: D

Q30: The use of pathogens to control dodder weeds is a
A) Physcial methos
B) Mechanical method
C) Biological method
D) Cultural method
Answer: C

Q31: The digestive function of the rumen in ruminant nutrition is enchanced by the
A) Absorption of water
B) Presence of micro-organisms
C) Absorption of food nutrients
D) Retention of unwanted foreign materials
Answer: B

Q32: The duration of the oestrus cycle of sow is
A) 14-28 days
B) 6-10 days
C) 3-5 days
D) 1-2 days
Answer: A

Q33: Natural immunity to diseases in calves is acquired through access to
A) Vaccine
B) Colostrum
C) Balanced diet
D) Salt licks
Answer: B

Q34: If a sow conceived on the 5th of june in particular year, it will probably farrow the same year on
A) 8th August
B) 18th September
C) 28th September
D) 28th October
Answer: D

Q35: The act of parturtion in rabbit is known as
A) Calving
B) . Lambing
C) Farrowing
D) Kindling
Answer: D

Q36: The extra oyster shell meal supplied to breeding hens
A) Prevents excess abdominal fat
B) Prevents anaemia
C) Aids in hardening egg shells
D) Shortens the incubation period of eggs
Answer: C

Q37: Iron is important in the diet of livestock for
A) Teeth formation
B) Feather production
C) Hair formation
D) Blood production
Answer: D

Q38: Established pasture cannot be harvested by
A) Using the mower
B) Zero grazing
C) Using combine harvester
D) Cutting with sickle.
Answer: D

Q39: The mating of a white fulani bull and an N'dama cow could be termed
A) Inbreeding
B) Line breeding
C) Outbreeding
D) Cross breeding
Answer: D

Q40: . Which of the following organisms is not an endoparasite?
A) Rounworm
B) Liverfluke
C) Tick
D) Cestode
Answer: C

Q41: Which of the following compounds can be used to seal soil pores and prevent loss of water in a fish pond?
A) Suphur (IV) oxide
B) Ammonium suphate
C) Calcium carbonate
D) Potassium hydroxide
Answer: C

Q42: The demand for cassava is not affected by
A) Cost of production
B) Taste of consumers
C) Change in income
D) Price of cassava
Answer: A

Q43: A farmer obtained a loan of #250,000 at a simple interest rate of 8% per annum to be paid in two years what would be the interest the farmer will pay on the loan?
A) #20,000
B) . #40,000
C) #250,000
D) #400,000
Answer: B

Context: A farmer bought a farm implement for 12,500 in 2007. At the end of the fourth year he sold if for #4,300.
Q44: . Calculate the total depreciation of the implement
A) #16,800
B) #8,200
C) #3,125
D) #1,075
Answer: B

Q45: The annual depreciation of the implement is
A) #4,300
B) #3,125
C) #2,050
D) #1075
Answer: B

Q46: Which of the following methods is inapropriate when introducing a new variety of rice to farners?
A) Farmers' cooperarive society
B) Circular letters
C) Demonstrations
D) Field trips
Answer: B

Q47: The term fingerling refers to a young
A) Rabbit
B) Fish
C) Goat
D) Turkey
Answer: B

papers.subject: Agricultural Science

papers.sourceText:
Q1: Which of the following suggestion would solve transportation problems associated with agriculture?
A) Establishment of tractor hiring units
B) Efficient railway system
C) Establishment of car hire units
D) Provision of extension services
Answer: B

Q2: Which of the following statements is not correct about agriculture in most West African countries?
A) employment
B) fuel
C) food
D) income
Answer: B

Q3: The document given to a farmer on acquiring a piece of land from government is called
A) certificate of purchase
B) receipt of ownership
C) certificate of occupancy
D) receipt of lease
Answer: C

Q4: The surveying instrument used for measuring horizontal and vertical angles is called
A) theodolite.
B) Gunter's chain
C) Gunter's chain
D) arrow
Answer: A

Q5: Crop rotation is often used in maintaining soil fertility because
A) all crops grown, add nutrient to the soil
B) some of the crops fix nitrogen in the soil
C) crops grown are ploughed into the soil
D) the crops are rotated on different farmlands
Answer: B

Q6: Land is said to be a fixed asset in Agriculture. This means that
A) its features and topography are fixed
B) soil nutrients and its vegetative cover can be replaced.
C) its size remains fixed over time
D) its micro organic composition is constant over time.
Answer: A

Q7: The most limiting factor affecting land availability for agriculture in urban settlements is
A) soil type
B) topography
C) climate
D) population pressure
Answer: D

Q8: Rhizobium supplies nitrogen to leguminous plants by
A) incorporating urea into their bodies
B) . fixing atmospheric nitrogen into the soil
C) decomposing plant and animals remains
D) decreasing the pH value of the soil
Answer: B

Q9: An example of igneous rock is
A) granite
B) limestone
C) coal
D) sandstone
Answer: A

Q10: In chemical weathering of rocks, the equation Fe2 O3+3H2O ---> Fe2 O33H2O represents
A) carbonation.
B) hydration
C) solution
D) oxidation
Answer: B

Q11: Which of the following statement is a disadvantages of decaying organic matter in soils?
A) Bacterial and fungal growth is enhanced
B) minerals in organic matter are released into the soil
C) physical condition of soil is enhanced
D) . Water-holding capacity of soil is improved
Answer: A

Q12: Lost soil nutrients can be replenished by the following methods except
A) organic manuring
B) fertilizer application
C) continuous grazing
D) cover cropping
Answer: C

Q13: In the carbon cycle, carbon dioxide in the air may be replenished by
A) respiration
B) transpiration
C) lighting.
D) . denitrification
Answer: A

Q14: Irrigation can be described as the
A) reduction of soil water
B) spraying of minerals on plants
C) application of dissolved fertilizers to the soil
D) application of water to the soil
Answer: D

Q15: Which of the following conditions is a characteristic of a poorly drained soil?
A) presence of a large number of termites
B) Presence of high amount of humus
C) Decrease in the activities of microorganisms
D) High soil fertility and productivity
Answer: C

Q16: The process of removing excess maize seedlings from a stand is known as
A) pruning
B) supplying
C) thinning
D) wedding
Answer: C

Q17: Which of the following crops requires shade at the early stage of is growth?
A) Plantain
B) Banana
C) Cocoa
D) Sugarcane
Answer: C

Q18: Which of the following plants is not a leguminous forage?
A) Centrosema Pubescens
B) Panicum maximum
C) Stylosanthes gracilis
D) Calopogonium mucunoides
Answer: B

Q19: The process of crossing two pure lines of plants of the same species is called
A) selection
B) genotype improvement
C) hybridization
D) inbreeding
Answer: D

Q20: Pure lines of crops are produced through continuous
A) selection
B) hybridization
C) cross breeding
D) inbreeding
Answer: D

Q21: Quarantine regulations are established so as to
A) allow the importation of diseased plant and animal materials
B) prevent the introduction of foreign diseases into a country
C) assist farmers to grow foreign crops
D) facilitates the rapid spread of foreign diseases.
Answer: B

Q22: The most effective method of controlling viral diseases in crops is by .
A) spraying with Bordeaux mixture.
B) removing and burning affected crops
C) practicing crop rotation
D) planting at recommended spacing
Answer: B

Q23: Which of the following insects transmits swollen shoot virus of Cocoa?
A) Stem borer
B) Mealybug
C) White fly
D) Capsid
Answer: B

Q24: The use of parasites and predators to control weeds is referred to as
A) biological control
B) chemical control
C) cultural control
D) mechanical control
Answer: A

Q25: Forest resources can be managed by the following measures except
A) taungya farming
B) selective exploitation
C) promoting deforestation
D) preventing bush burning
Answer: C

Q26: The continuous removal of forest tress without replacement is known as
A) afforestation
B) taungya farming
C) deforestation
D) selective exploitation
Answer: C

Q27: A farm animal which possesses a pair of caeca is
A) pig
B) fowl
C) sheep
D) cattle
Answer: B

Q28: Ostrogen in female animals is not responsible for
A) development of secondary sexual characteristics
B) onset of heat period
C) milk let-down after parturition
D) development of udder
Answer: C

Q29: A beef cow gained 75 kg over a period of two months and two days. What is its average weight gain?
A) 0.83 kg
B) 1.21 kg
C) 1.28 kg
D) 2.25 kg
Answer: B

Q30: A disadvantage of natural incubation is that
A) the eggs cannot be candled
B) the chicks are less healthy
C) the brooding hens sometimes abandon the eggs.
D) it takes a longer time for eggs to hatch
Answer: C

Q31: Ruminants fed on dried grasses are given feed supplements to
A) increase water intake
B) provide bulk to feed
C) reduce microbial activity
D) provide deficient nutrients
Answer: D

Q32: Which of the following animal diseases is not associated with malnutrition?
A) Aspergillosis
B) Acidosis
C) Acidosis
D) Rickets
Answer: A

Q33: The botanical name of Northern gamba grass is
A) Cynodon dactylon
B) Cynodon dactylon
C) Pennisetum purpureum
D) Andropogon gayanus
Answer: D

Q34: The cut and carry system of feeding livestock is termed
A) rotational grazing
B) zero grazing
C) zero grazing
D) controlled grazing
Answer: B

Q35: . Progeny selection involves selection of breeding stock on the basis of
A) feed conservation efficiency of the parents
B) merits of each animal
C) merits of the dam only
D) performance of offspring
Answer: D

Q36: The cattle disease which is likely to be most common in the forest belt of West Africa is
A) . foot and mouth
B) trypanosomiasis
C) anthrax
D) tuberculosis.
Answer: B

Q37: Ecto-parasites can be controlled by
A) administering antibodies to host
B) administering antibiotics to host
C) dipping of host
D) deworming of host
Answer: C

Q38: Cropping in fish farming is the act of
A) stocking fish
B) processing fish
C) harvesting fish
D) feeding fish
Answer: C

Q39: Methods of preserving fish including the following except
A) drying
B) smoking
C) salting
D) soaking.
Answer: D

Q40: Determine the price elasticity of demand if the price of yam tuber rises by 10% (0.1) and the quantity demanded falls by 5% (0.05).
A) 0.5
B) 0.4
C) 0.3
D) 0.1
Answer: A

Q41: Most farm business fail because of
A) death of the manager
B) lack of capital
C) . labour problems
D) poor management
Answer: D

Q42: Which of the following activities is not a marketing function?
A) Buying of agricultural commodities
B) planting of crops
C) 
D) 
Answer: B

Q43: Risks on commercial farms could result from
A) price stability
B) crop failure
C) insurance
D) diversification
Answer: B

Q44: An agricultural extension officer should be able to
A) create new jobs for farmers.
B) raise funds for farmers
C) cultivate a large farm
D) guide and educate farmers
Answer: D

papers.sourceText:
Q1: . The branch of agriculture which deals with the production of fruits is called
A) Pomology
B) floriculture
C) olericulture
D) nematology
Answer: A

Q2: One advantage of cooperative farming is that it
A) allows farmers to have small and scattered plots
B) enables individual farmers to acquire loans from the banks
C) enables farmers to acquire loans from the banks
D) facilitates the use of local tools
Answer: C

Q3: Which of the following statements is not a problem associated with land tenure system through inheritance?
A) family members have small land holdings
B) family members have right to free use of land
C) Non-family members cannot inherit land
D) Farm mechanization is restricted
Answer: B

Q4: A farmland measures 50 m x 50 m. Determine its area in hectares
A) 25 ha
B) 2.5 ha
C) 0.25ha
D) 0.025 ha
Answer: C

Q5: A farming system in which different types of crops are grown in succession, in a definite order on the same piece of land is termed
A) mixed farming
B) land rotation
C) continuous cropping
D) crop rotation
Answer: D

Q6: Land use for agriculture in West Africa is influenced by the following factors except
A) population density
B) topography
C) fallowing
D) climatic conditions
Answer: C

Q7: A social factor which affects land availability and use is
A) temperature
B) soil pH
C) light intensity and duration
D) culture of the people
Answer: D

Q8: The followings are climatic factors affecting agricultural production except
A) rainfall
B) relative humidity
C) temperature
D) topography
Answer: D

Q9: Predators are used by farmers to
A) control pests
B) induce flowering in plants
C) protect the soil
D) hasten fruit ripening
Answer: A

Q10: Which of the following agents is not associated with chemical weathering?
A) Oxidation
B) Pressure
C) Hydrolysis
D) Carbonation
Answer: B

Q11: Which of the following statements is not correct about soil texture?
A) Soils with fine particles have higher water holding capacity than coarse soils
B) Fine-textured soils are warm soils and coarse-textured soils are cool soils
C) The effect of leaching in coarse-textured soils is greater than that in fine-textured soils
D) Fine-textured soils have higher nutrient holding capacity than coarse-textured soils
Answer: B

Q12: Inhibition of root and fruit formation are deficiency symptoms of
A) iron
B) nitrogen
C) chlorine
D) phosphorus
Answer: D

Q13: In the carbon cycle, carbon dioxide is used by crops for
A) photosynthesis
B) transpiration
C) decomposition
D) respiration
Answer: A

Q14: Flood irrigation is used for the cultivation of
A) water melon
B) swamp rice
C) oil palm
D) coconut
Answer: B

Q15: The presence of excess water in the colloids of soil particles is known as
A) drainage
B) waterlogging
C) irrigation
D) leaching
Answer: B

Q16: If rows of crops are spaced 1.0 m apart with one seed sown per stand, determine the spacing between stands to obtain a plant population of 40,000 plants per hectare
A) 0.25 m
B) 0.45 m
C) 0.45 m
D) 1.00 m
Answer: A

Q17: The correct sequence of pre-planting operations is
A) clearing → stumping →ploughing → harrowing
B) 
C) stumping → ploughing → harrowing → clearing
D) clearing → bulldozing → stumping → harrowing
Answer: A

Q18: Heat treament of oil palm seeds before sowing helps to
A) mobilize nutrients for the embryo
B) harden the mesocarp
C) break embryo dormancy
D) improve disease resistance
Answer: C

Q19: Imported plants are expected to be
A) vaccinated
B) improved upon
C) treated
D) quarantined
Answer: D

Q20: A breeding method which involves the production of heterozygous populations from homozygous lines is
A) inbreeding
B) introduction
C) selection
D) hybridization
Answer: A

Q21: . A raw material that could be obtained from the forest is
A) margarine
B) honey
C) mutton
D) butter
Answer: B

Q22: Which of the following methods of plant propagation is limited to plants which root easily?
A) Grafting and cutting
B) Layering and cutting
C) Budding and layering
D) Grafting and layering
Answer: B

Q23: Which of the following practices is not a way of maintaining ornamental plants?
A) Pruning
B) Weeding
C) Watering
D) Harvesting
Answer: D

Q24: Which of the following pairs of diseases attack® coffee?
A) Mosaic and smut
B) Smut and midge
C) Rust and mosaic
D) Rust and leaf spot
Answer: D

Q25: Insect-pests of crops could be controlled by
A) cover cropping
B) mulching
C) crop rotation
D) organic manuring
Answer: C

Q26: Which of the following insect-pests does not attack cotton?
A) Aphid
B) Cotton stainer
C) weevil
D) pink bollworm
Answer: C

Q27: Which of the followimg practices is an example of a cultural weed control method?
A) Use of insects
B) Mowing
C) Application of herbicides
D) Mulching
Answer: D

Q28: . A farmer collects 800 eggs from a laying stock of 1,200 birds per day. Determine the laying percentage of the stock
A) 150%
B) 67%
C) 50%
D) 33%
Answer: B

Q29: . By-products of livestock used as feed ingredients in poultry ration include
A) hides and hoofs
B) blood and bones
C) feathers and fur
D) skin and bones
Answer: B

Q30: The practice of mating closely related animals is called
A) cross breeding
B) hybridization
C) in-breeding
D) out-breeding
Answer: C

Q31: In fish farming, clarias is introduced to a pond stocked with Tilapia in order to
A) regulate the population for Tilapia
B) compete with Tilapia for feed
C) check pests in the pond water
D) regulate the turbidity of the pond water.
Answer: C

Q32: The demand for agricultual produce is generally
A) infinite
B) inelastic
C) unitary
D) static
Answer: B

Q33: Subsidies are given to farmers in the form of
A) reduced prices of inputs
B) provision of social infrastructure
C) high tariff on imported inputs
D) short term loans
Answer: A

papers.sourceText:
Q1: Which of the following problem does not cause of farm produce?
A) Use of crude farm tools
B) Poor transportation network
C) inadequate processing facilities
D) Inadequate storage facilities
Answer: A

Q2: Which of the following statements is not a reason for providing tractor-hiring services to farmers? To
A) encourage farm mechanization
B) increase the area of land to be cultivated
C) increase the cost of production
D) boost food production
Answer: C

Q3: The land tenure system which involves the outright purchase of land is
A) leasehold
B) communal
C) freehold
D) inheritance
Answer: C

Q4: . Which of the following statement is not a tractor-coupled implement?
A) plough
B) sheller
C) ridger
D) harrow
Answer: B

Q5: Which of the following statements is not true of electrical power? It
A) can be generated from solar energy
B) is the cleanest source of farm power
C) can perform work on its own
D) 
Answer: C

Q6: The survey equipment used for measuring angular distance is
A) offset staff
B) measuring tape
C) ranging pole
D) prismatic compass
Answer: D

Q7: . The practice of growing arable and forage crops alternately on a piece of land is called
A) ley farming
B) mixed farming
C) alley farming
D) pastoral farming
Answer: A

Q8: . Which of the following groups of raw materials are used in textiles industries?
A) Guinea corn, wheat and kenaf
B) Cotton, jute and wool
C) coffe, cotton and cocoa
D) wool, palm kernel and maize
Answer: B

Q9: Which of the following is an example of igneous rock?
A) Basalt
B) dolomite
C) limestone
D) Marble
Answer: A

Q10: The chemical composition of soil is mostly influenced by
A) climate
B) time
C) topography
D) parent material
Answer: D

Q11: A beneficial effect of bush burning on the soil is the
A) reduction of soil microbial activities
B) exposure of soil surface to erosion
C) destruction of weed seeds
D) destruction of soil organic matter
Answer: C

Q12: Which of the following practices does not replenish lost soil nutrients?
A) crop rotation
B) fallowing
C) liming
D) bush burning
Answer: D

Q13: The use of inorganic fertilizer is preferable to organic manure because inorganic fertilizer
A) improves soil structure
B) releases nutrients to the soil faster
C) . reduces leaching of soil nutrients
D) improves soil water holding capacity
Answer: B

Q14: Which of the following statement describes an advantage of underground drainage? It
A) allows for free movement of farm machinery
B) checks the growth of weeds
C) improves soil texture
D) . increases organic matter content of soil
Answer: A

Q15: Which of the following crops is usually classified as a vegetable?
A) Lycopersicon esculentum
B) Ananas sativa
C) Hevea brasiliensis
D) Theobroma cacao
Answer: A

Q16: Thinning is a farm operation in which
A) empty spaces where seeds did not germinate are replanted
B) the number of seedlings per stand is reduced to one or two
C) fertilizers and manures are applied to crops.
D) effort is made to control pests.
Answer: B

Q17: Which of the following plants is not a pasture grass?
A) Pennisetum purpureum
B) Axonopus compressus
C) Stylosanthes gracilis
D) Panicum maximum
Answer: C

Q18: One advantage of cross breeding is that the
A) offspring resemble the recessive parent
B) yield of the offspring may not be comparable to those of the parents
C) offspring perform better than the average of the parents
D) offspring cannot survive adverse environmental conditions.
Answer: C

Q19: Assuming that brown colour is dominant over black colour in cowpea. What percentage of the F1 generation will have brown colour, if a homozygous brown cowpea is crossed with a homozygous black cowpea?
A) 100%
B) 75%
C) 50%
D) 25%
Answer: A

Q20: Ornamental plants are commonly used for the following purposes except
A) for exterior decorations
B) as sources of perfumes
C) provision of shade
D) as bedding materials for animals
Answer: D

Q21: Hibiscus and Croton are examples of
A) ground covers
B) hedge plants
C) lawn plants
D) avenue plants
Answer: B

Q22: . A disadvantage of vegetative propagation is that
A) plants are true to type
B) fruits are small in size
C) plants take a long time to mature
D) diseases are easily transferred to offspring
Answer: D

Q23: An effective method of preventing viral diseases in crops is by
A) treating the seeds with fungicides
B) practicing crop rotation
C) regular spraying of crops
D) planting resistant varieties

D) electoral officer
Answer: c

Q: Which of the following was the main organ of the defunct OAU?
A) The Liberation Committee
B) The Council of Ministers
C) The Commission for Meditation, Conciliation and Arbitration
D) The Assembly of Heads of State and Government
Answer: d
Solution: The Assembly of Heads of State and Government was the supreme organ of the Organization of African Unity (OAU). As the highest decision-making body, it convened annually to set policies, resolve continental disputes, and coordinate collective action. 

Q: Unwritten constitution means that the constitution is
A) not written down
B) based only on conventions.
C) not contained in any single book
D) in draft
Answer: c

Q: The process of depriving persons of the right of voting is known as
A) enfranchisement
B) disqualification
C) dismissal
D) disenfranchisement
Answer: d

Q: In a presidential system of government, ministers are
A) individually responsible to the president
B) individually responsible to the senate
C) collectively responsible to the president
D) collectively responsible to the electorate
Answer: a

Q: The main attributes of a state are
A) government, the police and the armed forces
B)  population, territory, government and sovereignty
C) federal state and local governments
D) the press, the legislature, the executive and the judiciary
Answer: b
Solution: The four essential attributes of a state are:

Population: A defined group of people within the state.

Territory: A recognized geographical area with borders.

Government: An organized system to enforce laws and administer policies.

Sovereignty: Supreme authority to govern without external interference.

Q: Under the 1999 Constitution, the appointment of Ministers and Ambassadors must be ratified by the ........
A) Senate
B) House of Representatives
C) National Council of States
D) Presidency
Answer: a
Solution: The appointment of ministers and ambassadors must be ratified by the Senate Under the 1999 Constitution.

Q: One of the programmes binding members of the Commonwealth is the
A) food and aid programme
B) cultural programmes
C) agenda for peace
D) scholarship scheme.
Answer: d

Q: Problems arising from population census in Nigeria are mainly caused by
A)  public opinions of the people
B) unreliable census figures
C) political manipulation by the elite
D) the registeration of the underaged people
Answer: c
Solution: The primary issue undermining Nigeria’s population censuses is political manipulation by elites. Political and ethnic leaders often inflate or suppress population figures to secure advantages such as:

Resource Allocation: Federal revenue and infrastructure projects are distributed based on population size, incentivizing states to overreport numbers.

Electoral Advantage: Larger populations translate to more legislative seats and political influence, driving falsification.

Ethnic and Regional Rivalry: Competing groups manipulate data to assert dominance, fostering distrust in census outcomes.

Q: Federalism was introduced in Nigeria under the
A) Lyttelton Constitution
B) Macpherson Constitution
C) Richards Constitution
D)  Independence
Answer: a
Solution: The Lyttleton Constitution was enacted in 1954 and it established the federal system of government and paved the way for independence.

This constitution is considered the start of federalism, as it provided for a division of power between the central government and the regions, unlike the Richards constitution that created provinces/regions, with no autonomy being given to the regions.

Q: The Headquarters of Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) is located in
A) Algiers
B) Baghdad
C) Riyadh
D) Vienna
Answer: d

Q: A key principle of the socialist system of government is the ___________.
A) minimal government intervention in the economy
B) private ownership of the means of production
C) power concentrated in the hands of a few elite individuals
D) equality of opportunity and outcome
Answer: d
Solution: A key principle of the socialist system of government is the equality of opportunity and outcome. This means that in a socialist system, the government controls the means of production and wealth is distributed equally among the population to ensure everyone has the same opportunities and outcomes.

Q: Argumentation, negotiation and deliberation on the subject matter of a bill begins at the_______
A) third stage
B)  first reading
C) committee stage
D)  second reading
Answer: d
Solution: The second reading is where debate, argumentation, negotiation, and deliberation on the subject matter of a bill begin. At this stage:

Lawmakers discuss the general principles of the bill.
They debate its merits and implications before deciding whether it should progress to the next stage.
If the bill passes the second reading, it moves to the committee stage for detailed examination.

Q: The delegation of Administrative Powers to the local units with the central supervision and control is called.
A) devolution
B) decentralization
C) deconcentration
D) centralization
Answer: a

Q: Which of the following is an obligation of a citizen?
A) Attending political rallies
B) Taking part in Independence Day celebrations
C) Contesting elections
D) Paying respect to the national flag.
Answer: d

Q: The administrative head of a public corporation in Nigeria is the
A) Managing Directors
B) Secretary
C) Board of Directors
D) Chairman
Answer: a

Q: The process of selecting candidates to represent a political party in elections is known as
A) campaigning
B) primaries
C) electioneering
D) lobbying
Answer: b
Solution: The process of selecting candidates to represent a political party in elections is known as primaries. In the primary election, party members or delegates vote for their preferred candidate from a list of candidates. The winner of the primary election becomes the party's candidate in the general election.

Q: A social group consisting of two or more people who interact and identify will one another is __
A) nation
B) society
C) government
D) state
Answer: b
Solution: A society consists of individuals who interact and identify with one another.

Q: Public opinion becomes politically relevant when it
A) criticises people in power
B) influences the decision of government
C) aggregates views and interests
D)  is in support of government
Answer: b
Solution: Public opinion becomes politically relevant when it actively shapes and influences the decisions made by the government. While public opinion can aggregate views, criticize those in power, or show support, its true political relevance is demonstrated when it translates into pressure on policymakers and affects policy outcomes. This influence on government decisions is key to the functioning of a democratic system, as it holds leaders accountable and ensures that public concerns are reflected in governance.

Q: The state is different from the government because
A) The state unlike the government is permanent
B) .
The government is made up of powerful people.
C) Members of the government are elected.
D) The state is created by God.
Answer: a

Q: In the presidential system of government , the leader is basically the head of state and
A) government
B) the police
C) the military
D) the judiciary
Answer: a
Solution: In the presidential system of government , the leader is basically the head of state and government.

The Presidential system of government is the type of political organization in which the leader popularly known as the President is the head of state in reality. In short, the President is both head of state and that of government. He then combines both the executive and ceremonial functions. He comes into power through free and fair periodic election.

Q: The Aro age-grade system in igboland was
A) a religious organization
B) a political organization
C) a commercial organization
D) an imperial organization
Answer: b

Q: The non-British colony which is a member of the Common wealth is
A) Rwanda
B) Guinea-Bissau
C) Mozambique
D) Eritrea
Answer: c
Solution: Mozambique was never a British colony; it was a Portuguese colony. However, it joined the Commonwealth of Nations in 1995, becoming the first country with no historical ties to Britain to do so. Other non-British colonies that later joined the Commonwealth include Rwanda, which became a member in 2009. However, since this question was set in 2003, Mozambique is the best answer to this question.

Q: In Nigeria, the head of the electoral commission is called the
A) Administrative Secretary
B) Chairman
C) Electoral Commissioner
D) Presiding Officer
Answer: b

Q: The organs of ECOWAS do NOT include the
A)  Accra
B) Abuja
C)  Niamey
D)  Cotonou
Answer: b
Solution: The ECOWAS Secretariat is located in Abuja, Nigeria. 

Q: The centre-piece of Nigeria’s foreign policy covers only
A) Asia
B) Europe
C) Africa
D) Latin America.
Answer: c

Q: The absence of the rule of law in government will bring about
A) human rights abuse
B) treasonable offences
C) corrupt practices
D) political apathy
Answer: a
Solution: The absence of the rule of law in government will bring about human rights abuse.

This is so as the rule of law refers to the constitutional provision which emphasizes the supremacy of the law, the equality before the law and existence of fundamental human rights.

Q: A major function of the warrant chiefs was to
A) prevent tribal wars
B)  supervise native courts and markets
C) stop ritual killingss
D) take charge of local administration.
Answer: d
Solution: A major function of the warrant Chiefs was to take charge of local administration.

The chiefs were the heads of the administration of their various communities.

Q: Which of the following is not a function of a party secretariat?
A) Electing the leader of the party
B) Organizing party conferences
C) Publishing the party’s manifesto
D) Planning party strategy to win election
Answer: a

Q: The Commission that examines complaints of civil wrongs committed by government employees is 
A)  Public Complaints Commission
B)  Civil Service Commission
C)  Economic and Financial Crimes Commission
D)  Judicial Service Commission
 
Answer: a
Solution: The Public Complaints Commission is a body responsible for receiving an responding to complaints from the public about the wrongdoings of civil servants and other government employees. They have the power to offer recommendations for the punishments of such employees. 

Q: Multi-laterism in Nigeria's foreign policy entails her
A) stand on Africa as the center piece of her policy
B) non-aligned posture in the international system
C) quest for a permanent seat in the UN Security Council
D) membership of international organizations
Answer: d
Solution: Multi-laterism in Nigeria's foreign policy entails her membership of international organizations.

Q: A major consequence of the privatization exercise in Nigeria is
A) the collapse of the Nigerian economy
B) reduction in foreign exchange
C) hıgh rate of indebtedness
D) mass retrenchment of labour
Answer: d
Solution: The sole aim of Privatization is profit-making. There is often a reduction of costs or spending and  mass retrenchment of labour in response to economic difficulty.

Q: The highest ruling body under the Murtala Obasanjo regime differed remarkably from that of the Gowon
A) administration because of the
B) inclusion of civilians as members
C) exclusion of military governors from the council
D) inclusion of the Chief justice as member
Answer: b

Q: Citizenship refers to the
A) legal status of a member of a state
B) indigenous member of a state
C) highest position in a state
D) social status of a person in a state
Answer: b

Q: Which of these is not a major characteristic of the rule of law?
A) Judicial independence
B) Separation of powers
C) Equality before the law
D) Supremacy of the law
Answer: b
Solution: Separation of powers is also called a system of checks and balances because the branches can check up on each other and if any of the branches get too strong, that branch will be balanced by the others. However, it is not a feature of the rule of law.

Q: Professor lbrahim Gambari was the Special Assistant to the United Nations Secretary General on____________
A) Security matters
B) African affairs
C) Political and social matters
D) The Economic Commission of Africa.
Answer: b
Solution: Professor Ibrahim Gambari was appointed as the Special Adviser to the United Nations Secretary-General on Africa in 1999. In this role, he focused on various issues pertaining to the African continent, including political, economic and social matters as well as promoting peace and development in Africa.

Q: Privatization and commercialization programmes in Nigeria have
A)  increased public utilities
B) de-emphasized government ownership
C) reduced government revenue
D) encouraged corruption
Answer: b
Solution: Privatization and commercialization programs in Nigeria were initiated to reduce the government's direct involvement in business enterprises. By transferring ownership and management of public enterprises to private entities, these programs aimed to enhance efficiency, stimulate economic growth, and alleviate the financial burden on the government. This strategic shift marked a significant move away from extensive government ownership toward a more market-driven economy.​

While these programs have had varied impacts, including debates on their influence on government revenue and concerns about corruption, their primary characteristic has been the reduction of government ownership in favor of private sector participation.

Q: The Nigerian federalism is a
A) four-tier system
B) three-tier system
C) two-tier system
D) one-tier system
Answer: b
Solution: The Nigerian federalism is a Three-Tier System.
They are as follows:

1. Federal or Central Government
2. Regional/State Governments
3. Local Governments.

Q: Which of the following was the main organ of the defunct OAU?
A) The Liberation Committee
B) The Council of Ministers
C) The Commission for Meditation, Conciliation and Arbitration
D) The Assembly of Heads of State and Government
Answer: d
Solution: The Assembly of Heads of State and Government was the supreme organ of the Organization of African Unity (OAU). As the highest decision-making body, it convened annually to set policies, resolve continental disputes, and coordinate collective action. 

Q: One major factor that differentiates the presidential from the parliamentary system is: 
A) separation of powers
B) judicial independence 
C) passage of bills  
D) party system.
Answer: a

Q: In a parliamentary system, when the legislature passes a vote of no confidence on the executive, it means that the
A) executive is required to resign
B) legislature ceases to trust the executive
C) legislature commences legal proceeding against the executive
D) executive is expected to go on suspension
Answer: a

Q: The final stage in the process of enacting legislation is  
A) assent  
B) final reading  
C) notification  
D) guillotine  
Answer: a

Q: An example of a country ruled by a constitutional monarch is
A) Uganda
B) Morocco
C) Italy
D) Libya
Answer: c

Q: Which of the following is NOT a source of local government finance?
A) Commercial ventures
B) Grants
C) Rates
D) Sale of bonds
Answer: d

Q: Government is the machinery established to manage the affairs of
A) rulers
B) aliens
C) the civil service
D) the state
Answer: d

Q: The second military coup data in Nigeria took place on 
A) 15-Jan-66
B) 1-Oct-66
C) 29-Jul-66
D) 13-Feb-76
Answer: c

Q: The first Military President of Nigeria is
A) Lt. General Olusegun Obasanjo
B) Major General J.T.U. Aguiyi-Ironsi
C) Major General Ibrahim Babangida
D) General Murtala Muhammed
Answer: c

Q: Nigeria's departure from pro-west policy during the Murtala Muhammed regime was as a result of
A) the economic interest of the West in Nigeria
B) Nigeria's increased international influence
C) the growing trade between Nigeria and the East
D) Nigeria's concern for decolonization in Africa
Answer: d
Solution: Nigeria departure from pro-west policy during the Murata Mohammed regime was a result of Nigeria's concern for decolonization in Africa.

Among the regime's achievements was its spectacular support for decolonization and self-determination as epitomized by its recognition of Agostino Neto's Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA)

Q: A Security Council resolution requires the concurrence of
A) 1 of the 5 permanent members
B) all of the 5 permanent members
C) 9 of the 15 council members
D)  3 of the 5 permanent members
Answer: c
Solution: In the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), a resolution requires the approval of at least 9 out of the 15 council members including the concurring votes of all 5 permanent members (United States, United Kingdom, China, Russia, and France). This means that while 9 votes are necessary, a single veto from any of the 5 permanent members can block the resolution.

Q: A country is most likely to have a good government only if it has
A) a good constitution but bad operators
B)  good operators but bad constitution
C) a good constitution and good operators
D) illegitimate government.
Answer: c
Solution: A good government requires both a sound legal framework (constitution) and competent leaders (operators).

Q: South-South cooperation is a major policy plan on which Nigeria bases her relations with
A) developed countries
B) countries of the southern hemisphere
C) developing countries
D) member countries of OAU
Answer: c
Solution: South-South cooperation refers to the collaboration between countries in the Global South, primarily focused on mutual development, technical exchange and sharing of resources and knowledge to address common challenges. Nigeria, as a developing country, engages in South-South cooperation with other developing nations, rather than with developed countries.

Q: Under the 1979 Constitution, statutory allocation of revenue to local government councils is the responsibility of the
A) Council of State
B) Houses of Assembly
C) National Economic Council
D) Federal Legislature.
Answer: d

Q: One of the major defects of the Nigerian council which necessitated its replacement was that....
A) the meetings of the council were poorly attended
B) the council could only make law for the southern protectorate
C)  the executive council was powerful than it
D) the council was unrepresentative
Answer: d
Solution: The unrepresentative nature and figurehead stance of the Nigerian Council's membership is a stand-alone reason for the flaw of the platform. Most members were Whites who didn't understand the interests of the people they seek to govern.

Q: The Headquarters of Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) is located in
A) Algiers
B) Baghdad
C) Riyadh
D) Vienna
Answer: d

Q: Africans were first elected to the legislature council in British West African 
A) Ghana 
B) Sierra Leone 
C) The Gambia 
D) Nigeria
Answer: d

Q: The United Nations Organization (UNO) was founded in
A) 1919
B) 1935
C) 1939
D) 1945
Answer: d

Q: Election among candidates from the same party before the final elections are called
A) Primaries
B) Running Mates
C) Second ballots
D) Party conventions
Answer: a

Q: The pre-colonial Tiv society can best be described as
A) republican
B) aristocratic
C) feudalism
D) monarchical
Answer: a
Solution: The pre-colonial Tiv society was republican in structure, characterized by a decentralized, egalitarian system without centralized monarchy (D) or hereditary aristocracy (B).

Q: In the Pre-colonial Igbo society,the maintenance of peace and order was,the function of the
A) assembly of ezes
B) clan elders
C) age-grades
D) assembly of title holders
Answer: c
Solution: In pre-colonial Igbo society, age grades were groups of people of similar ages who played a key role in maintaining peace and order within the community. They were responsible for duties such as defending the community against external aggression, performing police functions, and ensuring that laws and policies were enforced. Their role helped check abuses by other authorities and facilitated the execution of decisions made by community leaders.

Q: The ________ as a new policy direction introduced by the French government that was aimed at granting more autonomy to its colonies under pressure from independence movements.
A) policy of assimilation
B) indignant policy
C) policy of association
D) Loi cadre
Answer: d
Solution: The loi-cadre ( Reform Act) was a French legal reform passed by the French National Assembly on 23 June 1956. It marked a turning point in relations between France and its overseas empire. Under pressure from independence movements in the colonies, the government transferred a number of powers from Paris to elected territorial governments in French African colonies and also removed remaining voting inequalities by implementing universal suffrage and abolishing the multiple electoral college system.

Q: Who was appointed by the federal government of Nigeria as the administrator of western region in 1962?
A) Dr. M. A. Majekodunmi
B) Chief Odeleye Fadahunsi
C) Chief S. L. Akintola
D) Chief Remi Fani Kayode
Answer: c

Q: The right of a citizen to seek redress means the right to________
A) fair hearing
B) free access to legal materials
C) seek an appeal under another judgement
D) exercise his political liberty
Answer: c
Solution: Seek an appeal under another judgement is the best answer because,  ''the right to seek redress'' is a fundamental element of rule of law. It means that aggrieved parties should be afforded the opportunity to have their cases re-examined especially by a court of higher authority.

Q: The following countries are settler colonies except  
A) Nigeria 
B) south Africa 
C) Angola 
D) Mozambique.
Answer: a

Q: The council constituted by Lord Lugard in 1914 has
A) 105 members seat
B) 50 members on seat
C) 36 members on seat
D) 25 members on seat
Answer: c
Solution: The council constituted by Lord Lugard in 1914, following the amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria, had 36 members; 24 official and 12 unofficial members. This was part of his administrative structure aimed at unifying the two regions.

Q: Before Nigeria became a republic, the highest body charged with the administrator of justice was the
A) Privy council
B) High court
C) Supreme court
D) Court of appeal
Answer: a
Solution: Before Nigeria became a republic, the highest body charged with the administration of justice was the Privy council. one of the features of the Republican Constitution of 1963 is that the supreme court of Nigeria became the highest court in Nigeria. Appeal cases stopped going to the privy council in London

Q: Nigeria’s non-aligned policy means that she will
A) have nothing to do with the super-powers
B) not take sides in international issues based on ideological considerations
C) avoid having any dealing with any country with Ideological
D) relate only with member countries of the Non-Aligned Movement
Answer: b

Q: Argumentation, negotiation and deliberation on the subject matter of a bill begins at the_______
A) third stage
B)  first reading
C) committee stage
D)  second reading
Answer: d
Solution: The second reading is where debate, argumentation, negotiation, and deliberation on the subject matter of a bill begin. At this stage:

Lawmakers discuss the general principles of the bill.
They debate its merits and implications before deciding whether it should progress to the next stage.
If the bill passes the second reading, it moves to the committee stage for detailed examination.

Q: Under the 1999 Constitution, the appointment of Ministers and Ambassadors must be ratified by the ........
A) Senate
B) House of Representatives
C) National Council of States
D) Presidency
Answer: a
Solution: The appointment of ministers and ambassadors must be ratified by the Senate Under the 1999 Constitution.

Q: In pre-colonial Igbo society, decisions on public issues were reached mainly through
A) the oracles
B) consensus
C) imposition
D) majority votes
Answer: b
Solution: In Pre-colonial Igbo society, decisions on public issues were reached mainly through consensus.

The decision were then taken back to the respective families for ratification or rejection.

Q: The highest grade in the Civil Service is known as the ............
A) Technical cadre
B)  Executive cadre
C) Clerical cadre
D) Administrative cadre
Answer: d
Solution: The Administrative cadre comprises the most senior civil servants who organize and coordinate the activities of the ministries. They execute high-level administrative work, advise ministers in the formulation and implementation of policies and serve as the communication link between the minister and other civil servants.

Recruitment to this class is based on university education and very competitive written examinations and interviews conducted by the civil service commission. In this class are directors-general, other directors, deputy directors, assistant directors, etc.

Q: The apex body under the military regime of Yakubu Gowon was __
A) Supreme military Council
B) Federal Executive Council
C) The Armed Forces Ruling Council
D) The national Council of State.
Answer: a
Solution: Under Yakubu Gowon, the Supreme Military Council was the highest governing body.

Q: The civil service in Nigeria operates under the principle of
A) autonomy
B)  separation of powers
C) none of the above
D) meritocracy
Answer: d
Solution: The civil service in Nigeria operates under the principle of meritocracy. This means that positions and promotions in the civil service are based on merit, rather than factors such as political affiliation or personal connections. This is intended to ensure that the civil service is staffed by competent and qualified individuals.

Q: The Independence constitution can be described as
A) monarchical and presidential
B) republican and parliamentary
C) monarchical and parliamentary
D) federal and republican
Answer: c

Q: A typical form of delegated legislation is
A) an act
B) a bill
C) a decree
D) a bye-law
Answer: d

Q: The responsibility for admitting new members to the OPEC rests with the
A) Summit
B) Secretariate
C) Conference
D) Board of Governors
Answer: c
Solution: The authority to admit new members to OPEC resides with the OPEC Conference, which is the organization's supreme decision-making body. Composed of delegations from all member countries, the Conference meets biannually and requires a three-quarters majority vote (including approval from all five founding members) to admit a new state.

Q: The decision to separate Lagos from the Western Region and make it a neutral Territory was taken at the party constitutional conference
A)  1950 general conference
B) 1953 constitutional conference
C) 1954 constitutional conference
D) 1963 All party constitutional conference
Answer: c
Solution: The 1954 conference led to Lagos being separated from the Western Region and becoming a neutral federal territory.

Q: In the parliamentary system of government, formal legislation can take the following forms except
A) royal proclamations
B) order in council
C) acts of parliament
D) ministerial pronouncement
Answer: a

Q: The essence of ECOWAS is to________
A) bring political parties together
B) foster interstate economic and political co-operation
C) emerging political event
D) expansion of scopes and powers
Answer: b
Solution: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is a regional organisation of 15 West African countries established on 28 May 1975. Its main goal is the promotion of the economic integration among its members. Indeed, ECOWASis one the five regional pillars of the African Economic Community (AEC).

Q: The ultimate aim of political parties is to
A) implement people-oriented programmes
B) acquire and exercise power
C) increase the political awareness of the electorate
D) formulate and implement policies
Answer: b

Q: A political party is different from a pressure group in its
A) source of finance
B) objective
C) organization
D) strategy.
Answer: b

Q: The agency responsible for investigating allegations of maladministration in the civil service is the
A)  Federal Civil Service Commission
B)  Code of Conduct Bureau
C)  Public Comlaints Commission
D) Federal Character Commission
Answer: c
Solution: The Public Complaints Commission (PCC) is the agency responsible for investigating allegations of maladministration in the civil service and other public institutions in Nigeria. It serves as an ombudsman, handling complaints from the public about injustice, corruption, and administrative inefficiency.

Q: An alien who has lived in Nigeria for twenty years may acquire citizenship by
A) nationalisation
B) naturalization
C) registration
D) marriage
Answer: b
Solution: An alien who has lived in Nigeria for many years can acquire citizenship through naturalization.

Q: An example of a country ruled by a constitutional monarch is
A) Uganda
B) Morocco
C) Italy
D) Libya
Answer: c

Q: Nigeria's commitment to the liberation of Africa could best be seen in her policy towards
A) Namibia and Mozambique
B) the Congo and Zimbabwe
C) Sierra Leone and Chad
D) South Africa and Angola
Answer: d
Solution: During the liberation struggles in Southern Africa, Nigeria was a leading voice in supporting anti-colonial and anti-apartheid movements. It provided both political and moral support to groups fighting apartheid in South Africa and to liberation movements in Angola. These policies were part of Nigeria’s broader commitment to Pan-Africanism and the liberation of oppressed peoples across the continent, making its stance toward South Africa and Angola a prominent example of this commitment.

Q: One of these was in existence  before the outbreak of the Second World War 
A) The OAU  
B) League of Nations 
C) The UNOD  
D) The Commonwealth of nations 
Answer: b

Q: The ratification of the appointment and dismissal of an Emir in the pre-colonial Fulani Empire was done by the
A) Empire of Lafiagi and the Etsu of pategi
B) Emirs of Kano and Katsina
C) Emirs of Gwandu and Sokoto
D) Emir of llorin
Answer: c

Q: One of the first action of military governments when they take over power in Nigeria is to
A) detain all the politicians
B) appoint new ministers and commissioners
C) tour the country to explain why they have taken over
D) suspend the constitution
Answer: d

Q: The type of government operated in Nigeria between October 1st 1979 to December 3 1983 is called a __________
A) Collegial system of government
B) Presidential system of government
C) Unitary system of government
D) Parliamentary system of government
Answer: b
Solution: During this period, Nigeria operated under the Second Republic, which was modelled after the United States' presidential system. In this system, the President is both the head of state and the head of government, separate from the legislature. This period marked a shift from the parliamentary system used during the First Republic.

Answer: d

D) Northern Region
Answer: a

A) funded by political parties
B) headed by a justice of the Supreme Court
C) headed by a professor of political science
D) independent of government control
Answer: d

Q: Which of the following was done during the Gowon administration to reduce regional structural imbalance in the federation?
A) Appointment of ministers
B) Creation of states
C) Increase in revenue allocation
D) Formation of political parties
Answer: b

Q: In important advantage of creating more constituents in a federal state is to 
A) Enhance the people’s participation in government 
B) Enable ambitions politicians gain political power

Answer: a

D)  Manufacturers Association of Nigeria
Answer: c
Solution: Promotional pressure groups are primarily focused on advocating for a specific cause or value system rather than representing economic or professional interests. The Civil Liberties Organisation is known for campaigning to promote human rights and civil liberties in Nigeria, making it a clear example of a promotional pressure group. By contrast, the Nigerian Medical Association and Manufacturers Association of Nigeria represent professional and economic interests respectively, while the Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs functions more as a religious advisory body.

Q: Multilaterism in Nigeria’s foreign policy entails 
A) Africa being the centre piece of Nigeria’s foreign policy 
B) Non aligned posture in international affairs 
C)  Quest   for a permanent membership  of the UN security Council 
D) Membership of International Organizations
Answer: d

Q: The immediate cause of the 1966 military coup de'etat in Nigeria was
A) nepotism
B) political instability
C) military ambition
D) corruption
Answer: b
Solution: The immediate cause of the 1966 military coup de'etat in Nigeria was political instability. It should be noted that the Action Group Crises of 1962 was one of the crisis that led to the military take-over of government in January 1966. The 1962 Action Group crisis continued to rear its ugly head, until Western Nigeria election crisis of 1965. The disagreement over the election result between UPGA and NNA in Western region resulted to a crisis which led to a breakdown of law and order. This situation attracted military intervention on 15th January, 1966.

Q: Freedom of speech is a fundamental human right enjoyed by citizens but it may be limited if
A) loyalty is not shown to the ruling party
B) it exposes the wrong doings of the government
C) it endangers the security of the state.
D) it is used to cause embarrassment to the judiciary.
Answer: c

Q: One of the following is not a specialized agency to the United Nations Organization

B) International Labour Organization 
C) World Health Organization 
D) UNESCO
Answer: a

Q: Fascism as an ideology facilitates
A) totalitarianism
B) socialism
C) communalism
D) liberalism
Answer: a
Solution: Fascism as an ideology facilitates Totalitarianism. It is an Italian version of totalitarianism which grew up in Italy under Benito Mussolini

Q: Diplomatic immunity is a limitation to
A) the theory of separation of powers.
B) principles of checks and balances.
C) parliamentary supremacy.
D) the rule of law
Answer: d

Q: Under the Hausa pre-colonial administration, the office of the Prime Minister is usually occupied by 
A)  sarki
B)  waziri
C) galadima
D)  madawaki
Answer: b
Solution: The waziri, in the Hausa pre-colonial era, was the Prime Minister in charge of all the officials in the palace. 

Q: A major characteristic of a confederal state is that
A) there is supremacy of the constitution
B) the citizens often owe allegiance to the centre
C)  political stability is usually low
D) the centre overides the regions
Answer: c
Solution: A confederal state is characterized by a weak central government with most authority vested in constituent regions or states. This decentralization often leads to political instability due to:

Lack of Cohesion: Competing regional interests and priorities can cause disputes, making collective decision-making difficult.

Limited Central Enforcement: The central authority lacks power to enforce laws or resolve conflicts between states, fostering uncertainty.

Historical Examples: The U.S. under the Articles of Confederation (1781–1789) faced instability (e.g., Shays' Rebellion, economic disarray) until replaced by a federal system.

Q: A fascist regime is both
A) representative and accountable
B) responsive and responsible
C) fair and legitimate
D) authoritarian and totalitarian
Answer: d

Q: The commitee that scrutinizes budget proposals in the legislature is the
A) Rules and Business Committee
B)  Public Accounts Committee
C) Finance Committee
D)  Appropriation Committee
Answer: d
Solution: The Committee that scrutinizes budget proposals in the legislature is the Appropriation Committee.

Q: The main objective of pressure groups is to
A) promote the interest of political parties
B) influence legislation for the benefit of their members
C) protect the interest of the country against foreigners
D) serve as opposition to the government
Answer: b

Q: The highest court of appeal under the Republican constitution of Nigeria was the
A) Federal High Court
B) Judicial Committee of the Privy Council
C) Regional court of Appeal
D) Supreme Court
Answer: d

Q: The process of pressure groups trying to influence legislation is known as
A) ultimatum
B) dialogue
C) strike
D) lobbying
Answer: d
Solution: Pressure groups are organisations which seek to influence the policies of the government and this process is known as lobbying.

Q: A political entity that possesses independence is a
A) community
B) nation
C) society
D) state
Answer: d
Solution: A political entity that possesses independence is a state.

The state must posses supreme authority within its territory. It must be independent of any foreign control.

Q: The creation of the office of the Prime Minister in Nigeria was accomplished in
A) 1951
B) 1954
C) 1957
D) 1959
Answer: c

Q: The leader of the northern people’s congress was 
A) Yakubu Maitama Sule 
B) Abubakar Tafawa Balewa 
C) Aminu Kano 
D) Ahmadu Bello
Answer: d

Q: The permanent members of the Security Council of the United Nations are
A) Germany, France, Poland, Hungary and China
B) Britain, Japan, Australia, Germany and the United States
C) the United States, Russia, France, Britain and Japan
D) the United States, Russia, France, Britain and China
Answer: d
Solution: The five permanent members of the UN Security Council, established after World War II, are the United States, Russia (originally the Soviet Union), France, the United Kingdom (Britain), and China. These nations hold veto power over substantive resolutions.

Q: One judicial function performed by the executive is
A) granting of amnesty
B) implementing judicial orders
C) ensuring obedience to the law
D) appointing judges.
Answer: a

Q: If the president refuses to sign a bill within a specific period, it can still become a law through
A)  legislative override
B) none of the above
C) judicial review
D) public petition
Answer: a
Solution: If the president refuses to sign a bill within a specific period, it can still become a law through legislative override. This means that if a sufficient majority of the legislature votes in favor of the bill, they can override the president's veto and the bill becomes law.

Q: It is the duty of a government to perform all the following functions, except
A) Preventing internal disorder
B) Ensuring security of life and property
C) Providing basic welfare services
D) Providing all the needs of its citizens
Answer: d

Q: Citizens who are legally qualified to vote form
A) Political parties
B) A Trade Union Congress
C) Members of the House of House Assembly
D) The electorate
Answer: d

Q: The subject matter of politics is best described  as   
A) political parties

Answer: b

Q: A state with a hegemonic political party is one in which
A) there is one dominant party
B) there is no opposition party
C) there is only one party
D) other parties are officially recognized
Answer: a

Q: Which of these is not a major characteristic of the rule of law?
A) Judicial independence
B) Separation of powers
C) Equality before the law
D) Supremacy of the law
Answer: b
Solution: Separation of powers is also called a system of checks and balances because the branches can check up on each other and if any of the branches get too strong, that branch will be balanced by the others. However, it is not a feature of the rule of law.

Q: A major feature of the policy of deregulation in Nigeria is the: 
A) enthronement of market forces mechanism 
B) increasing dominance of the economy by the state 
C) proliferations of public corporations 
D) phenomenal increase in direct foreign investment
Answer: a

Q: Delegated legislation refers to the laws made by
A) the legislature
B) military governments
C) civilian governments
D) non-legislative bodies
Answer: d
Solution: Delegated legislation refers to laws or regulations made by bodies other than the legislature, having been granted the authority to do so. This means they are created by non-legislative bodies, such as administrative agencies or local governments, under powers conferred by the legislature.

Q: Which of these is not an instrument of foreign policy
A) war    
B) diplomacy  
C) subversion   
D) foreign aid
Answer: d

Q: The Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy in the 1979 constitution do not include _________
A) democracy and social justice
B) federal character and inequality
C) concentration of wealth and provision of maximum welfare
D) national integration and ethnic loyalty
Answer: c
Solution: The Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy in the 1979 Nigerian Constitution were designed to guide government policies and promote national development. These principles focused on democracy, social justice, federal character, national integration, and equal opportunities for all citizens.

The constitution aimed to reduce the concentration of wealth in the hands of a few and instead promote fair distribution of resources and social welfare.
Option C is incorrect because "concentration of wealth" contradicts the principles of the constitution.

Q: Traditional rulers were restricted to ceremonial rules by the local  government  reforms of 
A) 1966
B) 1976
C) 1984
D) 1987
Answer: b

Q: An example of a country with a flexible constitution is
A) South Africa
B) Britain
C) Benin Republic
D) the United States of America.
Answer: d

Q: A recurring principal objective of Nigerian foreign policy is
A) defending Nigeria's friends in Africa
B)  cementing Nigeria's foreign relations
C)  promoting world peace with justice
D)  Justıfyıng Nıgeria's supremacy in Africa
Answer: c
Solution: A recurring principal objective of Nigeria's foreign policy has been the promotion of world peace with justice, especially through African unity, regional stability, and global cooperation. Nigeria's foreign policy is centered on:

Respect for international law and justice
Commitment to global peace and security
Promotion of African unity and economic development
Non-alignment and peaceful resolution of conflicts

Q: The central legislature of Nigeria became bicameral in
A) 1960
B) 1951
C) 1959
D) 1963
Answer: a
Solution: The central legislature of Nigeria became bicameral in 1960.  Macpherson Constitution of 1951 created two chambers of regional legislatures known as the House of Chiefs and the House of Assembly in the Northern and Western regions. Coming then to the independence constitution of 1960, bicameral legislatures were adopted in both the federal and regional government including the Eastern region.

papers.name: WAEC 2019 — Government (may-june)
papers.sourceText:
Q: The European Union (EU) is an 
A) Economic organization 
B) Association of former British colonies  
C) Organization of European states 
D) Union  of European  organization
Answer: c

Q: The ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID) has its headquarters in
A) Abuja
B) Abidjans
C) Lome
D) Dakar
Answer: c
Solution: The ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID), is the financial institution established by the 15 Member States of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) comprising Benin, Burkina Faso, Capo Verde, Côte d'Ivoire, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone and Togo.
The Bank's headquarters is in Lome, Togolese Republic.

Q: The option A4 model was used in the conduct of the
A) 2007 elections
B) 1983 elections
C) 1993 elections
D) 1999 elections
Answer: c

Q: Nigeria''s support for the South-South Cooperation is based on her desire to
A) assert her leadership role in Africa
B) promote her non-aligned policy
C) promote economic understanding in the Third World
D) counter the political and military domination by major powers
Answer: c
Solution: Nigeria's support for South-South Cooperation is rooted in its commitment to fostering economic collaboration and mutual development among developing nations (the "Third World"). This cooperation aims to enhance resource sharing, technology transfer, and collective self-reliance, reducing dependency on the Global North.

Q: The basic unit of every political organization in the Igbo pre-colonial era was the
A) ala
B) family
C) age-grade
D) village council
Answer: b
Solution: The Family Group is one of the most recognized institutions in pre-colonial Igbo society as the basic unit of every political institution.

Q: An attribute that Nigeria shares with most non-aligned countries is
A) her large population
B) her heterogeneous population
C) her large size
D) the state of  her economy.
Answer: d

Q: A parliamentary-cabinet system of government is practiced in
A) Canada
B) Nigeria
C) the Soviet Union
D) all European countries
Answer: a

Q: Occupational pressure groups pursue their objectives mainly by
A) issuing ultimatums and embarking on strikes
B) alienating the government
C)  embarking on guerrilla warfare
D) contesting elections
Answer: a
Solution: Occupational pressure groups pursue their objectives mainly by pursue their objectives mainly by issuing ultimatums and embarking on strikes. The pressure groups give, 7, 14 or 21 days ultimatum to the government at the end of this, any action which the group deems necessary will be taken against the government. If the demands of the pressure groups are not met at the end of the ultimatum given, they will have to embark on strikes and boycotts.

Q: The powers allocated to the central government in a federation are contained in the
A) central legislative list
B) exclusive legislative list
C) residual legislative list
D) concurrent legislative list.
Answer: b

Q: An interest group that admits members and conducts its affairs according to stated rules is described as
A) organizational
B) associational
C) non-associational
D) institutional
Answer: b
Solution: An interest group that admits members and conducts its affairs according to stated rules is described as associational

Q: which pre-colonial Nigerian Kingdom was known for its artistic and cultural achievement?
A) Nupe
B) Igbo
C) Kanem-Bornu
D) Benin
Answer: d
Solution: The Benin Kingdom, in pre-colonial Nigeria, was known for its artistic and cultural achievements. The kingdom was renowned for its brass sculptures, its ivory carvings, and its palace architecture. The Benin Kingdom's art was so highly valued that it influenced the development of modern Western art.

Q: Nigeria is regarded as a frontline state because she
A) sent policemen for peacekeeping in Namibia
B) assisted the liberation struggle in Southern Africa
C) assisted ECOMOG troops in Liberia
D) sent troops for peacekeeping Somalia.
Answer: b

Q: Nigeria's departure from pro-west policy during the Murtala Muhammed regime was as a result of
A) the economic interest of the West in Nigeria
B) Nigeria's increased international influence
C) the growing trade between Nigeria and the East
D) Nigeria's concern for decolonization in Africa
Answer: d
Solution: Nigeria departure from pro-west policy during the Murata Mohammed regime was a result of Nigeria's concern for decolonization in Africa.

Among the regime's achievements was its spectacular support for decolonization and self-determination as epitomized by its recognition of Agostino Neto's Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA)

Q: Bicameralism refers to
A) a one chamber legislature
B) the process of voting in the legislature

Answer: d

Q: In the Oyo traditional political system, the Alafin of Oyo was elected or chosen by a group known as
A) Oyo Mesi
B) Bales
C) Obas
D) Ogboni
Answer: a
Solution: In the Oyo Empire’s traditional political system, the Oyo Mesi (a council of seven high-ranking chiefs) held the authority to elect or depose the Alafin. This council ensured checks and balances by selecting a new Alafin from the royal lineage and overseeing his governance.

Q: Serfs are the dominated class under
A) capitalism
B) socialism
C) fascism
D) feudalism
Answer: d
Solution: Serfs are the dominated class under feudalism. The first class is the king who was regarded as the sole owner of the land. The Serfs were the actual cultivators of the land.

Q: In Nigeria, the agency mainly responsible for the maintenance of internal peace and security is the

Answer: d

Q: Nigeria teamed up with other developing countries to assert a neutral posture under the platform of
A) Nationalist Movement
B) Pan - African Movement
C) Non - aligned Movement
D) Negritude Movement
Answer: c

Q: Decree 34 of 1966 was unacceptable to many Nigerians because it was
A) seen as an instrument of impoverishment
B) perceived to abolish the federal system
C) promulgated without consultation with the people
D) considered as alien
Answer: b
Solution: Ironsi promulgated Decree Number 34 of 1966, which abrogated the federal system of government and substituted a unitary system; he argued that the military could only govern in this way.

Q: Under Nigeria’s Second Republic, the Senate was under the leadership of
A) John Wash Pam
B) J. S. Tarka
C) Joseph Wayas
D) Godwin Ume-Ezeoke.
Answer: c

Q: Nationalism in Africa eventually led to
A)  a rapid political awareness among the colonialists
B) the alignment of the new states
C) de-colonisation

Answer: c
Solution: African nationalism led to independence from colonial rule.

Q: The right of citizens to vote is
A) adult suffrage
B) universal suffrage
C) nationality suffrage
D) electoral suffrage.
Answer: b

Q: Who is the current chairperson of ECOWAS?
A) Bola Ahmed Tinubu
B)  Alassane Ouattara
C) Macky Sall
D) Nana-Akufo Ado
Answer: a
Solution: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has been elected the chairman of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS). He was elected at the 63rd ordinary session of the ECOWAS Authority of Heads of State and Government in Bissau, the capital city of the Republic of Guinea-Bissau.

Q: Unwritten constitution means that the constitution is
A) not written down
B) based only on conventions.
C) not contained in any single book
D) in draft
Answer: c

Q: The one-time president of the United Nations General Assembly was
A) Joseph Garba
B)  Ibrahim Gambari
C) Arthur Mbanefo
D) Maitama Sule
Answer: a
Solution: The one-time president of the United Nations General Assembly was Joseph Garba. He was one of the top army officers in Nigeria.

Q: The French policy of Assimilation

B) was the same in theory as the British policy of indirect rule
