D) enabled the French to stay in Africa
Answer: c

Q: The review of Nigeria foreign policy under the Murtala/Obasanjo regime was done by
A) Udoji Committee
B) Aboyade Committee
C) Adedeji Commission
D) Philips Commission
Answer: c

Q: In which of the following systems is the power of the component units more than that of the central government?
A) Monarchical
B) Federal Governments
C) Unitary
D) Confederal
Answer: d
Solution: In a confederal system, the component units (such as states or regions) possess more authority than the central government. This arrangement allows the constituent entities to retain their sovereignty and delegate only specific, limited powers to the central authority, often related to common interests like defense or foreign affairs. Consequently, the central government operates at the behest of the component units and lacks independent authority. 

Q: 
A) In a single member constituency the voters in that constituency have the right to
B) declare a winner of an election in their constituency
C) .
elect many representatives.
D) elect one representative.
Answer: a

Q: Which of these is not the supreme organ of the OAU?
A) The Council of Ministers
B) The Administrative Secretary General
C)  The Assembly of Heads of States and Government
D) Appointment of staff
Answer: d
Solution: The Organization of African Unity (OAU) had several principal organs, including:​

The Assembly of Heads of State and Government: The supreme decision-making body of the OAU.​

The Council of Ministers: Composed of foreign ministers or designated representatives from member states, responsible for preparing conferences and implementing decisions of the Assembly.​

The General Secretariat: Headed by the Administrative Secretary-General, responsible for coordinating the activities of the OAU.

Q: A typical form of delegated legislation is
A) a decree
B) a bill
C) a bye-law
D) an act
Answer: c

Q: The highest organ of the state during the Babangida Regime was the
A)  Provisional Ruling Council
B) Supreme Military Council
C)  Armed Forces Ruling Council
D) Federal Executive Council
Answer: c
Solution: The Supreme Military Council, SMC was the top highest organ of the Federal Government of Nigeria in the military regimes of Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi, General Yakubu Gowon, Murtala Mohammed, General Obasanjo and Major General Muhammadu Buhari.
The body was instituted in 1966 by the administration of Aguiyi Ironsi deriving power from statute 8 of decree 1, it was later replaced as the highest body in a military regime by President Ibrahim Babangida in 1985 who created the Armed Forces Ruling Council.

Q: How many countries are in Africa? 
A) fifteen 
B) fifty-three 
C) fifty
D) fifty-five
Answer: b

Q: Citizenship of a state by descent requires that
A) one is born and bred in the state
B) one's mother was born in the state
C) one's grand parents were citizens of the state
D) one is domiciled in that state
Answer: c
Solution: Citizenship of a state by decent requires that one's grandparents were citizens of that state. A child born to a Nigerian couple in the United States of America is a Nigerian citizen by descent because his parents are Nigerians.

Q: Democracy is a system of government that is
A) constituted by the will of the majority of the citizens
B) imposed on the majority of the citizens
C)  designed to favour the elite
D)  put in place to favour the party caucus
Answer: a
Solution: Democracy is a system of government that is constituted by the will of the majority of the citizens.

It could also be defined as government in accordance with the principles of popular sovereignty, political equality, popular consultation and majority rule. One of the characteristics of democracy is that all government actions must be open to criticisms and must be according to the decisions, wishes and aspirations of majority of the people.

Q: The headquarters of the International Court of Justice is in
A)  Washington, D.C
B) Paris
C) London
D) The Hague
Answer: d
Solution: The headquarters of the International Court of Justice is at Hague in the Court of Justice is at Hague in the Netherlands.

The court is composed of fifteen judges. The judges are elected independently by the security council and the general assembly. It elects its own president and vice president, a registrar and other officers. Only nations and not individuals can bring cases to the court.

Q: The French policy of Assimilation in West Africa was a form of
A) indirect rule
B) direct rule
C) democratic rule
D) monarchy
Answer: b

Q: Nigeria played fundamental roles in the creation of 
A)  ECOWAS
B)  OPEC
C) UN
D) Commonwealth
Answer: a
Solution: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was created on the 28th of May, 1975 in Lagos, Nigeria under the leadership of General Yakubu Gowon of Nigeria and President Eyedama of Togo. 

The organisation is headquartered in Abuja, Nigeria whereas its financial headquarters is in Lome, Togo. 

Q: catered for the three  regions of Nigeria 
A) a renewed concept in international studies 
B) limited to the west 
C) a process of making the world  smaller 
D) an increasing integration of the world.
Answer: b

Q: In a federal system of government, legislative items constitutionally reserved for only the central government fall under the _________ list.
A) concurrent
B) executive
C) residual
D) exclusive
Answer: d
Solution: Exclusive Legislative List

These are the areas the powers reserved exclusively for the central government are defined. This means that only the central or federal government can legislate on the subjects in the exclusive list. Interference of the regional or state governments on matters in the exclusive list can be declared null and void and unconstitutional.

Q: PCl₅(g) = PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g). In the reaction above, a decrease in pressure will
A) Decelerate the reaction
B) Increase yield of PCl₃
C) Increase the yield of PCl₅
D) Accurate the reaction
Answer: b
Solution: By Le Chatelier's principle, decreasing pressure favours the side with more moles of gas. The left side has 1 mole of gas and the right side has 2 moles (PCl₃ + Cl₂). A decrease in pressure therefore shifts equilibrium to the right, increasing the yield of PCl₃ and Cl₂.

Q: The filter in the cigarette reduce the nicotine construct by
A) burning
B) adsorption
C) evaporation
D) Absorption
Answer: b
Solution: The filter in cigarettes reduces nicotine content by adsorption. The filter's dense network of cellulose acetate fibers provides a large surface area onto which nicotine molecules and other smoke particles adhere (stick to the surface), preventing them from reaching the smoker's lungs.

Q: Cu₂S(s) + O₂(g) = 2Cu(s) + SO₂(g). 

In the above reaction, the oxidation number of Cu changes from ___ to ___?
A) +1 to 0
B) 0 to +2
C) +2 to +1
D) 0 to +1
Answer: a
Solution: In Cu₂S, copper has oxidation number +1 (since S is -2 and there are 2 Cu atoms: 2x + (-2) = 0, x = +1). In the product Cu(s), copper is in its elemental state with oxidation number 0. Therefore Cu changes from +1 to 0 (reduction).

Q: Rare gases are stable because they
A) are monoatomic
B) form ions easily
C) have duplet or octet electronic configuration in the outermost shells in their atoms
D) are volatile gases
Answer: c
Solution: Rare (noble) gases are stable because their outermost shells contain a full complement of electrons — a duplet (2 electrons, for He) or octet (8 electrons, for Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn). This full outer shell configuration makes them chemically inert with no tendency to gain or lose electrons.

Q: A small quantity of solid ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl) is heated gently in a test tube. The solid gradually disappears producing two gases. Later, a white cloudy deposit was observed on the cooler part of the test tube. The ammonium chloride is said to have undergone
A) Distillation
B) Sublimation
C) Precipitation
D) Evaporation
Answer: b
Solution: Ammonium chloride undergoes sublimation when heated - it changes directly from solid to gas (decomposing into NH₃ and HCl), then reforms as a white solid deposit on the cooler parts of the tube when the gases recombine and cool.

Q: The number of isomers formed by C₆H₁₄ is
A) 4
B) 5
C) 2
D) 3
Answer: b
Solution: Alkanes exhibit structural isomerism due to different arrangements of carbon atoms. For hexane (C₆H₁₄), the isomers are:

n-hexane (straight chain)

2-methylpentane (one methyl group on carbon 2)

3-methylpentane (one methyl group on carbon 3)

2,2-dimethylbutane (two methyl groups on carbon 2)

2,3-dimethylbutane (two methyl groups on carbons 2 and 3)


There are 5 structural isomers of hexane.

The number of isomers formed by C₆H₁₄ is 5.

Q: Atomicity of ozone is
A) 1
B) 2
C) 3
D) 4
Answer: c
Solution: The atomicity of ozone is 3 because each ozone molecule contains three oxygen atoms (O₃).

Q: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ supports?
A) Charles's law
B) Boyle's law
C) Graham's law
D) Avogadro's law
Answer: b
Solution: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ is the mathematical expression of Boyle's Law, which states that at constant temperature, the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its volume.

Q: A major source of oxide of nitrogen is from the burning of
A) coal
B) wood
C) fuel
D) chlorofluorocarbons
Answer: c
Solution: The burning of fuel (particularly fossil fuels in vehicle engines and power plants) at high temperatures causes atmospheric N₂ and O₂ to combine, producing oxides of nitrogen (NOₓ) such as NO and NO₂. These are major contributors to air pollution and acid rain.

Q: An oxidation state of Cr in K₂Cr₂O₇
A) 7
B) 6
C) 5
D) 4
Answer: b
Solution: In K₂Cr₂O₇: K is +1, O is -2. Let Cr = x. 2(+1) + 2x + 7(-2) = 0 → 2 + 2x - 14 = 0 → 2x = 12 → x = +6. The oxidation state of Cr is +6.

Q: A difference between chemical and physical change is that in a chemical change
A) oxygen is consumed
B) heat is supplied
C) the reversible process occurs
D) a new substance is formed
Answer: d
Solution: The defining characteristic of a chemical change is that a new substance with different chemical properties is formed. Physical changes alter the form or state of matter without producing a new substance. Options A, B, and C can occur in both types of change.

Q: NH₃(g) + HCl(s) → NH₄Cl(s). The entropy change in the system above is
A) positive
B) zero
C) negative
D) intermediate
Answer: c
Solution: In this reaction, a gas (NH₃) and a solid (HCl) combine to form a solid (NH₄Cl). The disappearance of the gaseous phase results in a large decrease in disorder. Since the number of gaseous moles decreases from 1 to 0, entropy decreases, giving a negative entropy change (ΔS < 0).

Q: Which of the following metals burns with brick red
A)  Pb
B) Ca
C) Na
D) Mg
Answer: b
Solution: The metal that burns with brick red is calcium.

Q: Which of the following results in the fall of acid rain?
A) oxide of lead
B) particulate matter
C) oxides of sulphur
D) gaseous hydrocarbon
Answer: c
Solution: Oxides of sulphur (SO₂ and SO₃), released mainly from burning fossil fuels, react with water vapour in the atmosphere to form sulphurous and sulphuric acids, which fall as acid rain. Oxides of nitrogen also contribute, but among the options given, oxides of sulphur is correct.

Q: Flow of current in electrolytes is due to the movement of
A) electrons
B)  Holes and electron
C) Ions
D) Charges
Answer: c
Solution: In electrolytes, electric current is carried by positive and negative ions (cations and anions) moving toward the oppositely charged electrodes.

Q: In the industrial production of H₂ from water gas, the CO₂ produced along with the H₂ is removed by
A) Washing under pressure
B) Drying over phosphorus (V) oxide
C) Passing the mixture through limewater
D) Using ammoniacal copper (I) chloride
Answer: a
Solution: Water gas shift reaction:

CO + H₂O → CO₂ + H₂
This produces hydrogen but also carbon dioxide as a byproduct.
CO₂ removal method:

In industrial hydrogen production from water gas, CO₂ is removed by washing under pressure, where the gas mixture is passed through water under high pressure to dissolve and remove the carbon dioxide.

Q: Which of the following gives a precipitation when treated with NaOH solution?
A) AlCl₃
B) NH₄Cl
C) Na₂CO₃
D) CH₃COONa
Answer: a
Solution: AlCl₃ reacts with NaOH to form aluminium hydroxide, Al(OH)₃, a white gelatinous precipitate: AlCl₃ + 3NaOH → Al(OH)₃↓ + 3NaCl. NH₄Cl produces ammonia gas (not a precipitate), while Na₂CO₃ and CH₃COONa are fully soluble in NaOH.

Q: All these are electromagnetic waves except
A) White light
B) Photon
C) X-ray
D) Infrared
Answer: b
Solution: A photon is a quantum (particle) of electromagnetic energy, not a type of electromagnetic wave. White light, X-rays, and infrared radiation are all types of electromagnetic waves within the electromagnetic spectrum.

Q: Tartaric acid is used industrially to
A) make baking powder
B) make fruit juice
C) remove rust
D) dry substance
Answer: a
Solution: Tartaric acid is used industrially to make baking powder. It acts as the acid component in baking powder, reacting with sodium bicarbonate to release CO₂ gas, which causes dough to rise.

Q: An elements used in production of matches is
A) nitrogen
B) aluminum
C) copper
D) sulphur
Answer: d
Solution: Sulphur is used in the production of matches as a key component of the match head, where it acts as a fuel that ignites easily when the match is struck.

Q: Which of the following types of alkanols undergo oxidation to produce alkanoic acids?
A) I, II and III
B) I and II only
C) III only
D) I only
Answer: d
Solution: Only primary alkanols (I) are oxidized to produce alkanoic acids. Primary alkanols oxidize first to aldehydes, then to carboxylic (alkanoic) acids. Secondary alkanols oxidize to ketones (not acids), and tertiary alkanols resist oxidation.

Q: Which of these require crystallization most?
A) Drug making
B) Cement making
C) Paint making
D) Perfume making
Answer: a
Solution: Drug making requires crystallization most because pharmaceuticals must be highly purified, and crystallization is the primary method to achieve the purity levels required for safe and effective medications.

Q: In the production of soap, concentrated sodium chloride solution is added to
A) increase the solubility of soap
B) decrease the solubility of the soap
C) saponify the soap
D) emulsify the soap
Answer: b
Solution: Concentrated NaCl solution is added during soap production to decrease the solubility of soap (salting out). The high ionic strength of NaCl reduces the solubility of soap in water, causing it to precipitate out and separate from the glycerol and excess reactants.

Q: The basic particles from which matter could be made up of are as follow, except?
A) Salt
B) Atom
C) Ion
D) Molecule
Answer: a
Solution: The basic particles from which matter is made up are atoms, ions, and molecules. Salt is a compound (e.g., NaCl), not a basic particle — it is itself made up of ions. Therefore salt is the odd one out.

Q: Electronic configuration of element 13 in the subsidiary energy level is
A) 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p¹
B) 1s²2s²2p⁴3p¹3s¹
C) 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p³
D) 1s¹2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁴
Answer: a
Solution: Element 13 is Aluminium (Al) with 13 electrons. Filling in order: 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p¹. Total: 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 1 = 13 electrons. This matches option A.

Q: In countries where the temperature fall below 273 K, salt is always spilled on the road in order to
A) increase the boiling point
B) increase the density of the ice
C) make the ice impure
D) reduce the freezing point of ice
Answer: d
Solution: Salt (NaCl) is spread on icy roads to reduce the freezing point of water (freezing point depression). Dissolving salt in water lowers its freezing point below 0°C (273 K), causing ice to melt even at sub-zero temperatures and preventing refreezing.

Q: A liquid that will dissolve fat is
A) hydrochloric acid
B) calcium hydrochloride
C) kerosene
D) water
Answer: c
Solution: Kerosene is a non-polar organic solvent that dissolves fats by the principle "like dissolves like." Fats are non-polar molecules, so they dissolve in non-polar solvents like kerosene, not in polar solvents like water or acids.

Q: Which of these radioactive elements is commonly used as a nuclear fuel?
A) uranium
B) palladium
C) actium
D) thorium
Answer: a
Solution: Uranium (specifically U-235) is the most commonly used nuclear fuel. Its nucleus undergoes fission when struck by a slow neutron, releasing enormous energy and additional neutrons that sustain a chain reaction in nuclear reactors.

Q: What volume of 0.5 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄ will exactly neutralize 20 cm³ of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ NaOH solution?
A) 2.0 cm³
B) 5.0 cm³
C) 6.8 cm³
D) 8.3 cm³
Answer: a
Solution: Reaction: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Moles of NaOH = 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Moles of H₂SO₄ needed = 0.002/2 = 0.001 mol. Volume of H₂SO₄ = 0.001/0.5 = 0.002 dm³ = 2.0 cm³.

Q: Which of the noble gases has the greatest ionization energy
A) He
B) Xe
C) Ar
D) Rn
Answer: a
Solution: Helium has the greatest ionization energy among noble gases because it has the smallest atomic radius and strongest nuclear attraction on its electrons.

Q: Alloys are best prepared by
A) electroplating
B) Arc-welding
C) reducing and mixture of their metallic
D) cooking a molten of the metals
Answer: d
Solution: Alloys are best prepared by melting (fusing) the component metals together in the molten state and allowing the mixture to cool and solidify. This ensures homogeneous mixing of the metals at the atomic level, producing a uniform alloy.

Q: The weakest attractive force that can be observed between two molecules is
A) ionic
B) covalent
C)  co-ordinate covalent
D)  vander Waals
Answer: d
Solution: Van der Waals forces are the weakest attractive forces between molecules, arising from temporary dipoles and induced dipoles. These include London dispersion forces and dipole-dipole interactions.

Q: A fixed mass of gas occupies 92 cm³ at 3°C. What will be its volume at 18°C if the pressure remains constant?
A) 15.3 cm³
B) 87.3 cm³
C) 2.0 cm³
D) 97.0 cm³
Answer: d
Solution: Using Charles's Law: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂. Convert temperatures to Kelvin: T₁ = 3 + 273 = 276 K, T₂ = 18 + 273 = 291 K. Therefore V₂ = (92 × 291)/276 = 97.0 cm³.

Q: When salt loses its water of crystallization to the atmosphere on exposure, the process is said to be
A) efflorescence
B) déliquescence
C) effervescence
D) fluorescence
Answer: a
Solution: When a salt loses its water of crystallization to the atmosphere on exposure, the process is efflorescence. The hydrated crystals spontaneously lose water and become powdery.

Q: The gas that is most useful in protecting humans against solar marathon is
A) chlorine
B) ozone
C) carbon IV oxide
D) hydrogen sulphide
Answer: b
Solution: Ozone layer (O₃) in the stratosphere absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun, particularly UV-B and UV-C rays that cause skin cancer, cataracts, and damage to DNA.

Q: A suitable reagent for distinguish between ethanoic and ethanol is
A) bromine water
B)  Fehling’s solution
C) sodium hydrogen trioxocarbonate (iv)
D) Ammoniacal silver trioxonitrate(V)
Answer: c
Solution: Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydrogen trioxocarbonate(IV) (sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃) to produce carbon dioxide gas, which effervesces.
Ethanol does not react with NaHCO₃.


Sodium hydrogen trioxocarbonate(IV) is suitable for distinguishing between ethanoic acid and ethanol.

Q: When sugar is dissolved in tea, the reaction is accomplished by?
A) positive change
B) negative entropy change
C) no entropy change
D) a minimum entropy change
Answer: a
Solution: Dissolving sugar in tea is a spontaneous mixing process. The sugar molecules disperse throughout the liquid, increasing the disorder of the system. This represents a positive entropy change (ΔS > 0), as entropy increases when a solute dissolves in a solvent.

Q: Which of the following ions requires the largest quantity of electricity for discharge at an electrode?
A) 2.0 mole of Q³⁺
B) 2.5 mole of R²⁺
C) 3.0 mole of T⁻
D) 4.0 mole of Y⁻
Answer: a
Solution: Charge required = moles × charge per ion × Faraday constant. A: 2.0 × 3 = 6F; B: 2.5 × 2 = 5F; C: 3.0 × 1 = 3F; D: 4.0 × 1 = 4F. Option A (6F) requires the largest quantity of electricity.

Q: Detergents are manufactured with straight hydrocarbon chains, is to make them
A) soluble
B) biodegradable
C) cheaper
D) foamy
Answer: b
Solution: Detergents with straight (unbranched) hydrocarbon chains are biodegradable because soil bacteria can break down straight chains enzymatically. Branched-chain detergents resist bacterial degradation and cause persistent foam pollution in water bodies.

Q: Vulcanization involve the removal of
A) monometer
B) the single bond
C) the double bond
D) a polymer
Answer: c
Solution: Vulcanization involves the removal (or breaking) of carbon-carbon double bonds in rubber molecules. Sulfur reacts with these double bonds to create cross-links between polymer chains, converting soft rubber into harder, more durable material.

Q: The droplets of water observed around a bottle of milk taken out of though refrigerator is due to the fact that the
A) Temperature of the milk drops as it loses heat into the surroundings
B) Saturated vapour pressure of the milk is equal to the atmospheric pressure
C) Water vapour in the air around loses some of its energy to the bottle
D) Water vapour in the air around the bottle gains some energy from the bottle
Answer: c

Q: The maximum number of electrons in the N shell is?
A) 2
B) 8
C) 18
D) 32
Answer: d
Solution: The maximum number of electrons in any shell is given by the formula 2n², where n is the principal quantum number. For the N shell, n = 4. Maximum electrons = 2 × 4² = 2 × 16 = 32.

Q: The shape of ammonia molecules is
A) trigonal pyramidal
B) octahedral
C) square planar
D) tetrahedral
Answer: a
Solution: NH₃ has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair of electrons around the nitrogen. The lone pair repels the bonding pairs more strongly, compressing the H-N-H bond angle to ~107°. This gives a trigonal pyramidal shape (not tetrahedral, which is the electron geometry).

Q: One of the following is not a water pollutant?
A) Inorganic fertilizers
B) Warm water affluent
C) Oxygen gas
D) Biodegradable waste
Answer: c
Solution: Oxygen gas (O₂) is not a water pollutant. In fact, dissolved oxygen is essential for the survival of aquatic organisms. Inorganic fertilizers cause eutrophication, warm water effluent (thermal pollution) reduces dissolved oxygen levels and harms aquatic life, and biodegradable waste depletes oxygen as it decomposes. None of these are beneficial to water quality, whereas oxygen is necessary.

Q: Which of these reagents can confirm the presence of a triple bond
A) Bromine water
B) Acidified KMnO4 
C) Copper (I) chloride
D) Bromine gas
Answer: c

Q: In the production of soap, concentrated sodium chloride solution is added to
A) increase the solubility of soap
B) decrease the solubility of the soap
C) saponify the soap
D) emulsify the soap
Answer: b
Solution: Concentrated NaCl solution is added during soap production to decrease the solubility of soap (salting out). The high ionic strength of NaCl reduces the solubility of soap in water, causing it to precipitate out and separate from the glycerol and excess reactants.

Q: The inherited traits of an organism are controlled by?
A) RNA molecules
B) Nucleotides
C) DNA molecules
D) Enzymes
Answer: c
Solution: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) molecules carry the genetic information that determines inherited traits in organisms. Genes are segments of DNA that encode specific proteins and traits passed from parents to offspring. RNA is involved in protein synthesis but does not store hereditary information. Enzymes are proteins that catalyse reactions.

Q: Which of the following shows little or no net reaction when the volume of the system is decreased
A)  H2(g)  +  l2(g)  ⇌  2Hl(g)
B) 2NO2(g)  ⇌  N2O4(g)
C)  PCl5(g)   ⇌ PCl3(g)  + Cl2(g)
D)  203(g)   ⇌  3O2(g)
Answer: a

Q: Cu₂S(g) + O₂(g) → 2Cu + SO₂(g). What is the change in the oxidation number of copper in the reaction?
A) 0 to +2
B) 0 to +1
C) +1 to 0
D) +2 to +1
Answer: c
Solution: In Cu₂S, S has oxidation number -2, so each Cu must be +1 (since 2(+1) + (-2) = 0). In the product Cu, copper is in its elemental state with oxidation number 0. Therefore copper changes from +1 (in Cu₂S) to 0 (in Cu) — this is a reduction.

Q: Nitrogen, a component of air is used for
A) production of cooling agent
B) production of margarine
C) production of HNO₃
D) manufacturing of oil
Answer: c
Solution: Nitrogen from air is used to produce ammonia (NH₃) via the Haber process, which is then oxidized to nitric acid (HNO₃) via the Ostwald process. Margarine production uses hydrogen, and cooling agents use other gases.

Q: Phosphorous is stored under water to precvent it from
A) Dehydrating
B) Becoming inert
C) Smelling
D) Catching fire
Answer: d

Q: The reaction of halogens with alkanes in the presence of sunlight is an example of
A) oxidation reaction
B) addition reaction
C) hydrogenation reaction
D) substitution reaction
Answer: d
Solution: When halogens react with alkanes in the presence of sunlight (UV light), a hydrogen atom in the alkane is replaced (substituted) by a halogen atom via a free radical mechanism. This is free radical substitution. For example: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl. Addition reactions occur with alkenes, not alkanes.

Q: When Calcium ethynide is decomposed by water, the gas produced is
A) CO
B) H₂
C) C₂H₂
D) CH₄
Answer: c
Solution: Calcium ethynide is calcium carbide (CaC₂). When it reacts with water, it produces ethyne (acetylene) gas and calcium hydroxide: CaC₂ + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + C₂H₂. The gas produced is ethyne (C₂H₂), also known as acetylene, which is used in oxyacetylene welding.

Q: A few drops of conc HCl are added to about 10cm³ of a solution of pH 3.4. The pH of the resulting mixture is?
A) less than 3.4
B) greater than 3.4
C) unaltered
D) the same as that of the pure water
Answer: a
Solution: pH 3.4 means the solution is already acidic. Adding concentrated HCl (a strong acid) increases the concentration of H⁺ ions in the solution. A higher H⁺ concentration means a lower pH. Therefore the resulting pH will be less than 3.4.

Q: When water drops are added to calcium carbide in a container and the gas produced is passed through a jet and lighted, the resultant flame is called an?
A) Oxyethene
B) Oxyhydrocarbon flame
C) Oxyacetylene flame
D) Oxymethane flame
Answer: c
Solution: Calcium carbide (CaC₂) reacts with water to produce acetylene gas (ethyne, C₂H₂): CaC₂ + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + C₂H₂. When acetylene is burned in the presence of oxygen, it produces the oxyacetylene flame, which reaches temperatures above 3000°C and is used in welding and cutting metals.

Q: The electronic configuration of an element is 1S² 2S² 2P⁶ 3S² 3P³. How many unpaired electrons are there in the element?
A) 5
B) 4
C) 3
D) 2
Answer: c
Solution: The configuration 3P³ has three electrons distributed across three separate p orbitals (by Hund's rule, each occupies its own orbital before pairing). So 3P³ contributes 3 unpaired electrons. The s orbitals (1S², 2S², 3S²) and 2P⁶ are all fully paired. Total unpaired electrons = 3.

Q: The solution that will conduct the highest amount of electricity is
A) 2.0 moldm-3 of ethanoic acid
B) 0.5 mol dm-3 of ethanoic acid
C) 2.0 mol dm-3 of hydrochloric acid
D) 0.5 moldm-3 of hydrochloric acid
Answer: c

Q: The chlorinated alkane often used industrially to remove grease is?
A) Tetrachloromethane
B) Chloromethane
C) Trichloromethane
D) Dichloromethane
Answer: a
Solution: Tetrachloromethane (CCl₄) is a non-polar solvent widely used industrially as a degreasing agent because it dissolves grease and oils effectively without itself being flammable. Its non-polarity allows it to interact with and dissolve the non-polar grease molecules through dispersion forces.

Q: How many moles of CO₂ are produced when ethanol is burnt with 6g of oxygen?
A) 0.125
B) 0.250
C) 0.375
D) 0.750
Answer: a
Solution: Equation: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. Moles of O₂ = 6 ÷ 32 = 0.1875 mol. From equation, 3 mol O₂ produces 2 mol CO₂. Moles of CO₂ = (2/3) × 0.1875 = 0.125 mol.

Q: Which group does calcium belong to in the periodic table?
A) Alkaline earth metals
B) Halogens
C) Alkali metals
D) Noble gases
Answer: a
Solution: Calcium (Ca) has atomic number 20 and electron configuration [Ar] 4s². It is in Group IIA (Group 2) of the periodic table, known as the alkaline earth metals. This group includes beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium, and radium. Alkali metals are Group IA, halogens are Group VIIA, and noble gases are Group VIII/0.

Q: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. What happens to zinc in the above reaction?
A) oxidized
B) a reactant
C) reduced
D) a metal
Answer: a
Solution: In this reaction, zinc (Zn) goes from an oxidation state of 0 in the element to +2 in ZnCl₂. A loss of electrons and an increase in oxidation number constitutes oxidation. Zinc is therefore oxidised. Hydrogen simultaneously goes from +1 in HCl to 0 in H₂ gas, meaning hydrogen is reduced. Zinc is the reducing agent.

Q: At a given temperature and pressure, a gas X diffuses twice as fast as gas Y. It follows that
A) Gas Y is two times as heavy as Gas X
B) Gas Y is four times as heavy as Gas X
C) Gas Y is monoatomic
D) Gas X is diatomic
Answer: b
Solution: By Graham's Law of diffusion: rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass. Rate_X/Rate_Y = √(M_Y/M_X). Given Rate_X = 2 × Rate_Y: 2 = √(M_Y/M_X). Squaring both sides: 4 = M_Y/M_X. Therefore M_Y = 4 × M_X. Gas Y is four times as heavy as Gas X.

Q: Atomicity of ozone is
A) 1
B) 2
C) 3
D) 4
Answer: c
Solution: The atomicity of ozone is 3 because each ozone molecule contains three oxygen atoms (O₃).

Q: An example of a polysaccharide is?
A) Dextrose
B) Mannose
C) Glucose
D) Starch
Answer: d
Solution: Polysaccharides are complex carbohydrates made of many monosaccharide units joined by glycosidic bonds. Starch is a polysaccharide made of many glucose units. Dextrose, mannose, and glucose are all monosaccharides (single sugar units).

Q: Stainless steel is used for making
A) Tools
B) Coins and medals
C) Moving parts of clocks
D) Magnets
Answer: a

Q: Pollution of underground water by metal ions is very likely in a soil that has high
A) Acidity
B) Alkalinity
C) Chloride content
D) Nitrate content
Answer: a

Q: The table shows the compositions of the atmosphere of planet X: CO₂ = 4%, N₂ = 72%, O₂ = 24%. Which of these gases are present in higher percentages on earth?
A) CO₂ and O₂
B) N₂ and CO₂
C) CO₂, O₂ and N₂
D) O₂ and N₂
Answer: a
Solution: On earth: N₂ ≈ 78%, O₂ ≈ 21%, CO₂ ≈ 0.04%. On planet X: CO₂ = 4%, N₂ = 72%, O₂ = 24%. Comparing each gas: CO₂ on planet X (4%) is far higher than on earth (0.04%). O₂ on planet X (24%) is higher than on earth (21%). N₂ on earth (78%) is higher than on planet X (72%). The gases present in higher percentages on planet X compared to earth are CO₂ and O₂.

Q: What happens to the value of the equilibrium constant (Kc) for a reaction if the reaction is reversed?
A) It becomes zero
B) It becomes negative
C) It remains the same
D) It becomes the reciprocal of the original value
Answer: d
Solution: The equilibrium constant Kc is defined as the ratio of product concentrations to reactant concentrations at equilibrium. When a reaction is reversed, products become reactants and vice versa. The Kc for the reversed reaction is therefore 1 divided by the original Kc (its reciprocal). For example, if Kc = 4 for the forward reaction, then Kc = 1/4 = 0.25 for the reverse reaction.

Q: The elements that belong to the third period of periodic table are
A) Li, Be, Al and D
B) Na, P, O and Cl
C) B, C, N, and O
D) Na, Mg, S and Ar
Answer: d
Solution: The third period (Period 3) contains elements with atomic numbers 11–18: Na, Mg, Al, Si, P, S, Cl, and Ar. Option D (Na, Mg, S, Ar) are all correctly in Period 3. The other options contain Period 2 elements (Li, Be, B, C, N, O).

Q: When a solid substance disappears completely as a gas on heating, the substance is said to have undergone?
A) Sublimation
B) Crystallization
C) Distillation
D) Evaporation
Answer: a
Solution: Sublimation is the direct change of state from solid to gas without passing through the liquid phase. When a solid disappears completely as a gas on heating without melting first, it has sublimed. Examples include iodine, dry ice (solid CO₂), and ammonium chloride.

Q: Which of the following organic compounds is very soluble in water
A) C2H2
B) C2H4
C) CH3COOC2H5
D) CH3COOH
Answer: d

Q: Tin is unaffected by air at ordinary temperature due to its
A) Low melting point
B) Weak electropositive character
C) High boiling point
D) White lustrous appearance
Answer: b
Solution: Tin is resistant to corrosion at ordinary temperatures because of its weak electropositive (low reactivity) character. It has a low tendency to lose electrons and oxidize in air. This weak electropositive character means it does not readily react with oxygen or moisture at room temperature, making it useful as a protective coating (tinning).

Q: The acid that is used to remove rust is
A) Hydrochloric
B) Trioxonitrate (V)
C) Tetraoxosulphate (VI)
D) Boric
Answer: b

Q: Which of the following best represents a solid-gas mixture?
A) milk
B) kerosene
C) soil
D) smoke
Answer: d
Solution: Smoke is a colloidal dispersion of solid particles (soot, ash, carbon) in a gaseous medium (air). It is classified as a solid-in-gas colloid, also known as an aerosol. Milk is a liquid-in-liquid colloid (emulsion), kerosene is a pure liquid, and soil is a solid mixture with no gas as the dispersing medium.

Q: An aqueous solution of a metal salt M gives a white precipitate with NaOH which dissolves in excess NaOH. With aqueous ammonia, the solution of M also gives a white precipitate which dissolves in excess ammonia. Therefore the cation in M is
A) Zn
B) Ca
C) Al
D) Pb
Answer: a
Solution: Zn²⁺ gives a white precipitate of Zn(OH)₂ with NaOH, which dissolves in excess NaOH (amphoteric): Zn(OH)₂ + 2OH⁻ → [Zn(OH)₄]²⁻. It also gives a white precipitate with NH₃ solution that dissolves in excess NH₃ to form the tetraamminezinc complex: Zn(OH)₂ + 4NH₃ → [Zn(NH₃)₄]²⁺. Al³⁺ dissolves in excess NaOH but not in excess NH₃, eliminating option C.

Q: The filter in a cigarette reduces the nicotine content by
A) Burning
B) Adsorption
C) Evaporation
D) Absorption
Answer: b

Q: Proteins in acid solution undergo
A) Polymerization
B) Substitution
C) Fermentation
D) Hydrolysis
Answer: d

Q: 2C2H2(g)  +  5O2(g)     4CO2(g)  +  2H2O(g) In the reaction, the mass of carbon (IV) oxide produced on burning 78g of ethyne is [C = 12, O = 16, H = 1]
A) 39
B) 352g
C) 264g
D) 156g
Answer: c

Q: The component of an atom that contributes least to its mass is the
A) Nucleus
B) Neutron
C) Electron
D) Proton
Answer: c

Q: The above orbital diagram shown the electronic configuration of
A) chlorine
B) nitrogen
C) calcium
D) neon
Answer: b
Solution: The orbital diagram shows 7 electrons with configuration 1s² 2s² 2p³, which corresponds to nitrogen. The 2p orbital has three unpaired electrons (one in each 2p orbital), following Hund's rule of maximum spin multiplicity.

Q: CH₄(g) + Cl₂(g) → CH₂Cl(s) + HCl(g). The major factor that influences the rate of the reaction above is
A) Concentration
B) Catalyst
C) Temperature
D) Light
Answer: d
Solution: The reaction of methane with chlorine is a free radical substitution reaction initiated by UV light. Light provides the energy to break the Cl-Cl bond homolytically (Cl₂ → 2Cl•), generating chlorine radicals that start the chain reaction. Without light, the reaction does not proceed at room temperature, making light the major rate-determining factor.

Q: The curve depicts titration between
A) Strong acid and strong base
B) Strong acid and weak base
C) Weak acid and weak base
D) Weak acid and strong base
Answer: b
Solution: The curve starts at a low pH (~3), indicating a strong acid. The equivalence point and the final pH (~5) are both in the acidic range, which is characteristic of a strong acid-weak base titration (the salt formed is acidic). A strong acid-strong base titration would end at pH 7, and a weak acid-strong base would end above pH 7.

Q: The compound CH₃-C(H)(OH)-COOH shown above exhibits
A) Geometric isomerism
B) Positional isomerism
C) Structural isomerism
D) Optical isomerism
Answer: d
Solution: The compound shown is lactic acid (2-hydroxypropanoic acid). The central carbon atom is bonded to four different groups: CH₃, H, OH, and COOH. A carbon bonded to four different substituents is a chiral centre, making the compound optically active. It exhibits optical isomerism (enantiomers).

Q: What volume of 0.5 M H₂SO₄ will exactly neutralize 20 cm³ of 0.1 M NaOH solution?
A) 2.0 cm³
B) 5.0 cm³
C) 6.8 cm³
D) 8.3 cm³
Answer: a
Solution: Reaction: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Moles of NaOH = 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Moles of H₂SO₄ required = 0.002/2 = 0.001 mol. Volume of H₂SO₄ = 0.001/0.5 = 0.002 dm³ = 2.0 cm³.

Q: An isotope has an atomic number of 15 and a mass number of 31. The number of protons it contains is
A) 16
B) 15
C) 31
D) 46
Answer: b
Solution: The atomic number of an element equals the number of protons in its nucleus. Since the atomic number is 15, the atom contains 15 protons. The number of neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 31 − 15 = 16.

Q: Which of the following compounds is used as a gaseous fuel?
A) CH₃-CH₂-CHO₂-COOH
B) CH₃-C≡CH
C) CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-CH₃
D) CH₂=CH-CH₃
Answer: c
Solution: CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-CH₃ is butane, a saturated alkane widely used as a gaseous fuel in LPG (liquefied petroleum gas). Option B is propyne (an alkyne), D is propene (an alkene) — both are flammable but not common domestic gaseous fuels. Option A is not a real stable compound.

Q: Which of the following statements is true about 2-methylpropane and butane?
A) They have different number of carbon atoms
B) They are members of same homologous series
C) They have the same boiling points
D) They have different chemical properties
Answer: b
Solution: 2-methylpropane and butane are structural isomers — both have the molecular formula C₄H₁₀ and belong to the alkane homologous series. They have the same number of carbon atoms and similar chemical properties, but different boiling points due to different branching.

Q: In the diagram above, X is the
A) Enthalpy
B) Activated complex
C) Activation energy
D) Enthalpy change
Answer: d
Solution: In the energy profile diagram, X is the arrow showing the difference in energy level between the reactants and the products. This energy difference is the enthalpy change (ΔH) of the reaction. Since products are lower in energy than reactants, ΔH is negative (exothermic). The activation energy would be measured from reactants to the peak, not between reactants and products.

Q: The compound produced when sodium peroxide is heated with excess sodium is
A) Na₂CO₃
B) Na₂O
C) NaNO₂
D) NaOH
Answer: b
Solution: When sodium peroxide (Na₂O₂) is heated with excess sodium metal, the oxygen in the peroxide is reduced and sodium oxide (Na₂O) is formed: Na₂O₂ + 2Na → 2Na₂O. The excess sodium reduces the peroxide to the monoxide.

Q: The radioisotope used in industrial radiography for the rapid checking of faults in welds and casting is
A) Phosphorus-32
B) Cobalt-60
C) Carbon-14
D) Iodine-131
Answer: b
Solution: Cobalt-60 emits high-energy gamma rays, making it ideal for industrial radiography to detect internal faults in welds and castings. Phosphorus-32 is used in medical/biological research; Carbon-14 is used in radiocarbon dating; Iodine-131 is used in thyroid treatment.

Q: Ammonium chloride can be separated from its mixture with common salt by
A) Distillation
B) Evaporation
C) Decantation
D) Sublimation
Answer: d
Solution: NH₄Cl sublimes — it converts directly from solid to vapour on heating without melting. NaCl (common salt) does not sublime. Heating the mixture causes NH₄Cl vapour to rise and re-solidify on a cooler surface, separating it cleanly from NaCl.

Q: The industrial preparation of hydrogen gas from water gas is referred to as
A) Bosch process
B) Contact process
C) Haber process
D) Bayer process
Answer: a
Solution: The Bosch process produces hydrogen from water gas (CO + H₂) by reacting it with steam over a catalyst: CO + H₂O → CO₂ + H₂. The Contact process makes H₂SO₄; the Haber process synthesizes NH₃; the Bayer process extracts alumina from bauxite.

Q: What is the concentration of a solution containing 2 g of NaOH in 100 cm³ of solution? [Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1]
A) 0.05 mol dm⁻³
B) 0.30 mol dm⁻³
C) 0.50 mol dm⁻³
D) 0.40 mol dm⁻³
Answer: c
Solution: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g mol⁻¹. Moles of NaOH = 2/40 = 0.05 mol. Volume = 100 cm³ = 0.1 dm³. Concentration = 0.05/0.1 = 0.50 mol dm⁻³.

Q: MnO₄⁻(aq) + Y + 5Fe²⁺(aq) → Mn²⁺(aq) + 5Fe³⁺(aq) + 4H₂O(l). In the equation above, Y is
A) 10H⁺(aq)
B) 5H⁺(aq)
C) 8H⁺(aq)
D) 4H⁺(aq)
Answer: c
Solution: Balancing the half-equation for MnO₄⁻ in acidic solution: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O. The 8H⁺ ions are needed to balance the 4 oxygen atoms from MnO₄⁻ (each O needs 2H⁺ to form H₂O), and to balance the overall charge. Therefore Y = 8H⁺(aq).

Q: Alkanols have the general molecular formula
A) CₙH₂ₙ₋₂
B) CₙH₂ₙ₊₁CHO
C) CₙH₂ₙ₋₂OH
D) CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH
Answer: d
Solution: Alkanols (alcohols derived from alkanes) have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH, where the CₙH₂ₙ₊₁ part is the alkyl group attached to the hydroxyl (-OH) functional group. For example, methanol is CH₃OH (n=1) and ethanol is C₂H₅OH (n=2).

Q: Cast iron is used in making
A) Chains and agricultural implements
B) Iron sheets and retort stand
C) Nails and iron rods
D) Stoves and cookers
Answer: d
Solution: Cast iron, which contains about 3–4% carbon, is hard but brittle. It is used in making stoves, cookers, manhole covers, engine blocks, and pipes. Wrought iron (low carbon) is used for chains and ornamental work; mild steel is used for nails, rods, and sheets.

Q: Which of the following is not an alkali?
A) Ca(OH)₂
B) NH₃
C) NaOH
D) Al(OH)₃
Answer: d
Solution: An alkali is a soluble base. Al(OH)₃ is amphoteric — it acts as both an acid and a base — and is insoluble in water, so it is not classified as an alkali. Ca(OH)₂ (slightly soluble), NH₃ (forms NH₄OH in water), and NaOH are all alkalis.

Q: An example of a solid emulsion is
A) Butter
B) Hair cream
C) Milk
D) Cod-liver oil
Answer: a
Solution: Butter is a solid emulsion — it is water droplets dispersed in a solid fat matrix. Milk is a liquid emulsion (fat droplets in water). Hair cream is a semi-solid emulsion (liquid in liquid). Cod-liver oil is a pure oil, not an emulsion. Therefore butter is the correct example of a solid emulsion.

Q: n monosaccharide ⇌ (P/Q) polysaccharide + n water. In the process above, P and Q respectively represent
A) Condensation and hydrolysis
B) Fermentation and condensation
C) Polymerization and hydrolysis
D) Polymerization and condensation
Answer: a
Solution: In the forward direction (monosaccharides → polysaccharide + water), water is eliminated — this is condensation polymerization. In the reverse direction (polysaccharide + water → monosaccharides), the polymer is broken down by water — this is hydrolysis. Therefore P = condensation and Q = hydrolysis.

Q: Ethanol is soluble in water due to the presence of a
A) Carbonyl group
B) Hydroxyl group
C) Phenyl group
D) Methyl group
Answer: b
Solution: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is soluble in water because of its hydroxyl group (-OH), which forms hydrogen bonds with water molecules. The -OH group is polar and interacts strongly with the polar water molecules, allowing ethanol to mix with water in all proportions.

Q: From the diagram above, an ideal gas can be represented by
A) K
B) M
C) L
D) N
Answer: d
Solution: An ideal gas obeys Boyle's Law perfectly: PV = constant, meaning V is inversely proportional to P, giving a straight horizontal line when plotted as PV vs P. Curve N is the flat horizontal line in the diagram, representing a gas that shows no deviation from ideal behaviour across all pressures. Real gases (K, L, M) show deviations — dipping below or rising above the ideal line.

Q: The colour of litmus in an alkaline medium is
A) Red
B) Yellow
C) Pink
D) Blue
Answer: d
Solution: Litmus is a pH indicator that turns blue in alkaline (basic) solutions and red in acidic solutions. In a neutral solution, it remains purple. Therefore, in an alkaline medium, litmus turns blue.

Q: The pollutant that contributes to the depletion of the ozone layer is
A) CFCs
B) NO₂
C) SO₂
D) CO
Answer: a
Solution: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are the primary cause of ozone layer depletion. When CFCs reach the stratosphere, UV radiation breaks them down to release chlorine radicals, which catalytically destroy ozone molecules (O₃) in a chain reaction. SO₂ causes acid rain; CO is a respiratory poison; NO₂ contributes to smog.

Q: The principle of column chromatography is based on the ability of the constituents to
A) React with the solvent in the column
B) React with each other in the solvent in the column
C) Dissolve in each other in the column
D) Move at different speeds in the column
Answer: d
Solution: Column chromatography separates mixtures based on the ability of components to move at different speeds through the stationary phase. Components with greater affinity for the stationary phase move more slowly, while those preferring the mobile phase move faster, achieving separation.

Q: The arrangement of particles in crystal lattices can be studied using
A) X-rays
B) β-rays
C) α-rays
D) γ-rays
Answer: a
Solution: X-ray crystallography is the technique used to study the arrangement of particles in crystal lattices. X-rays have wavelengths comparable to the spacing between atoms in crystals, causing diffraction patterns that reveal the three-dimensional structure of the crystal.

Q: Which of the following properties is not peculiar to matter?
A) Kinetic energy of particles increases from solid to gas
B) Random motion of particles increases from gas to solid
C) Orderliness of particles increases from gas to liquid
D) Random motion of particles increases from liquid to gas
Answer: b
Solution: Random motion of particles increases from solid to gas, not from gas to solid. Gas particles have the highest kinetic energy and random motion; solid particles have the least. Option B states the opposite of what is true, making it the incorrect (not peculiar to matter) statement.

Q: The drying agent suitable for drying ammonia is
A) Calcium Chloride
B) Calcium Oxide
C) Phosphorus (V) Oxide
D) Concentrated H₂SO₄
Answer: b
Solution: Calcium oxide (CaO) is the only suitable drying agent for ammonia because it is a basic oxide that does not react with ammonia. Concentrated H₂SO₄ and P₂O₅ are acidic and react with the basic NH₃. Anhydrous CaCl₂ forms a complex with ammonia (CaCl₂·8NH₃) and cannot be used.

Q: In a neutralization reaction involving HCl and NaOH using litmus as indicator, the colour at the end point is
A) Blue
B) Red
C) Orange
D) Purple
Answer: d
Solution: At the end point of neutralization between HCl and NaOH, the solution is neutral (pH 7). Litmus turns red in acid, blue in alkali, and purple (its natural colour) in a neutral solution. Therefore the colour at the equivalence point is purple.

Q: The compound H-C(H₂)-C(H)(OH)-C(H₂)-C(HCl)(Cl) shown above — the functional groups present in the compound are
A) Alkene and halo-group
B) Hydroxyl and chloro-group
C) Alkene and chloro-group
D) Hydroxyl and halo-group
Answer: b
Solution: From the structural diagram, the compound contains an -OH (hydroxyl) group on carbon 2 and two Cl (chloro) atoms on carbon 4. There are no double bonds (C=C) present, so it is not an alkene. The two functional groups are the hydroxyl group (-OH) and the chloro-group (-Cl). Note: halo-group and chloro-group are the same here, so B and D are equivalent — B is the more specific correct answer.

Q: The monomer of nylon is
A) Hydroxybenzene
B) Hexanedioic acid
C) Benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid
D) Ethane-1,2-diol
Answer: b
Solution: Nylon-6,6 is formed by condensation polymerization of hexanedioic acid (adipic acid) and hexane-1,6-diamine. Hexanedioic acid is one of the two key monomers of nylon. Benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid and ethane-1,2-diol are monomers of Terylene (polyester).

Q: Calculate the volume in cm³ of oxygen evolved at s.t.p when a current of 5 A is passed through acidified water for 193 s. 

[F = 96500 C mol⁻¹. Molar volume of a gas at s.t.p = 22.4 dm³]
A) 0.056 dm³
B) 0.224 dm³
C) 224.000 dm³
D) 56.000 dm³
Answer: a
Solution: Charge = I × t = 5 × 193 = 965 C. Moles of electrons = 965/96500 = 0.01 mol. At the anode: 2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻, so moles of O₂ = 0.01/4 = 0.0025 mol. Volume of O₂ = 0.0025 × 22.4 = 0.056 dm³.

Q: The compounds CH₃CH₂CHO and CH₃COCH₃ can be distinguished from each other using
A) Dilute ammonia
B) Benedict's solution
C) Tollen's reagent
D) Sodium hydroxide solution
Answer: c
Solution: Tollen's reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) distinguishes aldehydes from ketones. CH₃CH₂CHO is an aldehyde and reduces Tollen's reagent to produce a silver mirror, while CH₃COCH₃ (a ketone) does not react. Benedict's solution also works with reducing sugars but Tollen's reagent is the classic test here.

Q: The enzyme used in the hydrolysis of starch to dextrin and maltose is
A) Zymase
B) Sucrase
C) Amylase
D) Lactase
Answer: c
Solution: Amylase is the enzyme responsible for the hydrolysis of starch, breaking it down first into dextrin and then into maltose. Zymase converts sugars to ethanol; sucrase hydrolyses sucrose; lactase hydrolyses lactose.

Q: Diamond cannot be used
A) In making bicycle chains
B) As abrasives
C) In cutting glass and metals
D) As dies for drawing wires
Answer: a
Solution: Diamond is the hardest natural substance, making it useful as abrasives, for cutting glass and metals, and as dies for drawing wires. However, it cannot be used in making bicycle chains — that requires malleable and ductile metals like steel. Diamond is brittle and cannot be shaped into chains.

Q: The number of electronic shells contained in an atom with electron configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶4s² is
A) 3
B) 2
C) 4
D) 5
Answer: c
Solution: The electron configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶4s² corresponds to shells n=1, n=2, n=3, and n=4. Counting the principal quantum numbers occupied: shell 1 (1s), shell 2 (2s, 2p), shell 3 (3s, 3p), and shell 4 (4s) — giving 4 electronic shells. This is Calcium (Z=20).

Q: N₂O₄(aq) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), ΔH = +ve. In the reaction above, an increase in temperature will
A) Increase the reactant production
B) Increase the value of the equilibrium constant
C) Shift the equilibrium to the left
D) Decrease the value of the equilibrium constant
Answer: b
Solution: Since ΔH is positive (endothermic), the forward reaction absorbs heat. By Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature favours the endothermic (forward) direction, shifting equilibrium to the right and producing more NO₂. This increases the equilibrium constant K, since K increases with temperature for endothermic reactions.

Q: The process that requires the use of hard water in its operation is
A) Tanning
B) Bottling
C) Laundry
D) Dyeing
Answer: a
Solution: Tanning of leather requires hard water. The calcium and magnesium ions in hard water react with tannins to help harden and preserve animal hides. Hard water is undesirable for laundry (wastes soap), bottling, and dyeing processes.

Q: The products formed when primary alkanols are oxidized using acidified potassium tetraoxomanganate (VII) are what?
A) CH₃CH₂CHO and H₂O
B) CH₃CHO and CO₂
C) CH₃CH₂COOH and H₂
D) CH₃COOH and CO₂
Answer: a
Solution: When a primary alkanol such as propan-1-ol (CH₃CH₂CH₂OH) is oxidized with acidified KMnO₄ under mild/controlled conditions, it first forms an aldehyde (CH₃CH₂CHO, propanal) and water. Further oxidation gives the carboxylic acid, but the initial oxidation product of the primary alkanol is the aldehyde.

Q: Which of the following statements is correct about the periodic table?
A) Elements in the same group have the same number of electron shells
B) The non-metallic properties of the elements tend to decrease across each period
C) Elements in the same period have the same number of valence electrons
D) The valence electrons of the elements increase progressively across the period
Answer: d
Solution: Across a period, the number of valence electrons increases progressively from left to right (e.g., Period 2: Li has 1, Be has 2, B has 3 … Ne has 8). Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons (not shells); elements in the same period have the same number of shells (not valence electrons); non-metallic properties increase across a period.

Q: The ability of carbon to form long chains is referred to as
A) Alkylation
B) Acylation
C) Carbonation
D) Catenation
Answer: d
Solution: Catenation is the unique ability of carbon atoms to bond with each other to form long chains, rings, and branched structures. This property stems from the strength and stability of the C–C bond and is the foundation of all organic chemistry.

Q: Detergents are manufactured with straight hydrocarbon chains, is to make them
A) soluble
B) biodegradable
C) cheaper
D) foamy
Answer: b
Solution: Detergents with straight (unbranched) hydrocarbon chains are biodegradable because soil bacteria can break down straight chains enzymatically. Branched-chain detergents resist bacterial degradation and cause persistent foam pollution in water bodies.

Q: The acid that is used to remove rust is
A) Hydrochloric
B) Trioxonitrate (V)
C) Tetraoxosulphate (VI)
D) Boric
Answer: b

Q: The pressure of 100cm3 of oxygen at 350C is 750mmHg. What will be the volume of the gas if the pressure is reduced to 100mmHg  without changing the temperature
A) 850cm3
B) 750cm3
C) 650cm3
D) 580cm3
Answer: b

Q: The general formula of alkanones is
A) RCHO
B) RCOR'
C) RCOOH
D) RCOOR
Answer: b
Solution: Alkanones (ketones) have the general formula RCOR', where R and R' are alkyl groups flanking the carbonyl (C=O) group. RCHO is an aldehyde; RCOOH is a carboxylic acid; RCOOR is an ester.

Q: CuO(s) + H₂(g) ⇌ Cu(s) + H₂O(g). In the equation above, the effect of increased pressure on the equilibrium position is that
A) the equilibrium is shifted to the left
B) the equilibrium is shifted to the right
C) there is no effect
D) more H₂(g) is produced
Answer: c
Solution: In this reaction, CuO and Cu are solids and do not contribute to the gas-phase equilibrium. The gaseous species are H₂(g) on the left and H₂O(g) on the right — 1 mole of gas on each side. Since the number of moles of gas is equal on both sides of the equation, a change in pressure has no effect on the equilibrium position.

Q: The metal that liberates hydrogen from cold water in bubbles only is
A) Na
B) K
C) Ca
D) Al
Answer: c

Q: 2H2(g) +    O2(g)  ⇌ 2H2O(g)    ΔH   =  - ve  What happens to the equilibrium constant of the reaction above if the temperature is increased?
A) It becomes zero
B) It decreases
C) It increases
D) It is unaffected
Answer: b

Q: Deliquenscent substances are used for
A) Cooling
B) Wetting
C) Melting
D) Drying
Answer: d

Q: Which of the following methods can be used to remove temporary hardness from water?
A) Boiling
B) Filtration
C) Sedimentation
D) Chlorination
Answer: a
Solution: Temporary hardness is caused by dissolved calcium and magnesium hydrogen carbonates (bicarbonates). Boiling decomposes these salts: Ca(HCO₃)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂. The insoluble CaCO₃ precipitates out, removing the hardness. Filtration, sedimentation, and chlorination do not remove dissolved bicarbonate salts causing temporary hardness.

Q: The chemiocal used for coagulation in water purification is
A) Aluminum tetraoxosulphate(VI)
B) Copper tetratoxosulphate (VI)
C) Sodium tetraoxosulphate(VI)
D) Calcium tetraoxosulphate (VI)
Answer: a

Q: At a given temperature and pressure, a gas X diffuses twice as fast as gas Y. It follows that
A) Gas Y is two times as heavy as Gas X
B) Gas Y is four times as heavy as Gas X
C) Gas Y is monoatomic
D) Gas X is diatomic
Answer: b
Solution: By Graham's Law of diffusion: rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass. Rate_X/Rate_Y = √(M_Y/M_X). Given Rate_X = 2 × Rate_Y: 2 = √(M_Y/M_X). Squaring both sides: 4 = M_Y/M_X. Therefore M_Y = 4 × M_X. Gas Y is four times as heavy as Gas X.

Q: Diamond cannot be used
A) In making bicycle chains
B) As abrasives
C) In cutting glass and metals
D) As dies for drawing wires
Answer: a
Solution: Diamond is the hardest natural substance, making it useful as abrasives, for cutting glass and metals, and as dies for drawing wires. However, it cannot be used in making bicycle chains — that requires malleable and ductile metals like steel. Diamond is brittle and cannot be shaped into chains.

Q: A characteristic of the alkane family is
A) Addition reaction
B) Elimination reaction
C) Substitution reaction
D) Neutralization reaction
Answer: c

Q: The refreshing and characteristic taste of soda water and other soft drinks is as a result of the presence of
A) carbon (IV) oxide
B) carbon (II) oxide
C) soda
D) glucose
Answer: a
Solution: The refreshing taste and fizz of soda water and carbonated soft drinks is due to dissolved carbon (IV) oxide (CO₂). CO₂ dissolves under pressure to form carbonic acid (H₂CO₃), giving the drink its characteristic slightly acidic, tangy taste. When the pressure is released, CO₂ escapes as bubbles.

Q: The formula for ethyl butanoate is
A) C3H7COOC2H5
B) C2H5COOC3H7
C) C4H9COOC2H5
D) C2H5COOC4H9
Answer: a

Q: Which of the following pairs of substances will react further with oxygen to form a higher oxide?
A) CO₂ and H₂O
B) NO and H₂O
C) CO and CO₂
D) SO₂ and NO
Answer: d
Solution: SO₂ can be further oxidized to SO₃ (a higher oxide): 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃. NO can be further oxidized to NO₂: 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂. CO₂ and H₂O are already fully oxidized and cannot react further with oxygen. CO can be oxidized to CO₂, but CO₂ itself cannot go higher.

Q: 3Cu  +  pHNO3  → 3Cu(NO3)2  +  4H2O  + xNO   In the equation above, the values of p and x respectively are
A) 1 and 3
B) 2 and 3
C) 6 and 2
D) 8 and 2
Answer: d

Q: Duralumin consists of aluminum, copper and?
A) Zinc and Gold
B) Lead and Manganese
C) Nickel and Silver
D) Manganese and Magnesium
Answer: d
Solution: Duralumin is an alloy composed mainly of aluminium, copper, manganese, and magnesium. It is lightweight but strong, widely used in aircraft construction. Zinc, gold, lead, nickel, and silver are not components of duralumin.

Q: Which of the following is a primary constituent of crude oil?
A) Pentane
B) Ethanol
C) Heptane
D) Methane
Answer: c
Solution: Crude oil is a complex mixture of hydrocarbons. Heptane (C₇H₁₆) is a significant and representative primary constituent of crude oil, used as a reference compound in the octane rating scale (heptane = 0 octane rating). Pentane is also present in crude oil but heptane is more commonly cited as a primary constituent. Ethanol is not a constituent of crude oil, and methane is the main component of natural gas rather than crude oil.

Q: (I) 3CuO(s) + 2NH₃(g) → 3Cu(s) + 3H₂O(l) + N₂(g)
(II) 2NH₃(g) + 3Cl₂(g) → 6HCl(g) + N₂(g)
(III) 4NH₃(g) + 3O₂(g) → 6H₂O(l) + N₂(g)
The reactions represented by the equations above demonstrate the
A) basic properties of ammonia
B) acidic properties of ammonia
C) reducing properties of ammonia
D) oxidizing properties of ammonia
Answer: c
Solution: In all three reactions, nitrogen in NH₃ is oxidized from -3 to 0 (in N₂). In reaction I, NH₃ reduces CuO to Cu. In reaction II, NH₃ reduces Cl₂ (Cl goes from 0 to -1 in HCl). In reaction III, NH₃ is oxidized by O₂. In every case, NH₃ is the reducing agent — demonstrating the reducing properties of ammonia.

Q: Which of the following statements is true about 2-methylpropane and butane?
A) They have different number of carbon atoms
B) They are members of same homologous series
C) They have the same boiling points
D) They have different chemical properties
Answer: b
Solution: 2-methylpropane and butane are structural isomers — both have the molecular formula C₄H₁₀ and belong to the alkane homologous series. They have the same number of carbon atoms and similar chemical properties, but different boiling points due to different branching.

Q: The mass number of a nucleus is?
A) Always less than its atomic number
B) The sum of the number of protons and neutrons present in the nucleus
C) Always more than the atomic weight
D) A fraction
Answer: b
Solution: The mass number (A) of an atom is defined as the total number of nucleons (protons and neutrons) in the nucleus. Mass number = number of protons + number of neutrons. It is always a whole number. The atomic number is only the number of protons, and the atomic weight is an average that may be a decimal due to isotopes.

Q: Ammonium chloride can be separated from its mixture with common salt by
A) Distillation
B) Evaporation
C) Decantation
D) Sublimation
Answer: d
Solution: NH₄Cl sublimes — it converts directly from solid to vapour on heating without melting. NaCl (common salt) does not sublime. Heating the mixture causes NH₄Cl vapour to rise and re-solidify on a cooler surface, separating it cleanly from NaCl.

Q: The droplets of water observed around a bottle of milk taken out of though refrigerator is due to the fact that the
A) Temperature of the milk drops as it loses heat into the surroundings
B) Saturated vapour pressure of the milk is equal to the atmospheric pressure
C) Water vapour in the air around loses some of its energy to the bottle
D) Water vapour in the air around the bottle gains some energy from the bottle
Answer: c

Q: The ores that can be concentrated by flotation are
A) Nitride ores
B) Chloride ores
C) Oxide ores
D) Sulphide ores
Answer: d

Q: Which of the following shows little or no net reaction when the volume of the system is decreased
A)  H2(g)  +  l2(g)  ⇌  2Hl(g)
B) 2NO2(g)  ⇌  N2O4(g)
C)  PCl5(g)   ⇌ PCl3(g)  + Cl2(g)
D)  203(g)   ⇌  3O2(g)
Answer: a

Q: Ethene reacts with hydrogen bromide to give
A) CH2Br2
B) CH3CH2Br
C) C2H2Br2
D) CHBr3
Answer: b

Q: Which steam is passed over red-hot carbon, the substances produced are
A) Hydrogen and trioxocarbonate(IV) acid
B) Hydrogen, oxygen and carbon(IV) oxide
C) Hydrogen and carbon (II) oxide
D) Hydrogen and carbon (IV) oxide
Answer: c

Q: The mass of silver deposited when a current of 10A is passed through a solution of silver salt for 4830s is    [Ag = 108, F = 96500 Cmol-1]
A) 108.0g
B) 54.0g
C) 27.0g
D) 13.5g
Answer: b

Q: Strong acids can be distinguished from weak acids by any of the following methods, EXCEPT
A) Conductivity measurement
B) The use of litmus paper
C) Measurement of pH
D) Measurement of heat of reaction
Answer: b
Solution: Litmus paper only indicates whether a solution is acidic or basic — it turns red for any acid regardless of strength. It cannot distinguish between a strong acid and a weak acid. Conductivity measurement distinguishes them because strong acids fully ionise and conduct electricity much better. pH measurement distinguishes them since strong acids have lower pH at the same concentration. Heat of neutralisation also differs between strong and weak acids.

Q: Which of the following is used to power steam engines?
A) lubricating oil
B) coal
C) bitumen
D) diesel oil
Answer: b
Solution: Coal is the fuel used to power steam engines. It is burned in the furnace of the steam engine to heat water and produce steam, which drives the pistons or turbines. Coal was the primary fuel of the Industrial Revolution and early locomotives. Lubricating oil reduces friction; bitumen is used for road surfacing; diesel powers internal combustion engines.

Q: Which of the following describes the chemical property of acids?
A) None of the above
B) Acid + XCO₃ → Salt + H₂O + NH₃
C) Acid + NaOH → Normal salt + CO₂
D) Acid + XₙCO₃ → Salt + H₂O + CO₂
Answer: d
Solution: A standard chemical property of acids is their reaction with carbonates. Acid + metal carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide. Example: 2HCl + Na₂CO₃ → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. Option B wrongly gives NH₃ as a product; Option C wrongly gives CO₂ from acid + NaOH. Answer: D.

Q: The chlorinated alkane often used industrially to remove grease is?
A) Tetrachloromethane
B) Chloromethane
C) Trichloromethane
D) Dichloromethane
Answer: a
Solution: Tetrachloromethane (CCl₄) is a non-polar solvent widely used industrially as a degreasing agent because it dissolves grease and oils effectively without itself being flammable. Its non-polarity allows it to interact with and dissolve the non-polar grease molecules through dispersion forces.

Q: The dusty and sand particles present in the air is an example of
A) a suspension
B) a dispersion
C) an emulsion
D) a saturated solution
Answer: a
Solution: Dust and sand particles in air form a suspension — solid particles dispersed in a gas that will eventually settle due to gravity. An emulsion involves liquid-in-liquid dispersion, and a saturated solution requires complete dissolution of solute.

Q: A few drops of conc HCl are added to about 10cm³ of a solution of pH 3.4. The pH of the resulting mixture is?
A) less than 3.4
B) greater than 3.4
C) unaltered
D) the same as that of the pure water
Answer: a
Solution: pH 3.4 means the solution is already acidic. Adding concentrated HCl (a strong acid) increases the concentration of H⁺ ions in the solution. A higher H⁺ concentration means a lower pH. Therefore the resulting pH will be less than 3.4.

Q: What volume of 0.5 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄ will exactly neutralize 20 cm³ of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ NaOH solution?
A) 2.0 cm³
B) 5.0 cm³
C) 6.8 cm³
D) 8.3 cm³
Answer: a
Solution: Reaction: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Moles of NaOH = 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Moles of H₂SO₄ needed = 0.002/2 = 0.001 mol. Volume of H₂SO₄ = 0.001/0.5 = 0.002 dm³ = 2.0 cm³.

Q: When ammonia and hydrogen ion bond together to form ammonium ion, the bond formed is called
A) electrovalent bond
B) compound bond
C) ionic bond
D) dative covalent bond
Answer: d
Solution: When NH₃ donates its lone pair of electrons to H⁺ to form NH₄⁺, a dative covalent (coordinate) bond is formed: NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺. In a dative bond, both electrons in the bond come from one atom (the nitrogen in NH₃). This is a special type of covalent bond — also called a coordinate bond.

Q: The heaviest isotope of hydrogen is
A) Deuterium
B) Protium
C) Tritium
D) Positron
Answer: c
Solution: Hydrogen has three naturally occurring isotopes: Protium (¹H) with mass number 1 (no neutrons), Deuterium (²H) with mass number 2 (1 neutron), and Tritium (³H) with mass number 3 (2 neutrons). Tritium is the heaviest isotope of hydrogen. Positron is not an isotope of hydrogen — it is an antiparticle of the electron.

Q: The reaction between an organic acid and an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst is known as
A) saponification
B) dehydration
C) esterification
D) hydrolysis
Answer: c
Solution: Esterification is the reaction between a carboxylic acid (organic acid) and an alcohol, catalyzed by a concentrated acid (usually H₂SO₄), to produce an ester and water: RCOOH + R'OH ⇌ RCOOR' + H₂O. Saponification is the reverse (alkaline hydrolysis of esters); dehydration removes water to form alkenes.

Q: Sulphur exists in six forms in the solid state. This property is known as
A) Isomerism
B) Allotropy
C) Isotopy
D) Isomorphism
Answer: b
Solution: Allotropy is the existence of an element in two or more different physical forms in the same state. Sulphur exists in several allotropic forms including rhombic and monoclinic sulphur. Isomerism applies to compounds, isotopy refers to atoms of the same element with different mass numbers, and isomorphism refers to similar crystal structures in different substances.
