Q: Subscription in advance is treated in the balance sheet as a
A)  current asset
B) current liability
C) fixed asset
D) long term liability
Answer: b
Solution: current assets are assets of the company that can be easily converted to cash when needed

current liability: this is the liability owned to outsiders but still enjoying its benefit within a year e.g creditors, wages in arrears

Q: What is the effect of transaction when cash is paid into the bank
A) Bank balance decrease and cash balance increase
B)  bank balance decrease and cash balance decrease
C) cash balance increase and bank balance increase
D) cash balance decrease and bank balance increase
Answer: d
Solution: Cash balance decrease and bank balance increase: The cash as leaving the cash till and will be deposited into the bank

Q: The following appears in trading account except
A) sales
B) carriage outward
C) carriage inward
D) opening stock
Answer: b
Solution: carriage outward: it is the cost of transporting goods from the company to the buyer. it is on debit side of the profit and loss account because it is an expenses incurred on distributing the goods to customer.

Q: A double entry for a transaction that offsets one amount against another on both sides of the cashbook is a
A) original entry
B)  contra entry
C)  prime entry
D)  contract entry
Answer: b
Solution: contra entry is used to offset amount or same transaction against another on both side of the cashbook

Q: The correct expression of accounting equation is
A)  Assets = Liabilities + Equity
B) Net assets = Liabilities + Equity
C) Assets + Liabilities = Equity
D) Assets = Equity - liabilities
Answer: a
Solution: The fundamental accounting equation is Asset = Capital + Liabilities
Asset = Liabilities + Equity the total assets of the company is generated through liabilities to outsiders that the company is still enjoying in addition with the equity by the owners of the business

Q: The account where the profit are distributed to the partner in their profit sharing ratio in partnership
A)  trading account
B) appropriation account
C) balance sheet
D) profit and loss account
Answer: b
Solution: Appropriation account is the account into which the net profit found in the profit and loss account of the partner will be carried down to and will be shared according to their sharing ratio

Q: Two departments A and B have the following information: Department A has Sales ₦250,000, Purchases ₦150,000, Discount received ₦24,000, and Discount allowed ₦15,000. Department B has Sales ₦500,000 and Purchases ₦250,000. Calculate the discount received in Department B.
A) ₦12,000
B) ₦40,000
C)  ₦16,000
D) ₦9,000
Answer: b
Solution: Department A’s discount‑received rate is ₦24 000 ÷ ₦150 000 = 16%. Applying this to Department B’s purchases (₦250 000) gives ₦250 000 × 16% = ₦40 000 as the discount received by Department B.

Q: An advantage of FIFO method of stock valuation is that
A) it serves-as a control during inflation
B) it is calculated at the end of the year
C)  it is progressive in nature
D) its flow of cost is in sequence with the flow of stock.
Answer: d
Solution: The major advantage of the first in first out(FIFO) method of stock valuation

1. it is very easy to apply

2. no manipulation of income is possible

3. the balance sheet amount for inventory is likely to approximate the current market value

4. its flow of cost is in sequence with the flow of stock. Since the first stock will be considered for sale before other stock. the cost is always in sequence with the flow of stock because it corresponds with the normal physical flow of goods

Q: You add the following when starting with the balance as per cash book when preparing the bank reconciliation statement except
A) Unpresented
B) Dividend
C) Uncredited cheque
D) credit transfer
Answer: c
Solution: Uncredited cheque: This have to be deducted when starting balance as per cash book

Q: What is the main purpose of transaction file?
A) To record assets and liabilities
B) To update income and expenses
C) to update master files
D)  to make organization decision
Answer: c
Solution: The main purpose of organization file is to update the master file of the organization

Q: When starting with the cash book balance in preparing the bank reconciliation statement, the followings are added
A) Unpresented cheque
B) Dividend
C)  Uncredited cheque
D) credit transfer
Answer: c
Solution: Uncredited cheque have to be less when starting with balance as per cashbook not add because the cheque are yet to be credited by the bank

Q: Which of these is the main source document for recording cash paid into bank?
A) invoice
B) cheque book
C) credit note
D) pay-in-slip
Answer: d
Solution: Pay-in-slip:this is in form of a slip designed with the name of the bank on top that has dates amounts in figure and word, column for the denomination of money paid in signature bank teller, stamp to prove the money is deposited into the bank

Q: A business has the following bank reconciliation information: Balance as per cashbook ₦5,467, Uncredited cheques ₦4,410, Unpresented cheques ₦19,404, and Cheques wrongly debited by bank ₦1,404. What is the balance as per bank statement?
A)  ₦21,901
B) ₦19,057
C)  ₦21,109
D)  ₦21,091
Answer: b
Solution: Starting from the cashbook balance of ₦5,467, we adjust for items not yet reflected in the bank statement:

Add unpresented cheques (outstanding at bank): ₦19,404

Subtract uncredited cheques (lodgements in transit): ₦4,410

Subtract cheques wrongly debited by the bank (the bank has already taken this amount): ₦1,404

So the bank statement balance is:
5,467 + 19,404 − 4,410 − 1,404 = ₦19,057

Q: The tier of government that uses financial memorandum
A) Federal government
B)  state government
C)  local government
D) municipal government
Answer: c
Solution: In Nigeria, the Financial Memorandum is the guiding document issued by the State Accountant‑General that lays down the detailed rules and procedures for budget preparation, expenditure control, accounting, and reporting at the local government level. None of the other tiers use a standalone “financial memorandum” in the same way.

Q: One of the options below have the same features as the profit and loss account in non-profit organization
A) Income and expenditure account
B)  profit and loss account
C) receipts and payment account
D) Non profit account
Answer: a
Solution: Income and expenditure : This is the type of account that operate same features as the profit and loss account it takes in consideration all arrears and prepayments

Q: A business has the following information for a trading period: Stock Jan 1 ₦2600, Purchases ₦4000, Carriage inwards ₦500, Sales ₦9000, Carriage outwards ₦500. Determine the net profit.
A)  ₦4,000
B) ₦4,500
C) . ₦5,000
D) ₦1,400
Answer: d
Solution: Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases + Carriage inwards
= ₦2,600 + ₦4,000 + ₦500
= ₦7,100

Gross profit = Sales − Cost of goods sold
= ₦9,000 − ₦7,100
= ₦1,900

Net profit = Gross profit − Carriage outwards
= ₦1,900 − ₦500
= ₦1,400.

Q: Salaries in arrears is treated in the balance sheet as a
A)  current asset
B) current liability
C) fixed asset
D) long term liability
Answer: b
Solution: Current Liability: salaries in arrears fall into the category of them under the current liability because it is benefit due to outsiders but still enjoying by the organisation and can't exceed a year

Q: The principle of double entry developed from the axioms of accounting equation is given as
A)  Assets + Liability = Equity
B) Assets + Equity = Liabilities
C) Liabilities + Equity = Asset
D) Liabilities + Equity = Net assets
Answer: c
Solution: Liabilities + Equity = Asset is given as the fundamental equation

Q: The accounting entries for goods stolen in branch will be to debit
A)  The accounting entries for goods stolen in branch will be to debit
B)  branch stock account and credit branch adjustment account
C) branch adjustment account and credit profit and loss account
D) branch adjustment account and credit branch stock account
Answer: a
Solution: A branch account is a small part of business account operating with some degree of independence . It maintains its own personal/self accounting entries to determine the profit/loss made by a specific period of time

The accounting entries is to debit profit and loss account and credit branch stock. The profit and loss is debited because the cost of the stolen goods must be charged against the profit for the period to balance the account and the branch stock account is credited because the cost of the goods is out of the branch already.

Q: In the period of rising prices, which method of stock valuation is most appropriate?
A) Last in First Out
B)  weighted average
C)  First in First Out
D) Simple average
Answer: a
Solution: Last in first out:when price rise it results to lower bet income because the leftover inventory might be extremely old and perhaps obsolete

Q: When expenses are paid on behalf of the venture, the accounting entries is to debit
A) bank account and credit joint venture account
B) expenses account and credit bank account
C)  joint venture account and credit expenses account
D) joint venture account and credit bank account
Answer: d
Solution: Joint venture account is an account that all expenditure incurred for the venture is debited and all income is credited to.
Debit joint venture and credit bank account because expenses incurred on behalf of the venture has to be debited to the joint venture account and since the money is joint out the bank must be credited to balance the account

Q: The following are the importance of branch account except
A) it enable the organization to determine the branch that is making either profit or loss
B)  it allows proper control over the branch by the head office
C) it assist the organization to determine the performance of a branch manager
D) it allows fraud and wastage of resources
Answer: d
Solution: The activities and resources of branches is strictly monitored by the head office and each branch is supplied according to its need so it will be difficult to commit fraud or waste any resources

Q: Given:
I. Settlement of debts
II. Cessation of business
III. Introduction of assets
IV. Disposal of assets
Which of these constitutes dissolution of partnership?
A) II and IV only
B)  I, II and IV only
C)  I, II and III only
D)  II, III and IV only
Answer: b
Solution: Dissolution of partnership business simply means the break up of partnership business and which are caused by many factors
II,III and IV: disposal of asset does not constitute dissolution

Q: Discount allowed is enjoyed by
A) Managers
B) Customers
C) Suppliers
D) Staff of the company
Answer: b
Solution: Customer: customers are the one that enjoys discount allowed. It is allowed to them by the suppliers. it can be in cash or trade

Q: Which of these is the subsidiary book for return inwards?
A) Sales day book
B) Sales return journal
C)  Purchases day journal
D) Cash book
Answer: b
Solution: Sales return journal otherwise called return inward book is meant for recording of all good returned by customer

Q: An evidence of payment issued to a government ministry by a revenue collector is
A) treasury receipt
B)  receipt voucher
C) payment voucher
D)  treasury card
Answer: b
Solution: Receipt voucher is raised as evidence by revenue collector when government funds and property or received

Receipt voucher: these are vouchers raised as evidence for the receipt of government funds and property. The revenue collected is prepared for the government ministry as a means that revenue has been collected

Q: In manufacturing account, depreciation of office machine is charged to
A) trading account
B) appropriation account
C) balance street
D) profit and loss account
Answer: d
Solution: profit and loss account: the depreciation of the office machine is considered as part of administrative expense which must be charged against the profit of the company

Q: The discount column on the left-hand side of cashbook represents a discount
A) received from a creditor
B) allowed to a debtor
C) received from a debtor
D) allowed to a creditor
Answer: b
Solution: Allowed to a debtor: the debit side of the cashbook is where all proceeds from sales are recorded and have to be matched with the discount allowed to the debtor /creditor

Q: Given:
I. It records subscription in arrears
II. Payments of liabilities is effected
III. The account does not show if cash payment is revenue or capital expenditure
IV. It performs the same function as cashbook
The features of receipts and payment account includes
A) I, II and IV

B) II,III and IV

C) III and IV

D) I, II and III
Answer: b
Solution: A Receipts and Payments Account:

II. Records the payment of liabilities as they’re settled in cash.

III. Does not distinguish whether cash payments are for revenue or capital items.

IV. Functions in the same way as a cashbook, summarizing all cash and bank receipts and payments.

It does not record transactions on an accrual basis (so it does not capture subscriptions in arrears), making statement I incorrect.

Q: Which of these is a content of a master file?
A) All records relevant to the organisation.
B) Records of assets of the organisation
C) A collection of data items
D)  All records relating to employees
Answer: a
Solution: All record relevant to the organization: the records which are only relevant to the organization such as the name and address as well as summary information such as amount due and year to date sales will be in master file

Q: Two departments A and B have the following information: Department A has Sales ₦250,000, Purchases ₦500,000, Discount received ₦24,000, and Discount allowed ₦15,000. Department B has Sales ₦150,000 and Purchases ₦250,000. Determine the discount allowed by Department A.
A)  ₦5,000
B) ₦9,375
C) ₦5,625
D) ₦8,000
Answer: b
Solution: Step 1: Calculate total sales

Department A sales: ₦250,000
Department B sales: ₦150,000
Total sales: ₦400,000

Step 2: Calculate Department A's proportion of total sales
Department A's proportion = ₦250,000 ÷ ₦400,000 = 62.5%
Step 3: Allocate total discount allowed proportionally
Total discount allowed = ₦15,000 (given for the business)
Department A's discount allowed = ₦15,000 × 62.5% = ₦9,375
Department A's discount allowed is ₦9,375, representing their proportional share based on sales volume.

Q: The use of a three column cash book is determined by
A) cash discount
B) trade discount
C) cash transaction
D) Bank transaction
Answer: a
Solution: A cash discount is a deduction allowed by the seller of goods or by the provider of services in order to motivate the customer to pay within a specified time

Q: Goodwill can be created in the books of a partnership firm when
A) the partnership experiences super profit
B)  a new member is admitted
C) the business is being expanded
D)  the business suffers high loss
Answer: a
Solution: The partnership experiences super profit: super profit is the profit that is generated by intangible asset or the profit that is attributed by the tangible asset when such profit is capitalized we get intangible asset or goodwill

Q: A business acquisition shows the following assets and liabilities: Plant and Machinery ₦190,000, Motor Vehicle ₦170,000, Stock ₦60,000, Current Liabilities ₦50,000, Purchase consideration ₦400,000. Determine the amount of goodwill.
A) ₦110 000
B)  ₦80 000
C)  ₦90 000
D)  ₦30 000
Answer: d
Solution: Net assets acquired = (₦190,000 + ₦170,000 + ₦60,000) – ₦50,000 = ₦420,000 – ₦50,000 = ₦370,000
Goodwill = Purchase consideration – Net assets = ₦400,000 – ₦370,000 = ₦30,000.

Q: A company's inventory records show the following information for the year: Opening stock on January 1st was ₦2,000, purchases during the year totaled ₦4,000, carriage inwards was ₦500, sales amounted to ₦9,000, and carriage outwards was ₦500. Based on this information, what is the value of the Gross profit?
A) ₦9,000
B)  ₦2,500
C) ₦3,000
D) ₦1,500
Answer: b
Solution: 
COGS = 2,000 + 4,000 + 500 = ₦6,500

Gross Profit = Sales − COGS = 9,000 − 6,500 = ₦2,500

Q: Which of these accounts is dissolution expenses credited?
A) partners capital account
B) revaluation account
C) partners current account
D) Realization account
Answer: d
Solution: Realization account: the cash realized from sales of asset is credited to it

Q: one of the options below is not the source of income for non- profit organization
A) Entrance fees
B) subscription/dues
C) odrinary shares
D) Donations
Answer: c
Solution: Ordinary shares: This type of source of income is only used in profit oriented organization to generate fund the pubic so as to enable the organization make more profit at the end of a specified period

Q: The current growth in the volume of trading and financial dealing in Nigeria is helped by
A) increased financial activities
B) government intervention
C)  credit as a factor in business
D) Payment for goods in cashc
Answer: c
Solution: The availability of credit allows businesses and consumers to purchase goods and services beyond their immediate cash resources, thereby increasing the volume of transactions and financial dealings. While cash payments, government intervention, and broader financial activities all play roles in the economy, it is the extension of credit that most directly fuels higher trading volumes by enabling deferred payments and greater purchasing power.

Q: Which type of cashbook entry involves recording the same amount on both the debit and credit sides to offset each other?
A) Contra entry
B) Compound entry
C) Transfer entry
D) Journal entry
Answer: a
Solution: A contra entry in the cashbook is used when the business moves money between its own cash and bank accounts—such as depositing cash into the bank or withdrawing cash from the bank

Q: Given:
I. Cash refunds
II. Debit note issued
III. Dishonored cheque
IV. Purchases
The item on the credit side of purchases ledger control account includes
A)  I, II and III only
B)  I and II only
C) III and IV only
D) I, III and IV only
Answer: c
Solution: The credit side of the Purchases Ledger Control Account shows items that increase the amount you owe to suppliers. These are:

III. Dishonoured cheque, because a bounced cheque reverses a payment and increases your outstanding balance.

IV. Purchases, as credit purchases directly raise your payables.

Cash refunds (I) and debit notes issued (II) reduce what you owe and therefore appear on the debit side.

papers.sourceText: Q: In a system of incomplete records, the opening capital is determined by preparing A) statement of affairs B) balance sheet C) cash book D) trial balance. Answer: a Q: Use the information below to answer questions 19 and 20 Purchases ledger opening balance ₦4,000 Sales ledger opening balance ₦6,000 Credit purchases during the year ₦25,000 Discounts allowed ₦1,000 Returns inwards ₦2,000 Credit sales during the year ₦10,000 Returns outwards ₦6,000 What is the purchases ledger balance? A) ₦4,000 B) ₦23,000 C) ₦24,000 D) ₦29,000 Answer: b Solution: Purchases Ledger (Creditors) Balance: Closing balance = Opening balance + Credit purchases − Returns outwards = 4,000 + 25,000 − 6,000 = ₦23,000 Q: In an incomplete record system a trading account cannot be prepared until the? A) day book has been balanced B) amount of personal drawings has been established C) cash book has been balanced D) amount os sales and purchases has been established Answer: d Solution: Reason: a trading account needs total sales and cost of goods sold (which depends on purchases, opening and closing stock). In an incomplete records system you must first determine the totals for sales and purchases before you can prepare the trading account. Q: Prime cost is A) Direct cost of production B) Cost of raw materials consume: C) Cost of raw materials purchase-: D) Indirect cost of production Answer: a Q: Transactions are recorded or posted to the ledger in line with A) Accounting Concept B) Source document C) Double Entry Principle D) Data collection Answer: c Solution: The main principle of double-entry system is that for every debit there is a corresponding credit for an equal amount of money and for every credit there is a corresponding debit for an equal amount of money; i.e. for every transaction one account is debited for, the amount of transaction and the other account is also credited. Q: If goods are invoiced to the branch at cost and the in-voice par value is ₦2,000 with 5% discount rate, cash remitted to the head office is A) ₦2,100 B) ₦2,000 C) ₦1,900 D) ₦100 Answer: c Solution: Invoice price = ₦2,000 Discount rate = 5% Discount amount: ₦2,000 × 5% = ₦100 Cash remitted to the head office: Invoice price − Discount = ₦2,000 − ₦100 = ₦1,900 Q: The concise statement used to explain entries in the general journal is known as? A) narration B) summary C) information D) commentary Answer: a Solution: Reason: In accounting, a narration is the brief explanation written below a journal entry to describe the transaction. Q: In a bank reconciliation statement, Dishonoured cheques is added to A) unpresented cheques B) uncredited cheques C) statement of account D) aggregate balanace as per cash book Answer: b Solution: Dishonoured cheques are those which are refused payment by the bank because they are not in order or there is insufficient fund in the drawer's account. They are added to uncredited cheques just like standing order and bank charges. Q: Administrative, selling and distribution expenses in a manufacturing firm are recorded in A) Trading Account. B) Manufacturing Account. C) Profit and Loss Account. D) Balance Sheet. Answer: c Q: Asa Company bought a vehicle worth ₦20,000 and the vehicle is to be depreciated at 5%. Using the reducing balance method of depreciation, what would be the value of the asset after 3 years? A) ₦19,000.00 B) ₦18,050.50 C) ₦17,147.50 D) 16,290.13 Answer: c Solution: To find the value of the asset after 3 years using the reducing balance method, Apply the 5% depreciation rate to the remaining balance each year. Given information: Original cost: ₦20,000 Depreciation rate: 5% per annum Method: Reducing balance Period: 3 years Year-by-year calculation: Year 1: Depreciation = ₦20,000 × 5% = ₦1,000 Book value = ₦20,000 - ₦1,000 = ₦19,000 Year 2: Depreciation = ₦19,000 × 5% = ₦950 Book value = ₦19,000 - ₦950 = ₦18,050 Year 3: Depreciation = ₦18,050 × 5% = ₦902.50 Book value = ₦18,050 - ₦902.50 = ₦17,147.50 Alternative formula method: Book value = Original cost × (1 - depreciation rate)^number of years Book value = ₦20,000 × (1 - 0.05)³ Book value = ₦20,000 × (0.95)³ Book value = ₦20,000 × 0.857375 Book value = ₦17,147.50 Q: five hundred naria monthly is allowed on an imprest system. The following transactions took place. Period1: Cash advanced to petty cashier......₦500 Petty cashier paid out: stamp.......₦200 ₦ewspaper...........................₦250 Period 2: Cash to petty cashier...............₦450 Cashier paid for writing materials..₦350 What was the balance of cash with the petty cashier at the end of period 1? A) ₦50 B) ₦200 C) ₦300 D) ₦450 Answer: a Solution: From Period 1: Cash given = ₦500 Payments = ₦200 (stamp) + ₦250 (newspaper) = ₦450 Remaining cash = ₦500 − ₦450 = ₦50 Q: Money set aside for the saving of business overheads is referred to A) Capital Expenditure B) Revenue Expenditure C) Revenue receipts D) Answer: c Q: Processed data is only useful to user if it is A) complex B) quantitative C) relevant D) qualitative Answer: c Solution: first thing to be considered when gathering data is the relevant and usefulness of the data or information before considering the qualitative aspect and other things Relevant : even if the information of data is not processed, if the processed data is relevant, it will be useful to the user Q: The amount of a company’s profit given to a shareholder is known as A) premium B) dividend C) interest D) allotment Answer: b Q: A dividend of 10% in a company on 500 000 ordinary shares of ₦ 1 nominal value has been declared, How much will a shareholder receive if he has 200 shares? A) ₦ 500 000 B) ₦ 50 000 C) ₦200 D) ₦ 20 Answer: d Solution: Let's calculate the dividend for a shareholder with 200 shares: Dividend rate: 10% of the nominal value (₦1 per share) Dividend per share: 10% × ₦1 = ₦0.10 per share Total dividend for 200 shares: 200 × ₦0.10 =₦20 Q: Which of these is not a subsidiary books? A) sales day book B) purchase day book C) credit note D) return inward day book Answer: c Solution: The subsidiary book is a book of original entr or prime entry which consists of: purchases day book, sales day book, returns inwards day book, returns outward day book, cash book, journal, petty cash book. Q: Mini Enterprises Sales Ledger as at 31/12/94 read: ₦ Balance b/f 12750 Total credit sales 28185 Payments by debtors 12112 Discount allowed 638 Sales returns 1500 Prepare the sales ledger control account and determine the balance due from debtors. A) ₦40,935 B) ₦27,961 C) ₦26,685 D) ₦1,185 Answer: c Solution: Opening Debtors: ₦12 750 Add Credit Sales: ₦28 185 Less: Payments ₦12 112, Discounts ₦638, Returns ₦1 500 (total ₦14 250) Closing Debtors: ₦12 750 + ₦28 185 − ₦14 250 = ₦26 685 Q: Which of the following is not a book of original entry? A) Cash Book B) Purchases Ledger C) Returns Outwards Journal D) General Journal Answer: b Q: The three-column cash book differs from the two-column cash book in A) Cash column, B) Discount column C) Bank column, D) Folio column Answer: a Solution: The three-column cash book differs from the two-column cash book by having an additional discount column. Q: The beginning and ending accounts receivable balances were ₦20,000 and ₦30,000 respectively. The collection from customers during the period was ₦70,000. What was the total sale on account? A) ₦20,000 B) ₦60,000 C) ₦80,000 D) ₦120,000 Answer: c Solution: We can calculate total sales on account using the accounts receivable equation: Beginning A/R + Credit Sales − Collections = Ending A/R Substitute values: 20,000 + Credit Sales − 70,000 = 30,000 Credit Sales − 50,000 = 30,000 Credit Sales = 80,000 Q: Adex Ltd. issues stock to its retail branches at cost price. The following particulars relate to Ede branch: Stock at branch 1st January at cost ₦400, Goods sent to branch at cost ₦8000, Returns to head office ₦340, Cash sales ₦9160, Stock at branch 31st December at cost ₦720. Use the information to answer the question. calculate the gross profit A) ₦1870 B) ₦1530 C) ₦1640 D) ₦1820 Answer: d Solution: Gross Profit = Sales - Cost of Goods Sold….. Cost of Goods Sold = Opening Stock + Goods Sent - Returns - Closing Stock = ₦400 + ₦8,000 - ₦340 - ₦720 = ₦7,340…. Gross Profit = Sales - Cost of Goods Sold = ₦9,160 - ₦7,340 = ₦1,820 The branch made a gross profit of ₦1,820 for the period. Q: The chief accounting officer of the Federation is A) Auditor General B) Minister of Economic Planning C) Chief Accountant D) Accountant General Answer: d Solution: The Accountant General of the Federation is the head of the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation (OAGF), which is the treasury of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. They are responsible for overseeing the government's receipts and payments, ensuring proper accounting practices, and managing the Federation Account. Q: The law that currently regulates the registration of companies in Nigeria is the? A) Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 B) Nigeria Enterprises Promotion Decree, 1972 C) Companies and Allied Matters Decree, 1990 D) Companies Decree, 1968 Answer: c Solution: The law currently governing company registration in Nigeria is the Companies and Allied Matters Decree, 1990 (now the Companies and Allied Matters Act, CAMA). Q: Shares issued free of charge to existing shareholders based on their previous holdings is __ issue A) accrued B) premium C) floating D) bonus Answer: d Solution: A bonus issue is a way for a company to reward existing shareholders by distributing additional shares to them at no cost. The number of bonus shares received by each shareholder is typically proportional to their existing shareholding. Q: Use the information below to answer questions 11 and 12. The initial imprest as at July 1st was ₦500. Petty cash voucers with the custodian by July 15th added up to ₦394. An IOU slip received from a co-worker was ₦65 and there was a shorage of ₦5 cash. The co-worker made refund on July 18th just before the imprest was replenished. The amount required to replenish the payments made from the imprest was? A) ₦399 B) ₦394 C) ₦358 D) ₦101 Answer: a Solution: To find the amount required to replenish the imprest, determine what actual payments were made from the fund. Given information: Initial imprest: ₦500 Petty cash vouchers: ₦394 IOU from co-worker: ₦65 Cash shortage: ₦5 Co-worker made refund on July 18th (before replenishment) Analysis: The amount needed to replenish the imprest equals the actual payments made from the fund. Actual payments made: Petty cash vouchers represent legitimate business expenses: ₦394 Cash shortage represents money that's missing/lost: ₦5 IOU is NOT a payment - it's money lent to co-worker (and was refunded before replenishment) Total amount to replenish: ₦394 + ₦5 = ₦399 Since the co-worker refunded the ₦65 before replenishment, this doesn't need to be included in the replenishment amount. Q: book that contains individual accounts of suppliers is the A) purchases ledger B) general ledger C) nominal ledger D) sales ledger Answer: a Q: Which of the following is recorded on the debit side of the Trial Balance? A) Bank overdraft B) Returns outwards C) Purchases D) Capital Answer: c Q: Share premium can be used to? i. write off discount on shares ii. give loans to directors iii.pay dividends iv. pay company's formation expenses. A) i and iv only B) i and iii only C) ii and iii only D) iii and iv only Answer: a Solution: According to company law, the share premium account is treated as a capital reserve and can only be used for specific purposes, such as: Writing off discount on shares (i) Paying the company's formation (preliminary) expenses (iv) Issuing fully paid bonus shares Q: The balance of profit and loss account will be A) N 4,000 B) N 2,800 C) N 1,500 D) N 300 Answer: a Q: A company's inventory records show the following information for the year: Opening stock on January 1st was ₦2,000, purchases during the year totaled ₦4,000, carriage inwards was ₦500, sales amounted to ₦9,000, and carriage outwards was ₦500. Based on this information, what is the value of the Gross profit? A) ₦9,000 B) ₦2,500 C) ₦3,000 D) ₦1,500 Answer: b Solution: COGS = 2,000 + 4,000 + 500 = ₦6,500 Gross Profit = Sales − COGS = 9,000 − 6,500 = ₦2,500 Q: In analyzing incomplete records, which of the following should be investigated? A) The generalledger. B) The purchases daybook and sales day book C) The nature trading activities and the basis on which goods are sold. D) The asset register together with the depreciation schedule Answer: c Solution: When analyzing incomplete records (single-entry bookkeeping or missing information), understanding how the business operates and the basis on which goods are sold is crucial. This helps estimate missing figures such as sales, purchases, and gross profit. Q: What is the net working capital? A) N 2,600 B) N1,800 C) N 800 D) N 600 Answer: c Q: What is Kunle’s share of the profit? A) N 600 B) N 300 C) N180 D) N 120 Answer: d Q: Ojo, Sam and Ade are in partnership sharing profit in the ratio 4:3:1 respectively. From their books for the year ended, interest on drawings and capital is allowed at 5% respectively, and profit for the year amounted to ₦4,950. What is Ojo's share of profit? A) ₦7,000 B) ₦2,475 C) ₦3,000 D) ₦991.8 Answer: b Solution: To find Ojo's share of profit: The profit sharing ratio is 4:3:1 (Ojo : Sam : Ade) Total ratio = 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 parts Ojo's share = (4/8) × Total Profit Ojo's share = (4/8) × ₦4,950 Ojo's share = (1/2) × ₦4,950 Ojo's share = ₦2,475 Therefore, Ojo's share of profit is ₦2,475. Q: Books of account consists of A) ledgers and subsidiary books B) ledgers and principal books C) folios and subsidiary books D) ledgers and cash book. Answer: a Q: I.Profits and losses will be shared unequally II. Interest is not allowed on capital, III. Salaries are not allowed. IV. Interest is charged on drawings. Which of the following would apply where there is no agreement during partnership formation? A) I only B) I, II and III C) I, II and IV D) II and III. Answer: c Q: The receipt of cash from a customer who bought goods with ₦800 list price, 25% trade discount and 2/10, n/30 terms would, if paid within the discount period, amount to A) ₦576 B) ₦588 C) ₦600 D) ₦600 Answer: b Solution: Net after trade discount: ₦800 × (1−0.25) = ₦600 Then 2% cash discount on ₦600: ₦600 × 0.02 = ₦12 Amount paid = ₦600 − ₦12 = ₦588 Q: In Manufacturing Account, prime cost plus factory overhead is known as A) conversion cost B) cost of raw materials consumed C) total cost D) production cost Answer: d Q: Which of the following items is not treated in the Profit and Loss Account? A) Office expenses B) Salaries and allowances C) Carriage inwards D) Discounts allowed Answer: c Q: Rent accrued in 2009 was D140. In 2010, D900 was paid while D160 was outstanding. Rent for 2010 was A) D1,200. B) D1.060. C) D920. D) D880. Answer: c

Q: Which of the following is not an inventory costing method?
A) FIFO
B) LIFO
C) Average cost method
D) LILA
Answer: d
Solution: FIFO (First-In, First-Out), LIFO (Last-In, First-Out), and the Average Cost Method are all standard inventory valuation methods.

LILA is not a recognized inventory costing method.

Q: In the head office ledger, the value of goods sent to the branch are____________
A) Debited to the branch current account
B) Debited to the head office current account
C) Credited to the head office current account
D) Credited to the branch current account
Answer: b
Solution: Branch current account is maintained in the head office books to record all transactions between the head office and the branch. This account is debited with the following:

  i. Goods sent to branch

  ii. Expenses of the branch paid by the head office

  iii. Profit of the branch

Q: If the purchase price exceeds the net assets of a company, the excess amount is debited to________________

A) Cash account
B)  purchase account
C) goodwill account
D) sales account
Answer: c
Solution: Goodwill is the excess of purchase consideration over the total value of the business

Q: Which of the following methods of invoicing goods to branches facilitate easy checks on the activities of branches?
A) Selling price
B) Fixed percentage on cost
C) Cost price
D) Invoice price
Answer: c
Solution: Goods are transferred from head office to branch at cost price, selling price and cost price plus mark up

Q: Using the following information, calculate the balance that should appear on the bank statement. The cashbook shows a balance of ₦13,560. There are unpresented cheques totaling ₦5,120, and a cheque for ₦2,300 has been paid into the bank but not yet credited. The bank has also received a dividend of ₦2,000, charged ₦280 in bank fees, and processed a standing order of ₦600.
A) ₦10,740
B) ₦11,860
C)  ₦16,380
D) ₦17,500
Answer: d
Solution: Balance per bank statement = ₦13,560 + ₦5,120 + ₦2,000 – ₦2,300 – ₦280 – ₦600 = ₦17,500.

Q: A Trading account for the year ended 31st December 2009 shows the following information:
Opening Stock: ₦32,000
Purchases: ₦40,000
Carriage inwards: ₦1,000
Less Returns: ₦2,000
Sales: ₦48,000
Less Returns: ₦2,000
Closing Stock: ₦9,000
Calculate:

What is the cost of goods available for sale?

A)  ₦20,500
B) ₦71,000
C)  ₦28,000
D) ₦27,000
Answer: b
Solution: Calculate Cost of Goods Available
Cost of Goods Available = Opening Stock + Net Purchases + Carriage Inwards
= ₦32,000 + ₦39,000 + ₦1,000 = ₦71,000

Q: To account for expenses paid by head office on behalf of the branch, the branch should___________
A) Debit profit and loss account and credit head office account
B) Debit head office account and credit cash
C) Credit cash and debit profit and loss account
D)  Credit profit and loss account and debit head office account
Answer: a
Solution: The head office maintains a book, (branch account) more or less like other personal accounts, so that any expenses incurred on behalf of the branch will also be debited to the branch account. Similarly, in the branch books, there will be head office accounts

Q: Gross profit in the branch adjustment account is transferred to the branch____________
A) Income and expenditure account
B) profit and loss account
C) receipt and payment account
D) trading account
Answer: d
Solution: In branch accounting, the Branch Adjustment Account is used to record inter‐branch adjustments such as stock transfers and branch expenses. Any gross profit worked out in this account is then transferred to the Branch Trading Account, where it becomes part of the overall trading results for that branch.

Q: In reconciling the branch and head office accounts, remittance in transit in the branch books is treated as a_____________
A) Debit entry
B)  Contra entry
C) . Credit entry
D) Reversal entry
Answer: a
Solution: In the branch’s own books, when cash is sent to head office but not yet received there, it isn’t left in the cash balance, instead the branch debits a “Remittance in Transit” asset account and credits cash. Thus, on reconciliation, the branch treats remittances in transit as debit entries.

Q: A partnership’s internal regulation are set out by________
A)  A constitution
B) A law
C) A deed
D) . An article
Answer: c
Solution: A partnership deed is a written agreement among the partners specifying rules and regulations and is signed by all the partners and stamped as per stamp act with an aim to prevent possible disputes and disagreements among the partners at future dates

Q: Use the information to answer the questions

  Rakiya and joy are in a partnership and agreed that 5% interest per annum is to be charged on drawings. The drawing made by both partners in one year were:

  Rakiya, ₦200 on March 31 and ₦300 on September 30.

  Joy, ₦100 on April 1 and ₦240 on July 1.

  The interest on Joy’s drawing is___________
A) ₦11.25
B) ₦500.00
C) ₦9.75.
D) ₦340.00
Answer: c
Solution: The interest on Joy’s drawings is ₦9.75, calculated as follows:

₦100 drawn on April 1 for 9 months:
₦100 × 5% × 9/12 = ₦3.75

₦240 drawn on July 1 for 6 months:
₦240 × 5% × 6/12 = ₦6.00

Total interest = ₦3.75 + ₦6.00 = ₦9.75.

Q: What act generally includes completing unfinished partnership business, collecting and paying debts, collecting partnership assets to be turned into cash and taking inventory?
A) Formation
B) dissolution
C)  winding up
D)  termination
Answer: b
Solution: It is the first step in termination process

Q: Why should a new partner contribute towards goodwill on his admission?
A) It is a norm
B) to ensure new partner also have a stake in the business
C) the firm into which he is entering already has some goodwill in the market
D) to purchase the business
Answer: c
Solution: Goodwill is being paid by a new partner because the partnership he is entering into already has goodwill in the market as well as to pay for the portion sacrificed by existing partners in form to their profit to admit the new partner.

Q: The amount called in respect of a share but not paid before or on the date fixed for payment is referred to as:
A) Call in advance
B) call in arrears
C) forfeiture
D) shares
Answer: b
Solution: the amount called by the company which is not paid by the shareholders before the due date fixed for payment

 

Q: Using the following:

Balance as par overdraft of the cashbook is ₦4000 ,uncredited cheque is ₦2300, bank charges ₦300, unpresented cheque ₦5000.

  what is the adjusted cashbook balance?
A) ₦4000
B) 3₦00
C) ₦4300
D) ₦5000
Answer: c
Solution: Adjusted cashbook balance=–₦4000–₦300=–₦4300

Q: In departmental accounting, which is not a transfer pricing_________
A) cost based transfer price
B) market based transfer pricing
C) Dual pricing system
D) peak pricing
Answer: d
Solution: The standard transfer‐pricing methods used in departmental accounting are:

Cost‐based transfer pricing (using internal cost as the basis)

Market‐based transfer pricing (using external market prices)

Dual pricing system (charging one price to the selling division and another to the buying division)

Peak pricing, on the other hand, is a demand‐management strategy for external customers (adjusting prices during high‐demand “peak” periods) and is not used for inter‐departmental transfer pricin

Q: Profit or loss in a partnership is usually arrived at after deducting from gross profit all expenses including____________
A)  Partners salaries
B) Interest on capital
C)  Interest on loans
D) Partners drawings
Answer: c
Solution: is charged in the profit and loss account as finance expenses

Q: A partnership deed is used to____________
A) Promote mutual understanding
B) Enhance mistrust
C) Encourage discrepancy
D) Control funds
Answer: a
Solution: Partnership deed can be used to:

  i. Indicates terms on which the business corporation us founded

  ii. To form a partnership for the purpose of doing business together

  iii. Prevent future disputes

  iv. Promote mutual understanding

  v. Avoid mistrust

Q: Transfers from the head office to branches are best carried out at__________
A) Cost price
B) Cost plus mark up
C) Selling price
D) Market price
Answer: b
Solution: Goods are transferred from head office to branch at cost price, selling price and cost price plus mark up

Q: Advertising expenses incurred on a product in a business organization should be charged to
A) Sales department
B) Production department
C)  Purchase department
D) Administration department
Answer: a
Solution: Advertising expenses are expenses incurred in order to enhance the sales of the company’s product/services

Q: Tea and Cup are into a partnership business. Interests on drawings made by partners are at 10% per annum. Tea’s capital is ₦70000 and current balance is ₦50000. He withdrew the following amounts during the year : 3000 on 31st January ,2000 on 31st March, 4000 on 1st July, 1500 on the 30th September, 2500 on 1st November. Cup’s capital is ₦100000 and current balance is ₦40000. He made no drawings during the period. What is the interest on the drawings of Tea?
A)  ₦705
B) ₦500
C) ₦1000
D) ₦10000
Answer: a
Solution: Interest on Tea’s drawings is calculated as the sum of each drawing × 10% × (months outstanding ÷ 12):

₦3 000 on 31 Jan: 3 000 × 10% × (11/12) = ₦275.00

₦2 000 on 31 Mar: 2 000 × 10% × (9/12) = ₦150.00

₦4 000 on 1 Jul: 4 000 × 10% × (6/12) = ₦200.00

₦1 500 on 30 Sep: 1 500 × 10% × (3/12) = ₦37.50

₦2 500 on 1 Nov: 2 500 × 10% × (2/12) = ₦41.67

Total interest = ₦275 + ₦150 + ₦200 + ₦37.50 + ₦41.67 = ₦704.17  ≈ ₦705..

Q: Which of the following is a common cause of a discrepancy between head office and branch trial office________
A) Stock and repayment
B) Creditors and cash in trans
C) Stock and cash in transit
D) Debtors and cash in transit
Answer: c
Solution: Goods in transit are goods sent by the head office to branch but by the close of financial year, these goods have not yet reached the branch.

 Cash in transit are cash remitted by the branch to head office by the end of the financial year this cash has not yet reached the head office

Another major cause of discrepancy is returns in transit. This is the returns by the branch to head office but by the end of the year, they have not been received by the head office

Q: During the period, Department P opened with stock of ₦2 000, made purchases of ₦2 500 and recorded sales of ₦6 000. Its closing stock was ₦1 500. Department P also received goods costing ₦300 transferred in from Department Q and incurred operating expenses of ₦200. What was Department P’s net profit for the period?
A)  ₦2,500
B) ₦2,800
C) ₦3,000
D) ₦5,200
Answer: a
Solution: Net profit for Department P = Sales ₦6 000 – Cost of Goods Sold [(₂₀₀₀ + ₦2 500 + ₦300 – ₦1 500) = ₦3 300] – Expenses ₦200 = ₦2 500.

Q: The rent expense for Trendy store is ₦3500. Trendy store has three departments; jewelry, hair dressing, and clothing. The floor spaces occupied by the departments are 3:2:5 respectively. What is the rent allocated to clothing department?
A) ₦700
B) ₦1050
C)  ₦1750
D) ₦3500
Answer: c
Solution: Jewelry 3/10 x 3500 = 1050

Hairdressing 2/10 x 3500 = 700

Clothing 5/10 x 3500 = 1750

Q: Calls in advance are treated in the balance sheet as_______
A) Current asset
B) Fixed asset
C) Current liability
D) Fixed liability
Answer: c
Solution: calls in advance is treated as a current liability until the calls are made and the amount actually becomes payable by the shareholders

Q: When goodwill is not retained in the business, the entries in the new partners books will be to debit______________

A) Goodwill account and credit partners capital account
B) Cash account and credit goodwill account
C) Goodwill account and credit cash account
D)  Partners capital account and credit goodwill account
Answer: d
Solution: When goodwill is not retained in the business, it means the goodwill account is written off immediately after being created. This involves a two-step process:
Step 1: Create goodwill

Debit: Goodwill Account
Credit: Partners' Capital Accounts (in profit-sharing ratio)

Step 2: Write off goodwill (since it's not retained)

Debit: Partners' Capital Accounts (in new profit-sharing ratio)
Credit: Goodwill Account

The net effect in the new partners' books is:

Debit: Partners' Capital Account
Credit: Goodwill Account

This represents the partners absorbing the goodwill write-off through their capital accounts rather than keeping it as an asset on the books.

Q: Which of the following should not be adjusted for in the profit and loss account?
A) Accruals
B) inventory
C) subscription
D) depreciation
Answer: c
Solution: is adjusted for in the income and expenditure account

Q: Tea and Cup are into a partnership business. Interests on drawings made by partners are at 10% per annum. Tea’s capital is ₦70000 and current balance is ₦50000. He withdrew the following amounts during the year : 3000 on 31st January , 2000 on 31st March, 4000 on 1st July, 1500 on the 30th September, 2500 on 1st November. Cup’s capital is ₦100000 and current balance is ₦40000. He made no drawings during the period. what is the closing balance in Tea’s current account
A) 36,925Cr
B)  40,000Cr
C) 50,000Dr
D)  36,295Dr
Answer: d
Solution: Starting with Tea’s opening credit balance of ₦50 000, we subtract his total drawings (₦3 000 + 2 000 + 4 000 + 1 500 + 2 500 = ₦13 000) and the interest on those drawings (₦3 000×10%×11/12 + ₦2 000×10%×9/12 + ₦4 000×10%×6/12 + ₦1 500×10%×3/12 + ₦2 500×10%×2/12 ≈ ₦705), giving:

Closing current balance = ₦50000 − ₦13000 − ₦705 = ₦36295

Q: Ade, Tony, Rose share profit and losses in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 1 respectively. Ade retires and the remaining partners decide to take Ade’s share in the existing ratio. What is the new ratio?

A) 1 : 1
B) 3 : 6
C) 2 : 1
D) 2 : 6
Answer: c
Solution: When Ade’s 3‑part share is divided between Tony and Rose in their 2 : 1 ratio, Tony receives 3 × (2/3) = 2 parts and Rose receives 3 × (1/3) = 1 part, so Tony’s total becomes 2 + 2 = 4 and Rose’s becomes 1 + 1 = 2, giving a new ratio of 4 : 2 (i.e. 2 : 1).

Q: Branch stock adjustment account is prepared at?
A) Cost price
B)  new price
C) invoice price
D) normal price
Answer: c
Solution: Branch stock adjustment account deals with the loading on the respective items of goods relating to Branch stock account.

Branch adjustment account is prepared at invoice price.

 The difference between the two sides of this account reveals either gross profit (if credit side is greater than the debit side) or gross loss (if debit side is greater than the credit side).

Q: Why are adjustments in the profit and loss account necessary?
A) To cover some expenses of the following year
B) To show the provisions made during the year
C) To show the total expenses paid and income received during the year
D) To ascertain the actual expenses incurred and income earned during the year
Answer: d
Solution: Fundamental principle of preparing P&L account is that expenses and income relating to only the trading period are taken to the trading profit and loss account.

Q: A business has the following balance sheet as at the beginning of the year: Capital ₦40,000, Furnishing ₦10,000, Ceiling Fan ₦1,500, and Cash in Hand ₦28,500, with total assets and liabilities both equaling ₦40,000.
During the year ending 31/1/95, the following transactions occurred:

Rent for shop ₦12,000 paid for the year
Total purchases ₦15,000
Total sales ₦8,200
Stock of goods left ₦10,000
Paid sales boy ₦500

What is the new balance sheet total as at 31/1/95?
A)  ₦39,700
B)  ₦40,000
C)  ₦41,500
D) ₦48,500
Answer: a
Solution: Starting with opening cash of ₦28,500, we track cash movements:
Cash Outflows:

Rent paid: ₦12,000
Purchases: ₦15,000
Sales boy wages: ₦500
Total outflows: ₦27,500

Cash Inflows:

Sales: ₦8,200

New Cash Balance: ₦28,500 - ₦27,500 + ₦8,200 = ₦9,200
New Balance Sheet:

Assets: Furnishing ₦10,000 + Ceiling Fan ₦1,500 + Stock ₦10,000 + Cash ₦9,200 = ₦30,700
Capital: ₦40,000 - ₦300 (net loss) = ₦39,700
Prepaid Rent: ₦9,000 (11 months remaining)

New Balance Sheet Total: ₦39,700

Q: In the absence of a partnership deed, the act stipulates that____________
A) An amount should be fixed as salaries for partners
B) Profits and losses should not be shared equally
C) Interest on partner’s loan should be 25%
D) Interest should not be allowed on partners drawings
Answer: d
Solution: Under the Partnership Act, the following rules will be applied in the absence of an agreement among partners:

  i. Profit or losses of the firm will be shared equally by the partners

  ii. Interest on capital will not be allowed to any partner.

  iii. No interest will be charged on drawings

  iv. Interest on loan will be 6% on the loan

  v. No salary or remuneration will be allowed to any of the partners

  vi. Every partner must take part in the management of the partnership business

  vii. The partnership books are kept at the place of business of the partnership and every partner may have access to and inspect and copy any of them.

Q: Cost of rent as an expense can be apportioned to all department on the basis of:
A) No of employees
B) stock value
C) space occupied
D) wages
Answer: c
Solution: Indirect expenses are allocated among departments in order to ascertain the profits or loss made by each department

Q: When goods are sent to branch at cost plus mark up, it means that the branch should sell at_____________
A) Price above or below the stipulated price
B) Any price but not below the transfer price
C) Cost price
D) A price that is equal to the mark up
Answer: a
Solution: Cost plus mark up is a pricing strategy in which the selling price is determined by adding a specific amount mark up to a product unit cost

Q: In dealing with incomplete record, fixed assets are posted to___________-

A) Profit and loss account as brought forward figure
B) Closing balance sheet as carried forward figure
C) Closing balance sheet as brought forward figure
D) Profit and loss as carried forward figure
Answer: d
Solution: fixed asset are brought forward in closing balance sheet

Q: The cost price method is applicable when_____
A) Goods are sold at specific prices
B)  goods are perishable
C)  goods attract different gross profit percentage
D) to disclose gross profit or loss
Answer: b
Solution: cost price method is used to enhance quick sales

Q: Sule and Ahmed are in partnership sharing profit and losses equally. If Khadija is admitted as a new partner to take 1/5 th as her share. What is the new profit or loss sharing?
A)  Sule1/3, Ahmed1/3, Khadija 1/3
B) Sule1/3, Ahmed1/3, Khadija 1/3
C) Sule1/5, Ahmed1/5, Khadija3/5
D)  Sule2/5, Ahmed1/5, Khadija2/5
Answer: b
Solution: If Khadija is to take 1/5th i.e. 20%

  Sule and Ahmed are to share 80% (100% - 20%) equally

  Sule = 2/5

  Ahmed = 2/5

  Khadija = 1/5

Q: Adex Ltd. issues stock to its retail branches at cost price. The following information relates to Ede branch: Stock at branch 1st January at cost ₦400, Goods sent to branch at cost ₦8000, Returns to head office ₦340, Cash sales ₦9160, Stock at branch 31st December at cost ₦720. Calculate the cost of goods credited to the head office trading account.
A) ₦7340
B)  ₦7460
C)  ₦7500
D) ₦7660
Answer: a
Solution: The cost of goods credited to the Head Office Trading Account is computed as:

Opening stock (₦400)

Goods sent to branch (₦8,000)
– Returns to Head Office (₦340)
– Closing stock (₦720)
= ₦7,340

Q: Which of the following is not a type of branch?
A) Dependent branch
B) foreign branch
C) independent branch
D) single branch
Answer: d
Solution: Branches are typically classified as:

Dependent branches, which rely on the head office for purchases and policies

Independent branches, which operate like standalone entities with their own accounting systems

Foreign branches, which are located in another country and may involve additional currency and regulatory considerations

The term “single branch” isn’t used as a formal classification.

papers.sourceText: Q: Use the information below to answer questions 28 and 29. It is the tradition of the club to write off an amount equal to 25% of the subscriptions received as other expenses. What is the amount to be written off as other expenses? A) ₦4,500 B) ₦6,000 C) ₦4,000 D) ₦5,000. Answer: d Solution: Given Information: Subscriptions received: ₦20,000 Club tradition: Write off 25% of subscriptions received as other expenses Calculation: Amount to be written off as other expenses = 25% of subscriptions received = 25% × ₦20,000 = 0.25 × ₦20,000 = ₦5,000 Q: Given the following information: additional capital is ₦4,000, capital is ₦8,000, closing capital is ₦12,000, and net profit is ₦1,500, what are the drawings for the period? A) ₦1,500 B) ₦3,000 C) ₦12,000 D) ₦10,500 Answer: a Solution: To find the drawings, use the capital account equation: Opening Capital + Additional Capital + Net Profit - Drawings = Closing Capital Rearranging to find drawings: Drawings = Opening Capital + Additional Capital + Net Profit - Closing Capital From the given information: Opening Capital = ₦8,000 Additional Capital = ₦4,000 Net Profit = ₦1,500 Closing Capital = ₦12,000 Drawings = ₦8,000 + ₦4,000 + ₦1,500 - ₦12,000 Drawings = ₦13,500 - ₦12,000 = ₦1,500 Therefore, the drawings for the period stand at ₦1,500. Q: To account for expenses paid by head office on behalf of the branch, the branch should___________ A) Debit profit and loss account and credit head office account B) Debit head office account and credit cash C) Credit cash and debit profit and loss account D) Credit profit and loss account and debit head office account Answer: a Solution: The head office maintains a book, (branch account) more or less like other personal accounts, so that any expenses incurred on behalf of the branch will also be debited to the branch account. Similarly, in the branch books, there will be head office accounts Q: The petty cash book kept on imprest system should have A) A credit balance only B) A debit or nil balance C) A debit balance only D) Both debit and credit balance; Answer: c Q: The issued share capital is the number of shares that are A) shared among the directors B) authorised by the shareholders C) fully subscribed D) in the share certificate Answer: c Solution: Issued share capital represents the portion of the company’s authorized capital that has actually been allotted to and subscribed by shareholders. It is the total number of shares for which applications have been accepted (i.e., fully subscribed), not merely authorized or held by directors. Q: In preparing a profit and loss account, a decrease in provision for doubtful debts accounts is treated as A) Currentability B) expenses C) Income D) Current asset Answer: c Q: Abelawo ltd operates a retail branch at Aba. All purchases are made by the head office in Onitsha and goods are charged to the branch at cost plus 50%. During the year ended. Goods sent to branch at invoiced price is ₦30,870, cash sales ₦13,020 and Bad debt amounted to 129. From the following, what is the profit? A) ₦20,580 B) ₦10,290 C) ₦7,980 D) ₦30,870 Answer: b Solution: To find the profit, the unrealized profit in the goods sent to branch needs to be determined. Given information: Goods sent to branch at invoiced price = ₦30,870 Invoiced price = Cost + 50% markup Cash sales = ₦13,020 Bad debt = ₦129 Finding the cost price of goods sent to branch: If invoiced price = Cost + 50% of cost = 1.5 × Cost Then: Cost = ₦30,870 ÷ 1.5 = ₦20,580 Unrealized profit in goods sent to branch: Profit = Invoiced price - Cost price Profit = ₦30,870 - ₦20,580 = ₦10,290 The profit from the markup on goods sent to branch is ₦10,290. Q: Partners' salaries and drawings are usually posted to the? A) trading account B) current account C) capital account D) partners' account Answer: b Solution: Partners' salaries and drawings are usually posted to the current account. In partnership accounting, there are typically two main accounts for each partner: Capital Account - Records the permanent capital contributions and withdrawals of partners. This account usually remains relatively stable. Current Account - Records all regular transactions with partners including: Partners' salaries Partners' drawings Interest on capital Interest on drawings Share of profits or losses Q: Use the information below to answer questions 14 and 15 Palaju Enterprises had fixed assets of ₦3,100,000 at the end of the year. Fixed assets costing ₦900,000 with provision for depreciation of ₦150,000 were disposed of during the period. Fixed assets of ₦100,000 were added during the year. Provision for depreciation was ₦350,000 at the beginning of the year and ₦300,000 at the end of the year. What was the value of fixed assets at the beginning of the year? A) ₦2,900,000 B) ₦3,800,000 C) ₦3,900,000 D) ₦4,000,000 Answer: c Solution: Opening Balance + Additions - Disposals = Closing Balance Rearranging to find Opening Balance: Opening Balance = Closing Balance + Disposals - Additions Substituting the values: Opening Balance = ₦3,100,000 + ₦900,000 - ₦100,000 Opening Balance = ₦4,000,000 - ₦100,000 = ₦3,900,000 Q: Given: I. Cash refunds II. Debit note issued III. Dishonored cheque IV. Purchases The item on the credit side of purchases ledger control account includes A) I, II and III only B) I and II only C) III and IV only D) I, III and IV only Answer: c Solution: The credit side of the Purchases Ledger Control Account shows items that increase the amount you owe to suppliers. These are: III. Dishonoured cheque, because a bounced cheque reverses a payment and increases your outstanding balance. IV. Purchases, as credit purchases directly raise your payables. Cash refunds (I) and debit notes issued (II) reduce what you owe and therefore appear on the debit side. Q: Alabede (₦IG) limited issued 50 000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each at a market value of ₦2.50 each. the share premium is? A) ₦75,000 B) ₦500 000 C) ₦50 000 D) ₦25 000 Answer: a Solution: Calculate the share premium: Nominal value (par) = ₦1 per share Issue (market) price = ₦2.50 per share Premium per share = ₦2.50 − ₦1 = ₦1.50 Total share premium = Premium per share × Number of shares Share premium = ₦1.50 × 50,000 = ₦75,000 Q: The major sources of revenue for the state and local governments is A) value added tax B) statutory allocation C) taxes and levies D) recurrent revenue. Answer: b Q: The net book value at the time of sale was A) N= 16,000 B) N= 14,000 C) N= 12,000 D) N= 6,000. Answer: d Q: The major feature of a journal is that it has A) five columns, date, particulars, folio, debit and credit B) three columns, date, particulars, folio and amount C) Six columns, date. particulars, folio, amount debit and credit D) four columns, date, particulars, folio and amount Answer: a Solution: A typical journal entry usually has four columns: the date of the transaction, the particulars, and columns for the debits and credits. Sometimes, the folio column can be included, but is it not a compulsory requirement. Q: When a customer's cheque is returned unpaid in a debtor's control accounting system, the treatment will be? A) debit bank, credit custmer and credit conyrol account B) credit bank, debit customer, and credit control account C) debit customer, debit control accountand credit bank D) credit control account, debit bank and debit customer Answer: c Solution: When a customer's cheque is returned unpaid (dishonored), Reverse the original entry that was made when the cheque was first received. Originally when the cheque was received: Debit: Bank Credit: Customer's account Credit: Sales Ledger Control Account Now that the cheque is returned unpaid, reverse this entry: Debit: Customer's account (restore the debt) Debit: Sales Ledger Control Account (restore the control balance) Credit: Bank (remove the cash that was never actually received) Q: A sales for ₦2,570 was recorded in the sales day book as ₦2750. The error committed was A) error of principle B) error of commission C) error of original entry D) compensating error Answer: c Solution: An error of original entry occurs when an incorrect amount is posted to the correct account. A particular example of an error of original entry is a transposition error where the numbers are not entered in the correct order. This type of error deals directly with the wrong use of figures Q: Why are adjustments in the profit and loss account necessary? A) To cover some expenses of the following year B) To show the provisions made during the year C) To show the total expenses paid and income received during the year D) To ascertain the actual expenses incurred and income earned during the year Answer: d Solution: Fundamental principle of preparing P&L account is that expenses and income relating to only the trading period are taken to the trading profit and loss account. Q: Which of the following accounts would appear in the nominal ledger? (I) Sanison’s account (a debtor) ( II) Motor vehicle account (III) Sales account (IV) Rent and rates account A) I, II and III only B) I, III and IV only C) II, III and IV only D) Ill and IV only Answer: b Q: Balance as per cashbook ₦2, 970 Bank Charges ₦220 Unpresented cheques ₦3, 950 Uncredited cheques ₦4, 178 Direct debit by bank ₦1, 0000 Determine the balance as per bank statement. A) ₦ 1,978 B) ₦ 1962 C) ₦ 1,522 D) ₦ 2,522 Answer: c Solution: Calculation: Balance as per bank statement = 2,970 + 3,950 - 4,178 - 220 - 1,000 = 2,970 + 3,950 - 5,398 = 6,920 - 5,398 = 1,522 Q: On December 31, 2012, Infinite Grace had a note payable due on August 1, 2013. On January 20, 2013, Infinite Grace signed a financing agreement to borrow the balance of the note payable from a lending institution to refinance the note. The agreement does not expire within one year, and no violation of any provision in the financing agreement exists. On February 1, 2013. Infinite Grace was informed by its financial advisor that the lender is not expected to be financially capable of honouring the agreement. Infinite Grace's financial statements were issued on March 31, 2013. How should Infinite Grace classify the note on its balance sheet at December 31,2012? A) as a current liability because the financing agreement was signed after the balance sheet datecapable of honouring the agreement B) as a current liability because the leader is not expected to be financially C) as a long-term liability because the agreement does not expire within one year D) as a long-term liability because no violation of any provision in the financing agreement exists. Answer: c Q: Which of the following is accounted for in receipts and payments account? A) Accrued expenses on annual dances B) Subscriptions due but not yet received C) interest on bank deposit D) Depreciation of the club house Answer: c Solution: "A receipt and payment account is a summarized cash book (cash and bank) for a given period" The bank column would reflect interest on bank deposits Q: The following accounting entries are made when bad debt is recovered A) debit bad debts accounts and credit bad debt recovered account B) debit debtors accounts and recovered account C) debit bad debts recovered account and credit bad debts account D) debit bad debts account and credit profit and loss account Answer: b Solution: The standard “recovery of a previously written-off debt” entry is: Reinstate the debtor: Debit Debtors Control Account Recognize the income: Credit Bad Debts Recovered Account So the debit entry is against the Debtors Control Account. Q: When a transaction causes an assets account to increase, there is? A) a decrease of equal amount inthe owner's equity account B) an increase in a liability account C) an increase of equal amonut in another assets account D) a decrease of equal amount in a liability account Answer: b Solution: This question refers to the accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Owner’s Equity When an asset increases, something else must also increase or decrease to keep the equation balanced. Q: The following information were extracted from the books of Miliki state: sinking of bore holes ₦2,900,000, purchase of motor car ₦920,000, stationery ₦300,000, electricity ₦45,000, purchase of drugs ₦76,000, and purchase of beds ₦425,000. What is the recurrent expenditure? A) ₦345,000 B) ₦3,245,000 C) ₦421,000 D) ₦4,245,000 Answer: c Solution: Recurrent expenditure refers to operating expenses that occur regularly and are consumed within a short period (usually within a year). These are expenses for day-to-day operations. From the given items: Stationery: ₦300,000 (recurrent - office supplies) Electricity: ₦45,000 (recurrent - utility expense) Purchase of drugs: ₦76,000 (recurrent - medical supplies) The other items (sinking of bore holes, motor car, and beds) are capital expenditures as they are long-term assets. Recurrent expenditure = ₦300,000 + ₦45,000 + ₦76,000 = ₦421,000 Therefore, the recurrent expenditure is ₦421,000. Q: Use the information below to answer questions 28 and 29 Subscription received during the year ₦30,000 Subscription owed last year ₦4,000 Subscription received for next year ₦6,000 What is the subscription to be charged to income and expenditure account? A) ₦28,000 B) ₦34,000 C) ₦30,000 D) ₦20,000 Answer: a Solution: Income = Received during year + Opening arrears − Advance for next year Substituting the numbers: Income = ₦30,000 + ₦4,000 − ₦6,000 = ₦28,000 Q: In a not - for - profit making organization, when the total income is less than the total expenditure, the difference is a A) surplus B) shortfall C) loss D) deficit Answer: d Q: From the following bank reconciliation information: Balance as per cash book is ₦5,467, Uncredited cheques amount to ₦4,410, and Unpresented cheques total ₦19,404. What is the balance as per bank statement? A) ₦20,461 B) ₦21,091 C) ₦21,109 D) ₦19,021 Answer: a Solution: Balance per bank statement = Balance per cash book + Unpresented cheques − Uncredited cheques = ₦5,467 + ₦19,404 − ₦4,410 = ₦20,461 Q: An increase in government expenditure within a year is taken care of by means of A) virement B) financial regulations C) supplementary estimate D) warrant. Answer: b Q: MORADE had total assets of N760,000, capital stock of N150,000 and retained earnings of N215,000. What was Morade's debt-to-equity ratio? A) 2.63 B) 1.08 C) 0.52 D) 0.48 Answer: b Q: Which of the following methods of invoicing goods to branches facilitate easy checks on the activities of branches? A) Selling price B) Fixed percentage on cost C) Cost price D) Invoice price Answer: c Solution: Goods are transferred from head office to branch at cost price, selling price and cost price plus mark up Q: The principle use of control accounts is to A) localize error within the ledger B) prevent fraud C) increase sales D) record assets and liabilities Answer: a Solution: Control accounts (like the sales ledger control account and purchases ledger control account) are used to check the accuracy of postings in the subsidiary ledgers. By comparing the totals, errors can be quickly identified and localized. Q: Use the information below to answer question 28 and 29. Raw materials inventory at the beginning of a period was ₦ 46,800 and at the close of the period there was a balance of ₦38,600. From the purchases made during the period, defective materials costing ₦9,200 were returned. Cost of materials consumed during the period was ₦448,500. What was the cost of materials available for use during the period? A) ₦487,100 B) ₦449,500 C) ₦448,500 D) ₦440,300 Answer: a Solution: Opening inventory + (Purchases − Returns) From the previous calculation, Purchases = ₦449 500 and Returns = ₦9 200, so net purchases = ₦449 500 − ₦9 200 = ₦440 300. Materials available = ₦46,800 + ₦440,300 = ₦487,100 Q: Based on the following information, calculate the The value of raw materials consumed: Opening stock of raw materials on 1/1/09 was ₦2,000, work-in-progress was ₦5,000, closing stock of raw materials on 31/12/09 was ₦500, work-in-progress was ₦4,000, raw materials purchased during the year was ₦18,000, direct labour was ₦7,500, direct expenses were ₦3,000, and factory expenses were ₦10,000. A) ₦18,500 B) ₦19,500 C) ₦26,000 D) ₦37,500 Answer: b Solution: To find the raw materials consumed, we use the formula: Raw Materials Consumed = Opening Stock of Raw Materials + Raw Materials Purchased - Closing Stock of Raw Materials Raw Materials Consumed = ₦2,000 + ₦18,000 - ₦500 Raw Materials Consumed = ₦20,000 - ₦500 = ₦19,500 Q: If the total discount allowed in a cash book was ₦230 and the total discount received was ₦255, which of the following is true concerning the two discounts? A) They must be balanced in the cash book and the difference taken to the debtors ledger B) They must be balanced in the cash book and the difference taken to the trial balance C) They should not be balanced in the cash book before being taking to the trial balance D) They should not appear in the trial balance as they were already either received or paid out Answer: c Solution: They should not be netted off in the cash book; both Discount Allowed (₦230) and Discount Received (₦255) are carried separately into the trial balance. Q: A provision is A) an expense of business to be paid for in cash B) an amount of loss from trading activities C) a loss in value of all business assets D) an expense the amount of which is not certain Answer: d Q: The amount of recurrent expenditure was A) Le 245,000. B) Le 175,000 C) Le 135,00. D) Le 80,000 Answer: c Q: The effect of overstating-revenue expenditure in the profit and loss account is that the A) opening stock will be increased B) net profit will be understated C) net profit will be overstated D) opening stock will be decreased Answer: b Q: Profit or loss in a partnership is usually arrived at after deducting from gross profit all expenses including? A) partners' salaries B) interest on capital C) partners' drawings D) interest on loans Answer: d Solution: Explanation: Profit or loss is found after deducting operating expenses (e.g., rent, wages, interest on loans). Items like partners' drawings are not expenses, and partners' salaries or interest on capital are typically treated as appropriations of profit (handled in the profit & loss appropriation account), not ordinary business expenses. Q: The use of the folio in the ledger is for A) referencing purposes B) particulars of the transaction C) the account titles D) only credit items Answer: a Solution: The folio in the ledger is used for referencing purposes. It helps in cross-referencing between the ledger and the journal, making it easier to track transactions and locate specific entries. Q: During the period, Department P opened with stock of ₦2 000, made purchases of ₦2 500 and recorded sales of ₦6 000. Its closing stock was ₦1 500. Department P also received goods costing ₦300 transferred in from Department Q and incurred operating expenses of ₦200. What was Department P’s net profit for the period? A) ₦2,500 B) ₦2,800 C) ₦3,000 D) ₦5,200 Answer: a Solution: Net profit for Department P = Sales ₦6 000 – Cost of Goods Sold [(₂₀₀₀ + ₦2 500 + ₦300 – ₦1 500) = ₦3 300] – Expenses ₦200 = ₦2 500.
