B) delivery van account
C)  cash account
D) profit and loss accounts
Answer: c
Solution: if there was a Loss on sale, we Debit cash for the amount received, debit all accumulated depreciation, debit the loss on sale of asset account, and credit the fixed asset.
if there was a Gain on sale. Debit cash for the amount received, debit all accumulated depreciation, credit the fixed asset, and credit the gain on sale of asset account.

Cash is received and expected to be debited going by the principles of double entry.

The MOA of a company contains the object for which the company is formed. It identifies the scope of its operations and determines the boundaries it cannot cross.

Q: Use the information below to answer this question.

A business has three departments x, y and z

You are given the following information

Selling and distribution expenses ₦5200
Rent for the year₦6000
Department turnover floor space in square metres

X ₦60,000 80

Y ₦80,000 60

Z ₦100,000 60

How much rent is apportioned to department Z?
A)  ₦1, 500
B) ₦3, 000
C) ₦1, 800
D) ₦2, 000
Answer: c
Solution: Rent is apportioned on floor‐space. Total space = 80 + 60 + 60 = 200 m², so rent per m² = 6 000 ÷ 200 = ₦30/m².
Department Z has 60 m², so its share = 60 × 30 = ₦1 800.

Q: Use the information below to answer this question

Segun Ojo, didn’t keep her books on double principle. On 1st Jan, 2014, cash in hand was 850, bank overdraft 3500, debtor 15,500,stock 18,000, fittings 9,000 and creditors 12,700. As at Dec, 2014, cash in hand was 1200, cash at bank 2,500, debtors 10,000, stock 20,500, furnishing 4,000 and creditors 17,000

Compute the capital as at 1st Jan, 2014.
A) 27,150
B) 43,350
C) 16,200
D) 34,350
Answer: a
Solution: To find Segun Ojo’s capital at 1 Jan 2014, take all assets less all liabilities at that date:

Opening assets

Cash in hand: ₦ ⁠850

Debtors: ₦ 15 500

Stock: ₦ 18 000

Fittings: ₦ ⁠9 000
Total assets = 850 + 15 500 + 18 000 + 9 000 = ₦ 43 350

Opening liabilities

Bank overdraft: ₦ ⁠3 500

Creditors: ₦ 12 700
Total liabilities = 3 500 + 12 700 = ₦ 16 200

Opening capital = Total assets – Total liabilities
= 43 350 – 16 200
= ₦ 27 150

Q: Which of the following is not a proper form of the accounting equation
A) fixed assets + current assets - liabilities = capital
B) fixed assests + current assests + liabilities = capital
C) ixed assets – liabilities + current assets = capital
D) fixed asset + current asset – capital = liabilities
Answer: b
Solution: The simplest presentation of capital employed is total assets minus current liabilities. Sometimes, it is equal to all current equity plus interest-generating loans (non-current liabilities).

Q: Using the given information, calculate the acid test ratio:

Stock: ₦11,250
Debtors: ₦18,750
Creditors: ₦3,750
Bank: ₦4,000
Net profit: ₦7,500
Net: ₦60,000
A) 5 : 1
B)  6 : 1
C)  6 : 1 : 1
D) 4 : 1
Answer: b
Solution: Quick assets = Debtors + Bank = 18,750 + 4,000 = 22,750
Acid-test ratio = Quick assets/Creditors = 22,750/3,750 ≈ 6.06 : 1. Rounded to the nearest whole‐number ratio, that’s 6 : 1.

Q: The following account are prepared when goods are sent to branch except
A) Branch stock
B) Goods set to branch account
C) Branch adjustment account
D) Branch debtors account
Answer: d
Solution: Branch debtors account is used to exercise control over branch debtors. It is maintained when the branch is allowed to sell goods on credit. This account records transactions with the branch debtors and is prepared like sundry debtors account

Q: What does liquidity ratio measure?
A) measures operating efficiency of a company
B)  measures the ability of a company to meet its current obligations.
C)  measures the value of investments of a company
D) measures the financial leverage of a company
Answer: b
Solution: liquidity ratio attempt to measure the ability to meet up with current obligations e.g. current ratio which measures the current asset to current liabilities.

Q: Goods stolen at the branch is debited to
A) branch stock account
B) defalcations account
C) branch debtors account
D) branch adjustment account
Answer: b
Solution: When goods are stolen at a branch, this represents a loss due to dishonest activities or theft. In accounting, such losses are recorded in a defalcations account, which is specifically used to track losses arising from fraud, theft, or other dishonest acts.

Q: Determine wage expenses from the given information, wages outstanding at the beginning, wages paid during the period 15000 and wages outstanding of the period 2,000
A)  ₦16,000
B)  ₦17,000
C)  ₦13,000
D) ₦14,000
Answer: b
Solution: Wage Expense=Wages Paid + Outstanding:
Wage Expense = 15,000 + 2,000 = 17,000

Q: The income and expenditure account of a club is the same as
A) single entry account
B) a profit and loss account
C) a trading account
D) a cash book
Answer: b
Solution: this is because the income and expenditure account just like the profit and loss account shows the income to ascertain surplus or deficit.

Q: Keeping records under single entry system has the advantage of
A) Keeping records under single entry system has the advantage of
B) Simplicity in terms of operation
C) Accuracy in terms of operation
D) Completeness in terms of records
Answer: b
Solution: Advantages Of Single Entry System. Single entrysystem does not need any special accounting knowledge and personnel to record financial transaction of the business. It can be maintained easily by the business owner. So, this system of book-keeping is simple to maintain and easy to practice.

Q: The ledger entries to be made if cash sales is banked is debit
A) cash, credit sales
B) sales, credit cash
C)  bank, credit cash
D) bank, credit sales
Answer: d
Solution: When you make a cash sale and lodge the proceeds directly into the bank, you:

Debit Bank (to increase your bank balance)

Credit Sales (to record the revenue earned)

Q: The act of making necessary adjustment after comparing the actual cost with targeted cost is cost ----------------------------
A) conversion
B) control
C) allocation
D) analysis
Answer: b
Solution: The process of reviewing actual costs against targeted (or budgeted) costs and then making the necessary corrective adjustments is known as cost control.

Q: The income and expenditure account of a club is the same as
A) single entry account
B)  a profit and loss account 
C) a trading account
D) a cash book
Answer: b
Solution: The income and expenditure account of a club serves exactly the same purpose as a profit and loss account in a trading concern: it summarizes all the revenues (incomes) and the expenses (expenditures) for the period to show the net surplus or deficit.

Q: The basis of accounting for public sector is
A) accrual basis
B) cost basis
C) revenue basis
D) cash basis
Answer: d
Solution: This is the basis for recording in government accounting where revenue are recorded when cash is received.
 

Q: When shares are sold at more than the par value, they are said to have been issued at
A) A premium
B) Normal value
C) A discount
D) A profit
Answer: a
Solution: When shares are issued at a price above their par (nominal) value, the excess is called a share premium

Q: If sales return is understated, it implies that ------------------------------ is overstated
A) return inward
B)  sales figure
C) cost of sales
D) return outward
Answer: b
Solution: This is so because returns inwards are deducted from sales to ascertain the actual sales made after subtracting defected goods

Q: The accounting concept that allows the cost of kitchen cutlery to be expensed, though it can be used for more than one year is
A) Materiality
B) Accrual
C) Going concern
D) Business entity
Answer: a
Solution: Materiality states that only items of material values are recorded e.g. the cost of a stapler should not be capitalized but expensed just as kitchen cutlery.

Q: The major distinguishing element between the final account of a partnership and that of a sole trader is the
A) drawing account
B) capital account
C) Creditor account
D) Appropriation account
Answer: b
Solution: The Major Difference Of The Financial Statement between a Sole Proprietorship And Partnership is More than one capital account. The number of capital accounts depends on the number of partners in the Partnership concern. Profit & loss is distributed to the partners' capital account according to the agreed ratio

Q: Which of the following is shown in the profit and loss appropriation account of a company
A) interest charges
B) depreciation
C) directors emoluments
D) dividends
Answer: d
Solution: In general accounting, appropriation accounts are mainly prepared by partnerships and limited liability companies (LLCs). They are an extension of theprofit and loss statement, showing how the profits of a firm are allocated to shareholders or to increase reserves indicated in the balance sheet. it usually contains dividends, retained earnings, goodwill etc


Q: Which of the following cannot be realized?
A) creditors
B) debtors
C) motor vehicles
D) goodwill
Answer: d
Solution: Good will being an intangible asset cannot be seen or touched and are just believed to exist goodwill can only be valued to be a certain amount, the realizable value becomes a difficult task.

Q: Use the information below to answer this question.

Dangote acquired Dantata’s business for ₦350,000. The total asset work were ₦820,000 and liabilities amounted to ₦ 640,000

The double entry to record the goodwill in the books is debt
A) purchase of business account and credit cash account
B) goodwill account and credit purchase of business account
C) cash account and credit goodwill account
D) goodwill account and credit cash account
Answer: b
Solution: when there is excess of purchase consideration over net assets, the accounting entries is to debit goodwill account as the receiving account and credit purchase of business account as the giving account.

Q: Which of the following is true in public sector accounting? Cost of assets is
A) depreciated on straight line method
B) expensed in the year of purchase
C) charged to federation account
D) depreciated on reducing balance method
Answer: b
Solution: In government account, assets are written off in their year of purchase.

Q: Accounting information is used by investors and creditors of a company to predict
A) potential merger candidates for the company
B) appropriate remunerations for the company’s staff
C) future cash flows of the company
D) future tax payments of the company
Answer: c
Solution: The average lender or investor does not have ongoing inside access to the day-to-day operations of a company. Instead, it relies on financial accounting to provide accurate and readily comparable information. Financial accounting allows outside actors to observe the profitability and value of a business.

Creditors are interested in accounting information, because it enables them to determine the credit worthiness of the business.

Q: Which method of pricing can be used satisfactorily in either rising or falling price situation?
A) Market price
B) Average method
C) FIFO
D) Standard price
Answer: b
Solution: An average method which accommodate all the prices and then divide (inform of mean) is well acceptable in either of the two situation.

Q: Impersonal account is subdivided into

Real accounts (assets—both tangible and intangible)

Nominal accounts (income, expenses, gains and losses)

Q: An item in the balance sheet of a limited liability company is
A)  accrued expenses
B)  lighting and heating
C) salaries and wages
D) general expenses
Answer: a
Solution: Accrued expense is expense which has been incurred but not yet paid. Expense must be recorded in the accounting period in which it is incurred. Therefore, accrued expense must be recognized in the accounting period in which it occurs rather than in the following period in which it will be paid.

It can be found on the liabilities part of a balance sheet of a limited liability company

A) Accumulated depreciation.
B) Retained profit.

Answer: b

Q: The major advantage of the journal proper is that it
A) helps in the preparation of the balance sheet
B) prevents fraud and theft of item of the business

Answer: b
Solution: The advantages of using a journal in the recording process is, it discloses in one place the complete effects of a transaction, it provides a chronological record of transactions, & it helps to prevent or locate errors because the debit and credit amounts for each entry can be easily compared.

Q: Use the information below to answer the question that follows,

A machine bought for ₦35,000 was estimated to have a life span of 5years with a scrap value of ₦9,000.
If the scrap value is now ₦15,000. What will be the yearly depreciation using the straight line method.?
A) ₦11,000
B)  ₦7,000
C) ₦4,000
D) ₦24,000
Answer: c
Solution: subtract the revised scrap value (₦15,000) from the original cost (₦35,000) to get ₦20,000, then divide by the machine’s 5-year lifespan. Thus, annual depreciation is ₦20,000 ÷ 5 = ₦4,000 per year.

Q: The ratio that gives the indication of the efficiency of a firm's sales with respect to cost of goods sold is a
A)  return on capital employed
B)  gross profit margin
C) net profit margin
D) return on equity
Answer: a
Solution: Return on capital employed or ROCE is a profitability ratio that measures how efficiently a company can generate profits from its capital employed by comparing net operating profit to capital employed.

Solution: You take the cost (₦35,000), subtract the scrap value (₦9,000) to get ₦26,000, then divide by the useful life of 5 years: So the annual depreciation is ₦5,200.

Answer: c

Q: Given the following information:

Drawings: ₦3,500
Net loss: ₦2,500
Capital as at 1.1.2007: ₦35,000
Additional capital: ₦10,000

The adjusted capital as at 31.12.2007 is:
A) ₦45,000
B) ₦39, 000
C) ₦35,000
D) ₦46,000
Answer: b
Solution: To find the adjusted capital as at 31.12.2007, start with the opening capital and adjust for all changes during the year.
Given:

Capital 1.1.2007: 35,000
Additional capital: 10,000
Net loss: 2,500
Drawings: 3,500

Capital Account Movement:
Starting capital (1.1.2007): 35,000
Add:

Additional capital: +10,000

Less:

Net loss: -2,500
Drawings: -3,500

Calculation:
Adjusted capital as at 31.12.2007 = 35,000 + 10,000 - 2,500 - 3,500
= 45,000 - 6,000
= 39,000

Q: When goods are sent to the branch at cost plus mark-up, it means that the branch should sell at
A) a price above or below the stipulated price
B)  any price but not below the transfer price
C) cost price
D) a price that is equal to the mark-up
Answer: b
Solution: Cost-plus pricing is a pricing strategy in which the selling price is determined by adding a specific amount markup to a product's unit cost.

Cost plus pricing involves adding a markup to the cost of goods and services to arrive at a selling price. Under this approach, you add together the direct materialcost, direct labor cost, and overhead costs for a product, and add to it a markuppercentage in order to derive the price of the product.

Q: The current growth in the volume of trading and financial dealing in Nigeria is helped by
A) increased financial activities
B) government intervention
C)  credit as a factor in business
D) Payment for goods in cashc
Answer: c
Solution: The availability of credit allows businesses and consumers to purchase goods and services beyond their immediate cash resources, thereby increasing the volume of transactions and financial dealings. While cash payments, government intervention, and broader financial activities all play roles in the economy, it is the extension of credit that most directly fuels higher trading volumes by enabling deferred payments and greater purchasing power.

Q: A business acquisition shows the following assets and liabilities: Plant and Machinery ₦190,000, Motor Vehicle ₦170,000, Stock ₦60,000, Current Liabilities ₦50,000, Purchase consideration ₦400,000. Determine the amount of goodwill.
A) ₦110 000
B)  ₦80 000
C)  ₦90 000
D)  ₦30 000
Answer: d
Solution: Net assets acquired = (₦190,000 + ₦170,000 + ₦60,000) – ₦50,000 = ₦420,000 – ₦50,000 = ₦370,000
Goodwill = Purchase consideration – Net assets = ₦400,000 – ₦370,000 = ₦30,000.

Q: Which of these is the subsidiary book for return inwards?
A) Sales day book
B) Sales return journal
C)  Purchases day journal
D) Cash book
Answer: b
Solution: Sales return journal otherwise called return inward book is meant for recording of all good returned by customer

Q: When starting with the cash book balance in preparing the bank reconciliation statement, the followings are added
A) Unpresented cheque
B) Dividend
C)  Uncredited cheque
D) credit transfer
Answer: c
Solution: Uncredited cheque have to be less when starting with balance as per cashbook not add because the cheque are yet to be credited by the bank

Q: Two departments A and B have the following information: Department A has Sales ₦250,000, Purchases ₦500,000, Discount received ₦24,000, and Discount allowed ₦15,000. Department B has Sales ₦150,000 and Purchases ₦250,000. Determine the discount allowed by Department A.
A)  ₦5,000
B) ₦9,375
C) ₦5,625
D) ₦8,000
Answer: b
Solution: Step 1: Calculate total sales

Department A sales: ₦250,000
Department B sales: ₦150,000
Total sales: ₦400,000

Step 2: Calculate Department A's proportion of total sales
Department A's proportion = ₦250,000 ÷ ₦400,000 = 62.5%
Step 3: Allocate total discount allowed proportionally
Total discount allowed = ₦15,000 (given for the business)
Department A's discount allowed = ₦15,000 × 62.5% = ₦9,375
Department A's discount allowed is ₦9,375, representing their proportional share based on sales volume.

Q: Salaries in arrears is treated in the balance sheet as a
A)  current asset
B) current liability
C) fixed asset
D) long term liability
Answer: b
Solution: Current Liability: salaries in arrears fall into the category of them under the current liability because it is benefit due to outsiders but still enjoying by the organisation and can't exceed a year

Q: The following appears in trading account except
A) sales
B) carriage outward
C) carriage inward
D) opening stock
Answer: b
Solution: carriage outward: it is the cost of transporting goods from the company to the buyer. it is on debit side of the profit and loss account because it is an expenses incurred on distributing the goods to customer.

Q: When expenses are paid on behalf of the venture, the accounting entries is to debit
A) bank account and credit joint venture account
B) expenses account and credit bank account
C)  joint venture account and credit expenses account
D) joint venture account and credit bank account
Answer: d
Solution: Joint venture account is an account that all expenditure incurred for the venture is debited and all income is credited to.
Debit joint venture and credit bank account because expenses incurred on behalf of the venture has to be debited to the joint venture account and since the money is joint out the bank must be credited to balance the account

Q: A business has the following information for the year: Debtors opening ₦4,000, Debtors closing ₦1,500, Cash received from debtors ₦8,500, Bad debts written off ₦350, Discount allowed ₦500, Discount Received ₦1,000. What is the amount of sales for the year?
A) ₦3850
B) ₦6650
C) ₦1550
D) ₦6850
Answer: d
Solution: Using the debtors account to find sales:
Debtors Account Movement:
Opening Balance + Sales - Cash Received - Bad Debts - Discount Allowed = Closing Balance
Substituting the values:
₦4,000 + Sales - ₦8,500 - ₦350 - ₦500 = ₦1,500
Solving for Sales:
₦4,000 + Sales - ₦9,350 = ₦1,500
Sales = ₦1,500 + ₦9,350 - ₦4,000
Sales = ₦10,850 - ₦4,000
Sales = ₦6,850
Note: Discount received (₦1,000) is not relevant to the debtors account as it relates to creditors/suppliers, not customers.
The sales for the year is ₦6,850.

Q: Two departments A and B have the following information: Department A has Sales ₦250,000, Purchases ₦150,000, Discount received ₦24,000, and Discount allowed ₦15,000. Department B has Sales ₦500,000 and Purchases ₦250,000. Calculate the discount received in Department B.
A) ₦12,000
B) ₦40,000
C)  ₦16,000
D) ₦9,000
Answer: b
Solution: Department A’s discount‑received rate is ₦24 000 ÷ ₦150 000 = 16%. Applying this to Department B’s purchases (₦250 000) gives ₦250 000 × 16% = ₦40 000 as the discount received by Department B.

Q: Subscription in advance is treated in the balance sheet as a
A)  current asset
B) current liability
C) fixed asset
D) long term liability
Answer: b
Solution: current assets are assets of the company that can be easily converted to cash when needed

current liability: this is the liability owned to outsiders but still enjoying its benefit within a year e.g creditors, wages in arrears

Q: Which of these is the main source document for recording cash paid into bank?
A) invoice
B) cheque book
C) credit note
D) pay-in-slip
Answer: d
Solution: Pay-in-slip:this is in form of a slip designed with the name of the bank on top that has dates amounts in figure and word, column for the denomination of money paid in signature bank teller, stamp to prove the money is deposited into the bank

Q: A part of public company's profits belonging to the shareholders is
A) public issue
B) bonus
C) right issue
D) dividends
Answer: d
Solution: Dividend is known as the kind of benefit enjoyed by the shareholder for investing their fund in a particular organisation

Q: An advantage of FIFO method of stock valuation is that
A) it serves-as a control during inflation
B) it is calculated at the end of the year
C)  it is progressive in nature
D) its flow of cost is in sequence with the flow of stock.
Answer: d
Solution: The major advantage of the first in first out(FIFO) method of stock valuation

1. it is very easy to apply

2. no manipulation of income is possible

3. the balance sheet amount for inventory is likely to approximate the current market value

4. its flow of cost is in sequence with the flow of stock. Since the first stock will be considered for sale before other stock. the cost is always in sequence with the flow of stock because it corresponds with the normal physical flow of goods

Q: One of the options below have the same features as the profit and loss account in non-profit organization
A) Income and expenditure account
B)  profit and loss account
C) receipts and payment account
D) Non profit account
Answer: a
Solution: Income and expenditure : This is the type of account that operate same features as the profit and loss account it takes in consideration all arrears and prepayments

Q: The movement of goods from head office to a branch is treated in the head office as
A) Sales
B) issue
C) purchases
D) requisition
Answer: b
Solution: When the head office sends goods to a branch, it doesn’t record a sale or purchase; instead it debits the Branch Account (or Branch Stock Account) and credits the Head Office’s Stock Account as an issue of goods to the branch.

Q: Which type of cashbook entry involves recording the same amount on both the debit and credit sides to offset each other?
A) Contra entry
B) Compound entry
C) Transfer entry
D) Journal entry
Answer: a
Solution: A contra entry in the cashbook is used when the business moves money between its own cash and bank accounts—such as depositing cash into the bank or withdrawing cash from the bank

Q: one of the options below is not the source of income for non- profit organization
A) Entrance fees
B) subscription/dues
C) odrinary shares
D) Donations
Answer: c
Solution: Ordinary shares: This type of source of income is only used in profit oriented organization to generate fund the pubic so as to enable the organization make more profit at the end of a specified period

Q: Given:
I. Settlement of debts
II. Cessation of business
III. Introduction of assets
IV. Disposal of assets
Which of these constitutes dissolution of partnership?
A) II and IV only
B)  I, II and IV only
C)  I, II and III only
D)  II, III and IV only
Answer: b
Solution: Dissolution of partnership business simply means the break up of partnership business and which are caused by many factors
II,III and IV: disposal of asset does not constitute dissolution

Q: In manufacturing account, depreciation of office machine is charged to
A) trading account
B) appropriation account
C) balance street
D) profit and loss account
Answer: d
Solution: profit and loss account: the depreciation of the office machine is considered as part of administrative expense which must be charged against the profit of the company

Q: A double entry for a transaction that offsets one amount against another on both sides of the cashbook is a
A) original entry
B)  contra entry
C)  prime entry
D)  contract entry
Answer: b
Solution: contra entry is used to offset amount or same transaction against another on both side of the cashbook

Q: The discount column on the left-hand side of cashbook represents a discount
A) received from a creditor
B) allowed to a debtor
C) received from a debtor
D) allowed to a creditor
Answer: b
Solution: Allowed to a debtor: the debit side of the cashbook is where all proceeds from sales are recorded and have to be matched with the discount allowed to the debtor /creditor

Q: Capital for a profit making organization is generated through
A) Subscription
B) shares
C) donation
D) gift
Answer: b
Solution: Share: profit making organizations use different shares such as ordinary and preference shares to source for money from the public

Q: Goodwill can be created in the books of a partnership firm when
A) the partnership experiences super profit
B)  a new member is admitted
C) the business is being expanded
D)  the business suffers high loss
Answer: a
Solution: The partnership experiences super profit: super profit is the profit that is generated by intangible asset or the profit that is attributed by the tangible asset when such profit is capitalized we get intangible asset or goodwill

Q: The use of a three column cash book is determined by
A) cash discount
B) trade discount
C) cash transaction
D) Bank transaction
Answer: a
Solution: A cash discount is a deduction allowed by the seller of goods or by the provider of services in order to motivate the customer to pay within a specified time

Q: Processed data is only useful to user if it is
A) complex
B) quantitative
C) relevant
D) qualitative
Answer: c
Solution: first thing to be considered when gathering data is the relevant and usefulness of the data or information before considering the qualitative aspect and other things
Relevant : even if the information of data is not processed, if the processed data is relevant, it will be useful to the user

Q: Discount allowed is enjoyed by
A) Managers
B) Customers
C) Suppliers
D) Staff of the company
Answer: b
Solution: Customer: customers are the one that enjoys discount allowed. It is allowed to them by the suppliers. it can be in cash or trade

Q: The authority warrant issued prior to the approval of the appropriate bill at the beginning of the year
A)  provisional general warrant
B) annual general warrant
C) Reserved expenditure warrant
D) contigencies
Answer: a
Solution: Provisional general warrant is issued by minister to enable money to be released for expenditure for the early of the year before the appropriation Act is passed

Q: The principle of double entry developed from the axioms of accounting equation is given as
A)  Assets + Liability = Equity
B) Assets + Equity = Liabilities
C) Liabilities + Equity = Asset
D) Liabilities + Equity = Net assets
Answer: c
Solution: Liabilities + Equity = Asset is given as the fundamental equation

Q: You add the following when starting with the balance as per cash book when preparing the bank reconciliation statement except
A) Unpresented
B) Dividend
C) Uncredited cheque
D) credit transfer
Answer: c
Solution: Uncredited cheque: This have to be deducted when starting balance as per cash book

Q: Which fund is used to meet unforeseen or urgent expenditure
A) General reserve fund
B) Consolidated Reserve Fund
C) contingencies fund
D) special fund
Answer: c
Solution: contingencies fund: if there is an urgent and unforeseen need for expenditure for which no other provision exist, such expenses shall be deducted from the contingencies fund

Q: An evidence of payment issued to a government ministry by a revenue collector is
A) treasury receipt
B)  receipt voucher
C) payment voucher
D)  treasury card
Answer: b
Solution: Receipt voucher is raised as evidence by revenue collector when government funds and property or received

Receipt voucher: these are vouchers raised as evidence for the receipt of government funds and property. The revenue collected is prepared for the government ministry as a means that revenue has been collected

Q: Which of these is a content of a master file?
A) All records relevant to the organisation.
B) Records of assets of the organisation
C) A collection of data items
D)  All records relating to employees
Answer: a
Solution: All record relevant to the organization: the records which are only relevant to the organization such as the name and address as well as summary information such as amount due and year to date sales will be in master file

Q: Which of the following is used to service all operations of government?
A) Consolidated Revenue Fund
B) Consolidated Reserve Fund
C) Special Operational Fund
D) General-Reserve Fund
Answer: a
Solution: consolidation revenue fund generate its revenue through allocation from the federation account, court fees and fines etc and is used to finance government operation e g cost, overhead

Q: What is the effect of transaction when cash is paid into the bank
A) Bank balance decrease and cash balance increase
B)  bank balance decrease and cash balance decrease
C) cash balance increase and bank balance increase
D) cash balance decrease and bank balance increase
Answer: d
Solution: Cash balance decrease and bank balance increase: The cash as leaving the cash till and will be deposited into the bank

Q: Use the following information for the period: the opening debtors balance is ₦4,000; the closing debtors balance is ₦1,500; cash received from debtors totals ₦8,500; bad debts written off amount to ₦350; discount allowed to customers is ₦500; and discount received from customers is ₦1,000. If the gross profit for the period is ₦5,000, what is the net profit?
A)  ₦4,350
B) ₦6,000
C) ₦5,150
D) ₦4,000
Answer: c
Solution: Net profit = Gross profit − Bad debts − Discount allowed + Discount received
= ₦5,000 − ₦350 − ₦500 + ₦1,000 = ₦5,150

Q: A business has the following bank reconciliation information: Balance as per cashbook ₦5,467, Uncredited cheques ₦4,410, Unpresented cheques ₦19,404, and Cheques wrongly debited by bank ₦1,404. What is the balance as per bank statement?
A)  ₦21,901
B) ₦19,057
C)  ₦21,109
D)  ₦21,091
Answer: b
Solution: Starting from the cashbook balance of ₦5,467, we adjust for items not yet reflected in the bank statement:

Add unpresented cheques (outstanding at bank): ₦19,404

Subtract uncredited cheques (lodgements in transit): ₦4,410

Subtract cheques wrongly debited by the bank (the bank has already taken this amount): ₦1,404

So the bank statement balance is:
5,467 + 19,404 − 4,410 − 1,404 = ₦19,057

Q: Given:
I. It records subscription in arrears
II. Payments of liabilities is effected
III. The account does not show if cash payment is revenue or capital expenditure
IV. It performs the same function as cashbook
The features of receipts and payment account includes
A) I, II and IV

B) II,III and IV

C) III and IV

D) I, II and III
Answer: b
Solution: A Receipts and Payments Account:

II. Records the payment of liabilities as they’re settled in cash.

III. Does not distinguish whether cash payments are for revenue or capital items.

IV. Functions in the same way as a cashbook, summarizing all cash and bank receipts and payments.

It does not record transactions on an accrual basis (so it does not capture subscriptions in arrears), making statement I incorrect.

Q: Given:
I. Cash refunds
II. Debit note issued
III. Dishonored cheque
IV. Purchases
The item on the credit side of purchases ledger control account includes
A)  I, II and III only
B)  I and II only
C) III and IV only
D) I, III and IV only
Answer: c
Solution: The credit side of the Purchases Ledger Control Account shows items that increase the amount you owe to suppliers. These are:

III. Dishonoured cheque, because a bounced cheque reverses a payment and increases your outstanding balance.

IV. Purchases, as credit purchases directly raise your payables.

Cash refunds (I) and debit notes issued (II) reduce what you owe and therefore appear on the debit side.

Q: The correct expression of accounting equation is
A)  Assets = Liabilities + Equity
B) Net assets = Liabilities + Equity
C) Assets + Liabilities = Equity
D) Assets = Equity - liabilities
Answer: a
Solution: The fundamental accounting equation is Asset = Capital + Liabilities
Asset = Liabilities + Equity the total assets of the company is generated through liabilities to outsiders that the company is still enjoying in addition with the equity by the owners of the business

Q: The cat DEVOURED the rat A) did the rat devour the cat? B) what devoured the rat? C) did the cat eat the rat? D) Is this the rat that the cat devoured? Answer: c Solution: In responding to questions on emphatic stress, Interrogative sentence that contradicts the emphasized word is the correct option. This means that, the statement that does not have the emphasized word in it is the correct answer. Option C is the correct answer here because the word ''eat contradicts ''devour'' Q: If Joy hadn't been tripped up halfway through the race, she would have came first A) discouraged B) disqualified C) interrupted D) exhausted. Answer: c Q: film A) salt B) walk C) pslam D) chalk Answer: a Q: This type of response is [typical] of a lazy teacher A) symptomatic B) characteristics C) universal D) incontestable Answer: b Solution: Characteristic is correct answer. A thing is described as 'typical' of something else when becomes an observable and noticeable quality or attribute of it. Q: Church? A) feature B) chauffeur C) ocean D) machine Answer: a Q: Kaltume crouched over the papers on her desk A) wrote on B) stood on C) walked over D) bent over Answer: d Q: The landlord is fond of throwing his weight about A) the landlord likes healthy exercise B) the landlord is overweight C) the landlord gives orders to people D) the landlord is respected by his tenants Answer: c Solution: Throw (one's) weight around. to use your position or influence unfairly to get what you want Q: shine A) clean B) fine C) machine D) lain Answer: c Q: At the time I arrived, Olu was lying in third place. A) Olu's third position coincided with my arrival. B) When I arrived Olu was sleeping in the space reserved for him. C) It was a competition and Olu was in third position when I arrived. D) On my arrival at the competition, Olu went to sleep. Answer: a Q: From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that rhymes with the given word. Tenderly A) actually B) slenderly C) faithfully D) constantly Answer: b Solution: tenderly; /ˈtɛnd(ə)li/ slenderly; slɛnd(ə)li/ Q: This class __________students and teachers A) comprise B) comprises C) comprise of D) comprises of Answer: b Solution: Comprise means 'made up of'. Therefore, to say 'Comprises of/ Comprise of ' is a tautology. Note that, singular verbs must agree with a singular noun. The subject of the sentence is 'This Class' which is a singular noun This makes Option B correct. Q: Our son was highly active and exuberant A) subdued B) fulsome C) lively D) bright Answer: a Solution: exuberant; full of energy, excitement, and cheerfulness. subdued; (of a person or their manner) quiet and rather reflective or depressed. Q: Bubble? A) guy B) bull C) bumper D) gurgle Answer: c Solution: bubble; /ˈbʌb(ə)l/ bumper; /ˈbʌmpə/ Q: What was Omar's JAMB exam score? A) 230 B) 250 C) 220 D) 260 Answer: a Q: Caliph? A) presently B) perhaps C) powerful D) opponent Answer: c Solution: caliph; /ˈkeɪlɪf,ˈkalɪf/ powerful; /ˈpaʊəfʊl,ˈpaʊəf(ə)l/ Q: Tunde's reaction underscores the point I was making? A) justifies B) emphasizes C) summarizes D) contradicts Answer: d Q: inoffensive A) inOFfensive B) inoffenSIVE C) inofFENsive D) INoffensive Answer: c Solution: Pronounced as in/of/FEN/sive. The third syllable is more pronounced. Q: Epitaph. A) Pneumonia. B) Pseudo. C) Fan. D) Paper. Answer: c Solution: epitaph; /ˈɛpɪtɑːf,ˈɛpɪtaf/ fan; /fan/ Q: departmentalize A) departMENtalize B) dePARTmentalize C) DEpartmentalize D) departmenTAIize Answer: d Q: Some people consider the leather uphoistery and thick rugs a bit sumptuous A) expensive B) desirable C) lavish D) simple Answer: d Q: I shall find time for my ……… when I get …… with this difficult assignment. A) Pat time /over B) pass-time/over C) pastime/through D) pastime/through Answer: d Q: This question is from the novel The Last Days at Forcados High school. __________ had been expelled from two different schools and kicked out of the university. A) jolly B) Jimi C) nene ekpo D) wole Answer: d Solution: In the latter part of chapter two, Jimi was actually thinking about all that had happened and recounting how his brother “wole” has been expelled from two different school and kicked out of the university. He also thought about about how he (wole) has falsified his father’s signature and made with a lot of money. The answer is (d) Wole Q: The officer was given an invidious task A) vivid B) cruel C) pleasant D) sinister Answer: c Q: The speaker was rather bold in his presentation of the case A) unfair B) reserved C) ashamed D) formal Answer: b Q: I have the ---------- of meeting him A) previlege B) privilege C) previledge D) priviledge Answer: b Solution: The correct answer is ‘B’ privilege which means (a peculiar benefit, advantage, or favour; a right or immunity not enjoyed by others by others or by all. The others are wrongly spelt. Q: It is surprising that this politician has now turned renegade? A) milliant B) corrupt C) loyal D) quiet Answer: c Q: For beating ……. his course mate, Agbaji was……… from the university. A) up/rusticated B) on/expelled C) at/removed D) away/sent out Answer: a Q: Prestige? A) bag B) badge C) reggae D) leisure Answer: b Q: There should be a level playing field for women entering politics. A) Women should not be allowed to enter politics B) Sports facilities should be provided for women entering politics. C) Special privileges should be given to women who want to enter politics D) Men and women should be able to compete are political arena on an equal basis. Answer: d Q: choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap(s). For fear of being caught, the thief shouted and cursed the slow bank manager in a language ________much for words. A) Way B) Too C) Very D) So Answer: b Solution: Here is an adverb of degree. The correct item to use is ‘too’. Q: I do not trust him', he said, in a rare moment of candour? A) reproach B) dishonesty C) frankness D) fairness Answer: b Solution: Candour; the quality of being open and honest; frankness Q: A) wife B) of C) off D) laugh Answer: b Q: God opposes the proud and rewards the _________ A) poor B) honest C) humble D) faithful Answer: c Solution: Humble is the opposite of the adjective 'Proud' Q: He says he ............. find me a job, but will accommodate me. A) could not B) was notable to C) is not able to D) cannot be able to Answer: a

Q: A business has the following balance sheet: Capital ₦40,000, Furnishing ₦10,000, Ceiling Fan ₦1,500, and Cash in Hand ₦28,500, with total assets and liabilities both equaling ₦40,000.
If at 31/1/95 the following information was ascertained:

Rent for shop ₦12,000 paid for the year
Total purchases ₦15,000
Total sales ₦8,200
Stock of goods left ₦10,000
Paid sales boy ₦500

What is the balance on its cash account as at 31/1/95?
A) ₦22,800
B) ₦9,200
C) ₦800
D)  ₦21,200
Answer: b
Solution: Starting with opening cash balance of ₦28,500, we calculate the cash movements:
Cash Outflows:

Rent paid: ₦12,000
Purchases: ₦15,000
Sales boy wages: ₦500
Total cash outflows: ₦27,500

Cash Inflows:

Sales (assuming cash sales): ₦8,200

Cash Balance Calculation:
Opening Cash + Cash Inflows - Cash Outflows
= ₦28,500 + ₦8,200 - ₦27,500
= ₦36,700 - ₦27,500
= ₦9,200
The cash account balance as at 31/1/95 is ₦9,200.

Q: Which of the following is a common cause of a discrepancy between head office and branch trial office________
A) Stock and repayment
B) Creditors and cash in trans
C) Stock and cash in transit
D) Debtors and cash in transit
Answer: c
Solution: Goods in transit are goods sent by the head office to branch but by the close of financial year, these goods have not yet reached the branch.

 Cash in transit are cash remitted by the branch to head office by the end of the financial year this cash has not yet reached the head office

Another major cause of discrepancy is returns in transit. This is the returns by the branch to head office but by the end of the year, they have not been received by the head office

Q: Using the following information, calculate the balance that should appear on the bank statement. The cashbook shows a balance of ₦13,560. There are unpresented cheques totaling ₦5,120, and a cheque for ₦2,300 has been paid into the bank but not yet credited. The bank has also received a dividend of ₦2,000, charged ₦280 in bank fees, and processed a standing order of ₦600.
A) ₦10,740
B) ₦11,860
C)  ₦16,380
D) ₦17,500
Answer: d
Solution: Balance per bank statement = ₦13,560 + ₦5,120 + ₦2,000 – ₦2,300 – ₦280 – ₦600 = ₦17,500.

Q: Profit or loss in a partnership is usually arrived at after deducting from gross profit all expenses including____________
A)  Partners salaries
B) Interest on capital
C)  Interest on loans
D) Partners drawings
Answer: c
Solution: is charged in the profit and loss account as finance expenses

Q: The major source of document which enables employer to calculate  the employee wages  is the?
A) norminal roll of employees
B) records of number of hours worked
C)  effort of the employee
D) Record of independence per employee
Answer: b
Solution: The numbers of hours worked is the period of time that a person spends at paid labour. This means that, an employee pay roll is prepared by calculating the number of hours that employee spend working for his or her employer. The wages / salaries of that employee is subject to hourly rate. ( the more time you spend at work, the more the pay).

It is however worthy to note that, not all employees / employers practice this payment method.

Q: The rent expense for Trendy store is ₦3500. Trendy store has three departments; jewelry, hair dressing, and clothing. The floor spaces occupied by the departments are 3:2:5 respectively. What is the rent allocated to clothing department?
A) ₦700
B) ₦1050
C)  ₦1750
D) ₦3500
Answer: c
Solution: Jewelry 3/10 x 3500 = 1050

Hairdressing 2/10 x 3500 = 700

Clothing 5/10 x 3500 = 1750

Q: Which of the following should not be adjusted for in the profit and loss account?
A) Accruals
B) inventory
C) subscription
D) depreciation
Answer: c
Solution: is adjusted for in the income and expenditure account

Q: What act generally includes completing unfinished partnership business, collecting and paying debts, collecting partnership assets to be turned into cash and taking inventory?
A) Formation
B) dissolution
C)  winding up
D)  termination
Answer: b
Solution: It is the first step in termination process

Q: Gross profit in the branch adjustment account is transferred to the branch____________
A) Income and expenditure account
B) profit and loss account
C) receipt and payment account
D) trading account
Answer: d
Solution: In branch accounting, the Branch Adjustment Account is used to record inter‐branch adjustments such as stock transfers and branch expenses. Any gross profit worked out in this account is then transferred to the Branch Trading Account, where it becomes part of the overall trading results for that branch.

Q: Transfers from the head office to branches are best carried out at__________
A) Cost price
B) Cost plus mark up
C) Selling price
D) Market price
Answer: b
Solution: Goods are transferred from head office to branch at cost price, selling price and cost price plus mark up

Q: Cost of rent as an expense can be apportioned to all department on the basis of:
A) No of employees
B) stock value
C) space occupied
D) wages
Answer: c
Solution: Indirect expenses are allocated among departments in order to ascertain the profits or loss made by each department

Q: When goods are sent to branch at cost plus mark up, it means that the branch should sell at_____________
A) Price above or below the stipulated price
B) Any price but not below the transfer price
C) Cost price
D) A price that is equal to the mark up
Answer: a
Solution: Cost plus mark up is a pricing strategy in which the selling price is determined by adding a specific amount mark up to a product unit cost

Q: Adex Ltd. issues stock to its retail branches at cost price. The following particulars relate to Ede branch: Stock at branch 1st January at cost ₦400, Goods sent to branch at cost ₦8000, Returns to head office ₦340, Cash sales ₦9160, Stock at branch 31st December at cost ₦720. Use the information to answer the question.  calculate the gross profit
A) ₦1870
B) ₦1530
C)  ₦1640
D) ₦1820
Answer: d
Solution: Gross Profit = Sales - Cost of Goods Sold….. Cost of Goods Sold = Opening Stock + Goods Sent - Returns - Closing Stock
= ₦400 + ₦8,000 - ₦340 - ₦720
= ₦7,340…. Gross Profit = Sales - Cost of Goods Sold
= ₦9,160 - ₦7,340 = ₦1,820
The branch made a gross profit of ₦1,820 for the period.

Q: Which of the following is not an inventory costing method?
A) FIFO
B) LIFO
C) Average cost method
D) LILA
Answer: d
Solution: FIFO (First-In, First-Out), LIFO (Last-In, First-Out), and the Average Cost Method are all standard inventory valuation methods.

LILA is not a recognized inventory costing method.

Q: Sule and Ahmed are in partnership sharing profit and losses equally. If Khadija is admitted as a new partner to take 1/5 th as her share. What is the new profit or loss sharing?
A)  Sule1/3, Ahmed1/3, Khadija 1/3
B) Sule1/3, Ahmed1/3, Khadija 1/3
C) Sule1/5, Ahmed1/5, Khadija3/5
D)  Sule2/5, Ahmed1/5, Khadija2/5
Answer: b
Solution: If Khadija is to take 1/5th i.e. 20%

  Sule and Ahmed are to share 80% (100% - 20%) equally

  Sule = 2/5

  Ahmed = 2/5

  Khadija = 1/5

Q: A business has the following balance sheet as at the beginning of the year: Capital ₦40,000, Furnishing ₦10,000, Ceiling Fan ₦1,500, and Cash in Hand ₦28,500, with total assets and liabilities both equaling ₦40,000.
During the year ending 31/1/95, the following transactions occurred:

Rent for shop ₦12,000 paid for the year
Total purchases ₦15,000
Total sales ₦8,200
Stock of goods left ₦10,000
Paid sales boy ₦500

What is the new balance sheet total as at 31/1/95?
A)  ₦39,700
B)  ₦40,000
C)  ₦41,500
D) ₦48,500
Answer: a
Solution: Starting with opening cash of ₦28,500, we track cash movements:
Cash Outflows:

Rent paid: ₦12,000
Purchases: ₦15,000
Sales boy wages: ₦500
Total outflows: ₦27,500

Cash Inflows:

Sales: ₦8,200

New Cash Balance: ₦28,500 - ₦27,500 + ₦8,200 = ₦9,200
New Balance Sheet:

Assets: Furnishing ₦10,000 + Ceiling Fan ₦1,500 + Stock ₦10,000 + Cash ₦9,200 = ₦30,700
Capital: ₦40,000 - ₦300 (net loss) = ₦39,700
Prepaid Rent: ₦9,000 (11 months remaining)

New Balance Sheet Total: ₦39,700

Q: Advertising expenses incurred on a product in a business organization should be charged to
A) Sales department
B) Production department
C)  Purchase department
D) Administration department
Answer: a
Solution: Advertising expenses are expenses incurred in order to enhance the sales of the company’s product/services

Q: Tea and Cup are into a partnership business. Interests on drawings made by partners are at 10% per annum. Tea’s capital is ₦70000 and current balance is ₦50000. He withdrew the following amounts during the year : 3000 on 31st January ,2000 on 31st March, 4000 on 1st July, 1500 on the 30th September, 2500 on 1st November. Cup’s capital is ₦100000 and current balance is ₦40000. He made no drawings during the period. What is the interest on the drawings of Tea?
A)  ₦705
B) ₦500
C) ₦1000
D) ₦10000
Answer: a
Solution: Interest on Tea’s drawings is calculated as the sum of each drawing × 10% × (months outstanding ÷ 12):

₦3 000 on 31 Jan: 3 000 × 10% × (11/12) = ₦275.00

₦2 000 on 31 Mar: 2 000 × 10% × (9/12) = ₦150.00

₦4 000 on 1 Jul: 4 000 × 10% × (6/12) = ₦200.00

₦1 500 on 30 Sep: 1 500 × 10% × (3/12) = ₦37.50

₦2 500 on 1 Nov: 2 500 × 10% × (2/12) = ₦41.67

Total interest = ₦275 + ₦150 + ₦200 + ₦37.50 + ₦41.67 = ₦704.17  ≈ ₦705..

Q: A Trading account for the year ended 31st December 2009 shows the following information:
Opening Stock: ₦32,000
Purchases: ₦40,000
Carriage inwards: ₦1,000
Less Returns: ₦2,000
Sales: ₦48,000
Less Returns: ₦2,000
Closing Stock: ₦9,000
Calculate:

What is the cost of goods available for sale?

A)  ₦20,500
B) ₦71,000
C)  ₦28,000
D) ₦27,000
Answer: b
Solution: Calculate Cost of Goods Available
Cost of Goods Available = Opening Stock + Net Purchases + Carriage Inwards
= ₦32,000 + ₦39,000 + ₦1,000 = ₦71,000

Q: If the purchase price exceeds the net assets of a company, the excess amount is debited to________________

A) Cash account
B)  purchase account
C) goodwill account
D) sales account
Answer: c
Solution: Goodwill is the excess of purchase consideration over the total value of the business

Q: A partnership’s internal regulation are set out by________
A)  A constitution
B) A law
C) A deed
D) . An article
Answer: c
Solution: A partnership deed is a written agreement among the partners specifying rules and regulations and is signed by all the partners and stamped as per stamp act with an aim to prevent possible disputes and disagreements among the partners at future dates

Q: Why should a new partner contribute towards goodwill on his admission?
A) It is a norm
B) to ensure new partner also have a stake in the business
C) the firm into which he is entering already has some goodwill in the market
D) to purchase the business
Answer: c
Solution: Goodwill is being paid by a new partner because the partnership he is entering into already has goodwill in the market as well as to pay for the portion sacrificed by existing partners in form to their profit to admit the new partner.

Q: Which of the following is a conversion cost?
A) Factory overhead
B) purchases
C) material cost
D) wages
Answer: a
Solution: Conversion costs are costs required to convert raw materials into finished goods

  Formula for conversion cost= direct labor+ factory overheads

Q: Ade, Tony, Rose share profit and losses in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 1 respectively. Ade retires and the remaining partners decide to take Ade’s share in the existing ratio. What is the new ratio?

A) 1 : 1
B) 3 : 6
C) 2 : 1
D) 2 : 6
Answer: c
Solution: When Ade’s 3‑part share is divided between Tony and Rose in their 2 : 1 ratio, Tony receives 3 × (2/3) = 2 parts and Rose receives 3 × (1/3) = 1 part, so Tony’s total becomes 2 + 2 = 4 and Rose’s becomes 1 + 1 = 2, giving a new ratio of 4 : 2 (i.e. 2 : 1).

Q: Statement of Financial Position as at 31st Dec 2010 showing:

Noncurrent assets: Plant and equipment ₦10,000
Current assets: Stock ₦7,000, Receivables ₦5,000 (Total current assets ₦12,000)
Total assets ₦22,000
Capital ₦15,000
Current liabilities: Payables ₦7,000
Total ₦22,000

What is the amount of capital employed?
A) ₦7000
B) ₦10000
C) ₦22000
D) ₦15000
Answer: d
Solution: Capital employed can be calculated in two ways:
Method 1 (Asset approach):
Capital Employed = Total Assets - Current Liabilities
= ₦22,000 - ₦7,000 = ₦15,000
Method 2 (Financing approach):
Capital Employed = Shareholders' Capital + Long-term Liabilities
= ₦15,000 + ₦0 = ₦15,000

Q: Capital ₦39,000, Long Term Loan ₦15,000, Creditors ₦9,000, Accrued wages ₦5,000 totaling ₦68,000 on one side, and Land ₦20,000, Building ₦30,000, Stock ₦40,000, Debtors ₦6,000, Cash ₦8,000 totaling ₦68,000 on the other side, use the information above to answer the question: The acid test ratio in the company is ________.
A) 1:1
B)  2:3
C)  1:2
D) 3:2
Answer: a
Solution: The acid test ratio (quick ratio) measures a company's ability to pay short-term debts using liquid assets.
Formula:
Acid Test Ratio = (Current Assets - Stock) ÷ Current Liabilities
Calculation:

Current Assets = Stock + Debtors + Cash = ₦40,000 + ₦6,000 + ₦8,000 = ₦54,000
Quick Assets = Current Assets - Stock = ₦54,000 - ₦40,000 = ₦14,000
Current Liabilities = Creditors + Accrued wages = ₦9,000 + ₦5,000 = ₦14,000

Acid Test Ratio = ₦14,000 ÷ ₦14,000 = 1:1
This means the company has exactly enough liquid assets to cover its current liabilities.

Q: A partnership deed is used to____________
A) Promote mutual understanding
B) Enhance mistrust
C) Encourage discrepancy
D) Control funds
Answer: a
Solution: Partnership deed can be used to:

  i. Indicates terms on which the business corporation us founded

  ii. To form a partnership for the purpose of doing business together

  iii. Prevent future disputes

  iv. Promote mutual understanding

  v. Avoid mistrust

Q: Adex Ltd. issues stock to its retail branches at cost price. The following information relates to Ede branch: Stock at branch 1st January at cost ₦400, Goods sent to branch at cost ₦8000, Returns to head office ₦340, Cash sales ₦9160, Stock at branch 31st December at cost ₦720. Calculate the cost of goods credited to the head office trading account.
A) ₦7340
B)  ₦7460
C)  ₦7500
D) ₦7660
Answer: a
Solution: The cost of goods credited to the Head Office Trading Account is computed as:

Opening stock (₦400)

Goods sent to branch (₦8,000)
– Returns to Head Office (₦340)
– Closing stock (₦720)
= ₦7,340

Q: In dealing with incomplete record, fixed assets are posted to___________-

A) Profit and loss account as brought forward figure
B) Closing balance sheet as carried forward figure
C) Closing balance sheet as brought forward figure
D) Profit and loss as carried forward figure
Answer: d
Solution: fixed asset are brought forward in closing balance sheet

Q: A Trading account for the year ended 31st December 2009 shows the following information:
Opening Stock: ₦32,000
Purchases: ₦40,000
Carriage inwards: ₦1,000
Less Returns: ₦2,000
Sales: ₦48,000
Less Returns: ₦2,000
Closing Stock: ₦9,000
Calculate:

What is the cost of goods sold?
A) ₦61,000
B) ₦62,000
C)  ₦58,000
D)  ₦57,000
Answer: b
Solution: Calculate Cost of Goods Sold
Cost of Goods Sold = Cost of Goods Available - Closing Stock
= ₦71,000 - ₦9,000 = ₦62,000

Q: During the period, Department P opened with stock of ₦2 000, made purchases of ₦2 500 and recorded sales of ₦6 000. Its closing stock was ₦1 500. Department P also received goods costing ₦300 transferred in from Department Q and incurred operating expenses of ₦200. What was Department P’s net profit for the period?
A)  ₦2,500
B) ₦2,800
C) ₦3,000
D) ₦5,200
Answer: a
Solution: Net profit for Department P = Sales ₦6 000 – Cost of Goods Sold [(₂₀₀₀ + ₦2 500 + ₦300 – ₦1 500) = ₦3 300] – Expenses ₦200 = ₦2 500.

Q: In departmental accounting, which is not a transfer pricing_________
A) cost based transfer price
B) market based transfer pricing
C) Dual pricing system
D) peak pricing
Answer: d
Solution: The standard transfer‐pricing methods used in departmental accounting are:

Cost‐based transfer pricing (using internal cost as the basis)

Market‐based transfer pricing (using external market prices)

Dual pricing system (charging one price to the selling division and another to the buying division)

Peak pricing, on the other hand, is a demand‐management strategy for external customers (adjusting prices during high‐demand “peak” periods) and is not used for inter‐departmental transfer pricin

Q: In the absence of a partnership deed, the act stipulates that____________
A) An amount should be fixed as salaries for partners
B) Profits and losses should not be shared equally
C) Interest on partner’s loan should be 25%
D) Interest should not be allowed on partners drawings
Answer: d
Solution: Under the Partnership Act, the following rules will be applied in the absence of an agreement among partners:

  i. Profit or losses of the firm will be shared equally by the partners

  ii. Interest on capital will not be allowed to any partner.

  iii. No interest will be charged on drawings

  iv. Interest on loan will be 6% on the loan

  v. No salary or remuneration will be allowed to any of the partners

  vi. Every partner must take part in the management of the partnership business

  vii. The partnership books are kept at the place of business of the partnership and every partner may have access to and inspect and copy any of them.

Q: Which of the following is not a type of branch?
A) Dependent branch
B) foreign branch
C) independent branch
D) single branch
Answer: d
Solution: Branches are typically classified as:

Dependent branches, which rely on the head office for purchases and policies

Independent branches, which operate like standalone entities with their own accounting systems

Foreign branches, which are located in another country and may involve additional currency and regulatory considerations

The term “single branch” isn’t used as a formal classification.

Q: When goodwill is not retained in the business, the entries in the new partners books will be to debit______________

A) Goodwill account and credit partners capital account
B) Cash account and credit goodwill account
C) Goodwill account and credit cash account
D)  Partners capital account and credit goodwill account
Answer: d
Solution: When goodwill is not retained in the business, it means the goodwill account is written off immediately after being created. This involves a two-step process:
Step 1: Create goodwill

Debit: Goodwill Account
Credit: Partners' Capital Accounts (in profit-sharing ratio)

Step 2: Write off goodwill (since it's not retained)

Debit: Partners' Capital Accounts (in new profit-sharing ratio)
Credit: Goodwill Account

The net effect in the new partners' books is:

Debit: Partners' Capital Account
Credit: Goodwill Account

This represents the partners absorbing the goodwill write-off through their capital accounts rather than keeping it as an asset on the books.

Q: Which of the following methods of invoicing goods to branches facilitate easy checks on the activities of branches?
A) Selling price
B) Fixed percentage on cost
C) Cost price
D) Invoice price
Answer: c
Solution: Goods are transferred from head office to branch at cost price, selling price and cost price plus mark up

Q: The amount called in respect of a share but not paid before or on the date fixed for payment is referred to as:
A) Call in advance
B) call in arrears
C) forfeiture
D) shares
Answer: b
Solution: the amount called by the company which is not paid by the shareholders before the due date fixed for payment

 

Q: In the head office ledger, the value of goods sent to the branch are____________
A) Debited to the branch current account
B) Debited to the head office current account
C) Credited to the head office current account
D) Credited to the branch current account
Answer: b
Solution: Branch current account is maintained in the head office books to record all transactions between the head office and the branch. This account is debited with the following:

  i. Goods sent to branch

  ii. Expenses of the branch paid by the head office

  iii. Profit of the branch

Q: To account for expenses paid by head office on behalf of the branch, the branch should___________
A) Debit profit and loss account and credit head office account
B) Debit head office account and credit cash
C) Credit cash and debit profit and loss account
D)  Credit profit and loss account and debit head office account
Answer: a
Solution: The head office maintains a book, (branch account) more or less like other personal accounts, so that any expenses incurred on behalf of the branch will also be debited to the branch account. Similarly, in the branch books, there will be head office accounts

Q: Departmentalization of accounts is useful because it shows the____________
A) Over all performance of a division
B) Cost per unit of a profit
C) Price per unit of a product
D)  Over all performance of a firm
Answer: a
Solution: Departmental accounting is prepared to ensure that the results of each individual department is known
